# pixi-reels

pixi-reels 4.3.1 is a reel engine for PixiJS v8.
It ships reel-only primitives. Win math, paytable math, RNG, and audio live in consumer code.
This file inlines every guide, API page, recipe (with source) and answered FAQ entry for offline LLM context.
The index alone, one line per page, is https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/llms.txt.

Site: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev
Repo: https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-reels
Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/pixi-reels

## Quick start

```bash
npm install pixi-reels pixi.js gsap
```

```ts
import { Application } from 'pixi.js';
import { ReelSetBuilder, SpriteSymbol } from 'pixi-reels';

const app = new Application();
await app.init({ width: 800, height: 480 });

const reelSet = new ReelSetBuilder()
  .reels(5).visibleCells(3).symbolSize(120, 120)
  .symbols(r => r.register('cherry', SpriteSymbol, { textures: { cherry: cherryTex } }))
  .ticker(app.ticker)
  .build();
app.stage.addChild(reelSet);

const result = reelSet.spin();
reelSet.setResult([{ visible: ['cherry','cherry','cherry'] }, /* one per reel */ ]);
await result;
```

## Mechanics

### Anticipation
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/
Hold the last reels back when a bonus is one scatter away, so the player watches them land.
Tags: anticipation, tension, scatter, near-miss, spine, horizontal, reverse, curve, acceleration

An anticipation tease slows the reels that could still complete a win, so the
player watches them land. Call `setAnticipation(reelIndices, options)` after
`spin()` and before `setResult()`. The named reels run an anticipation phase
before they stop. The set is cleared at the start of every `spin()`.

```ts
const spinDone = reelSet.spin();
const grid = await server.spin();          // ColumnTarget[]
reelSet.setAnticipation(anticipationForScatters(grid, { symbol: 'SCAT', trigger: 2 }));
reelSet.setResult(grid);
await spinDone;
```

The second argument is either a stagger (`0`, a number of ms, a list of ms,
or `'sequential'`) or an options object with `stagger`, `slowdown`,
`duration`, `protect`, `curve` and `cells`. The demos above cover each of
them. The speed profile's `anticipationDelay` sets how long a tease lasts, and a
profile with `anticipationDelay: 0` skips the tease unless you pass
`duration`.

##### Demos

#### Slow the last reels

Two scatters land on reels 0 and 2, and `setAnticipation([3, 4])` slows the last two reels so they land late.

Live demo (anticipate-a-reel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#anticipate-a-reel

#### Choose the reels from scatters

`anticipationForScatters` reads the result grid and returns the reels to tease. The demo alternates its two modes. `'all-remaining'` teases every reel after the one where the scatter count reaches `trigger`, empty reels included. `'scatter-only'` teases only the reels that hold a scatter, and the others stop as usual.

Live demo (scatter-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#scatter-driven-anticipation

#### Pacing several reels

##### One after another

`setAnticipation(reels, 'sequential')` holds each teasing reel until the one before it has landed, instead of slowing them all at once.

Live demo (staggered-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#staggered--sequential-anticipation

##### Slower on each reel

Each teasing reel slows further than the last, from 0.5x to 0.1x of spin speed, holds longer, and lands at that slow speed without returning to full speed first.

Live demo (slowing-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#slowing-anticipation

#### Teaser symbol

`setAnticipation` plus a `bufferStart` prefill. A chosen symbol sits in the slot above the window while the slow reels decelerate, so the player sees it approach, but it never lands.

Live demo (anticipation-teaser): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#anticipation-teaser

#### Turbo

The SuperTurbo profile sets `anticipationDelay` to 0, so a plain `setAnticipation` call skips the tease. Pass a `duration` override and the tease plays in every speed mode.

Live demo (turbo-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#anticipation-in-turbo

#### Skipping the tease

##### Skip at any point

A long sequential tease. A press mid-tease slams the reels onto the result.

Live demo (skip-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#skip-the-tease

##### Protected tease

The same long tease, but the first press only lands the reels around it. `protect: 'once'` makes sure both scatters are on screen and the slowdown has visibly started before a second press can end it.

Call `setAnticipation` before `setResult`. A press before the result arrives is queued by `requestSkip()` and fires the moment the result comes in, so the tease has to be registered by then or there is nothing to protect.

Live demo (protected-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#skip-that-cannot-hide-the-tease

`protect: 'stepwise'` moves the tease on by one reel per press instead of ending it in one go. Partial slams, per-reel spin floors and the case for protecting a tease over slowing the skip are on [Skip and slam](/mechanics/skip/).

#### Spine scatter animation

The scatter skeleton's own near-win clips. The leftmost scatter snaps its jaw, the loop holds while the tease runs, and the rightmost plays the result as it lands. Spins alternate between a hit and a miss.

Live demo (spine-scatter-jaw-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#scatter-jaw-anticipation

#### Shaping the slowdown

The default tease only slows down. These demos replace that shape with explicit speed segments, anchor the tease to a number of symbols, or limit acceleration for the whole spin.

##### Surge, then crawl

An ease applied to a speed changes the acceleration in one step. With `power2.out` the hardest deceleration is on the first frame, so the reel looks like it was switched to a lower speed instead of slowing down.

`curve` replaces the fixed shape with explicit segments. Speeds are multiples of `spinSpeed`, so `2` is a real surge and `0.08` a crawl. Segment eases default to `power2.inOut`, which ramps the acceleration in and out.

```ts
reelSet.setAnticipation([2, 3, 4], {
  stagger: 260,
  curve: [
    { speed: 2,    duration: 240, ease: 'power2.in' },
    { speed: 0.08, duration: 620, ease: 'power3.inOut', hold: 300 },
  ],
});
```

Passing `curve` and `slowdown` together throws, because `slowdown` is shorthand for a two-segment curve. The profile's `anticipationDelay` still decides whether the tease runs at all, so Turbo needs a `duration` override. The curve's own durations set the length.

Live demo (anticipation-surge-curve): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#shape-the-tease-surge-then-crawl

##### A curve per reel

Two curves of different lengths have no sensible midpoint, so instead of interpolating, `curve` takes a function, `(order, total) => AnticipationSegment[]`.

`order` is the reel's position in the anticipation set, not its index. `setAnticipation([4, 2, 3], ...)` passes `order: 0` to reel 4, the same as `slowdown` and `protect: 'stepwise'` do.

Live demo (anticipation-curve-per-reel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#a-different-curve-per-reel

##### Tease for a number of symbols

`duration` is a time budget, so how far a reel moves depends on its speed. When the tease is timed to symbols passing the window, as in "three more and it lands", use `cells: n`. It ends the tease after n symbol pitches, measured on `reel.travelledCells`, a counter that only goes up and is not reset by the snap at the end of each spin. `cells` also accepts a function of order, like `curve`.

The count applies to the last segment. Earlier segments always play in full, otherwise a fast opening segment could use up the count and skip the ones after it. `duration` is the backstop on that segment, since a reel at rest never reaches a travel target.

Live demo (anticipation-cells): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#tease-for-n-symbols-not-n-milliseconds

##### Limit acceleration

An ease shapes only the transition it is written for. `motionModel('drive', ...)` limits acceleration instead. Phases set `reel.targetSpeed`, and `Reel.update` moves the speed toward it, so every transition gets the same feel, an interruption is a single new target, and `jerkFrames` ramps the acceleration itself.

```ts
builder.motionModel('drive', { accelFrames: 20, decelFrames: 34, jerkFrames: 260 })
```

The limits are relative to the profile, in frames to reach the active profile's full speed. The presets run `spinSpeed` 30, 50 and 80, so one absolute px/frame^2 limit would make SuperTurbo start slower than Normal. The absolute `{ accel, decel, jerk }` form still works for a game with one profile; mixing the two throws.

It is set at build time and off by default. The default `'tween'` model is unchanged. Landing and a skip press are instant, as they are under `'tween'`. If the drive cannot reach a segment's speed in time, it reports that on the notice channel.

Live demo (anticipation-drive): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#the-gas-pedal-bounded-acceleration

#### Tease audio

`anticipation:reel` and `anticipation:reelEnd` mark the start and end of a reel's tease, which is where a tension loop starts and stops. `anticipation:segment` (`{ reelIndex, index, total, speed, targetSpeed }`) fires once per curve segment, so a surge can sound different from the crawl after it. For a pitch ramp that follows the actual slowdown, read `reelSet.reels[i].speedNormalized` from your own ticker. It is `1` at full spin speed, `0` at rest and above `1` during a surge.

#### Other reel directions

Reel indexes do not depend on orientation, so the anticipation code is the same. Only where the teasing reels sit on screen changes.

##### Horizontal set

Scatter-driven anticipation with the reels running sideways. `anticipationForScatters` and `setAnticipation` work as on a vertical set. Reels are stacked down the screen here, so the last two reels are the bottom two rows, and they slow while moving sideways.

Live demo (anticipation-horizontal-scatter): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#tension-on-a-horizontal-set

##### Teaser on reels that spin up

The teaser on a `direction('reverse')` set. Buffers are geometric, so `bufferStart` is still the slot above the window, and on a reverse reel symbols have already left through that side.

Put the teaser on the feed edge instead. `reel.axis.feedEdge` is `'start'` on a forward reel and `'end'` on a reverse one, so one branch covers both.

Live demo (anticipation-reverse-teaser): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#teaser-on-a-reel-that-spins-up

#### Faking a near-miss

Place one scatter fewer than the trigger needs and tease the reel that would have held the last one. The result is always a loss.

Some jurisdictions restrict engineered near-misses. Check with compliance before you ship one.

Live demo (near-miss): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/anticipation/#fake-a-near-miss

### Big symbols and MultiWays
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/
Symbols that span several cells, and boards whose reels show different numbers of rows.
Tags: big-symbols, multiways, pyramid, spine, geometry, sticky-wild, horizontal, reverse, orientation

Most slots are uniform: every reel has the same number of cells, and this
part does not apply to them. It covers three other shapes:

| Shape | Changes when | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Static pyramid (`3-5-5-5-3`) | Never. Fixed at build. | below |
| MultiWays | Every spin | [MultiWays](/mechanics/big-symbols/#concept-multiways) |
| Big symbols (`N x M` blocks) | Never. One symbol covers many cells. | [Big symbols](/mechanics/big-symbols/#concept-big-symbols) |

#### What cannot be combined

Two combinations throw at `build()`.

MultiWays and a pyramid. `visibleCellsPerReel()` declares a fixed shape and
`multiways()` declares one that the server sets. Both set the cell count, so
use one or the other.

MultiWays and big symbols. A 2x2 block cannot fit a reel that has reshaped
to 2 cells. Whether to truncate it, skip it or shrink it is a game design
decision, so the engine does not pick one.

Big symbols and pyramids do work together. So do MultiWays and cascades
(ADR 015).

#### Static pyramid

```ts
new ReelSetBuilder()
  .reels(5)
  .visibleCellsPerReel([3, 5, 5, 5, 3])
  .reelAnchor('center')                   // 'start' | 'center' | 'end'
  .symbolSize(120, 120)
  .build();
```

Short reels are offset along the strip so they sit where `reelAnchor` says.
The default mask clips each reel to its own box, so a short reel never shows
its buffer cells. `getCellBounds(reel, cell)` includes the offset.

The [per-reel shape demo](/mechanics/big-symbols/#pyramid-shape) runs this.

#### Masks

The clip mask comes from a `MaskStrategy`. Two ship with the library:

| Strategy | Clips | Costs you |
|---|---|---|
| `RectMaskStrategy` (default) | One rect per reel | A symbol spanning two reels is cut at the gap between them |
| `SharedRectMaskStrategy` | One rect over everything | On a pyramid, buffer cells past short reels show (the "pyramid peek") |

The engine picks `SharedRectMaskStrategy` when big or unmasked symbols are
registered and the gap between reels is non-zero, because per-reel rects would
visibly cut a block in that case. Override it with
`.maskStrategy()`.

```ts
import { SharedRectMaskStrategy } from 'pixi-reels';
builder.maskStrategy(new SharedRectMaskStrategy());
```

For a rounded frame or a hex grid, implement `MaskStrategy` yourself. It
takes one `MaskContext` and returns a `Graphics` filled with any shape Pixi
can draw. Set `version = MASK_STRATEGY_VERSION` on it. The
[masks page](/mechanics/masks/) has strategies for common shapes.

To see what is clipped:

```ts
import { debugOverlay } from 'pixi-reels/debug'; // needs pixi-silk, a dev dependency

debugOverlay(reelSet, { layers: ['mask', 'cells', 'buffers'] });
```

#### See also

- [MultiWays](/mechanics/big-symbols/#concept-multiways): per-spin shape, the adjust phase, pin migration
- [Big symbols](/mechanics/big-symbols/#concept-big-symbols): `N x M` blocks
- [Per-reel shape demo](/mechanics/big-symbols/#pyramid-shape): a runnable jagged layout
- [Cell bounds demo](/mechanics/cells-and-banners/#cell-bounds): overlays aligned to cells

A big symbol is one symbol that covers a rectangular block of cells, such as
a 2x2 bonus or a 1x3 bar. You declare it at registration with a `size` in its
symbol data. The result format does not change. The server places the symbol
id in the anchor cell, and the engine fills the rest of the block with a
placeholder.

For pyramids, MultiWays and what cannot be combined, start at
[Per-reel geometry](/mechanics/big-symbols/#concept-per-reel-geometry).

#### Declaration

Register it like any other symbol and add a `size`, with a reel count and a
cell count, to its symbol data:

```ts
.symbols((registry) => {
  registry.register('bonus', SpriteSymbol, { textures: { bonus: tex } });
})
.symbolData({
  bonus: { weight: 0, zIndex: 5, size: { reels: 2, cells: 2 } },
  //         ^^^^^^^^^ a block wider than one reel must have weight 0.
  //                   Random fill feeds one reel at a time and cannot place
  //                   it, so the builder throws on a non-zero weight.
})
```

The `zIndex: 5` is a convention in the recipes. It puts the anchor above its
1x1 neighbours so it draws on top.

#### The result format

The server puts the symbol id in the anchor cell of the block only. Every
other cell of the block can hold any string, because the engine overwrites it
with the occupied placeholder.

```ts
// 5x4 grid, 2x2 bonus anchored at (reel=2, cell=1):
setResult([
  { visible: ['low1', 'low2', 'low1', 'low2'] },
  { visible: ['low1', 'low2', 'low1', 'low2'] },
  { visible: ['low1', 'bonus',  '?',   'low2'] }, // '?' is whatever; engine paints OCCUPIED
  { visible: ['low1', '?',      '?',   'low2'] }, // '?' is whatever; engine paints OCCUPIED
  { visible: ['low1', 'low2', 'low1', 'low2'] },
]);
```

Before the per-reel frames are built, the spin controller reads the result
grid, finds the anchors, checks that each block fits, and paints the
placeholder across the rest of each block. At landing, the anchor symbol is
sized to span the whole block, gaps included: `w` cells wide plus `w - 1`
gaps, and `h` cells tall plus `h - 1` gaps. The other cells of the block get
an invisible stub, and the anchor's view covers them.

The public API never returns the placeholder. `Reel.getVisibleSymbols()` and
`ReelSet.getVisibleGrid()` both resolve it to the anchor's id, on the anchor's
reel and on the other reels the block covers, so the two return the same
data.

#### Block lookup

`getSymbolFootprint` returns the block itself, its anchor cell and size, for
win evaluation and event payloads. `getBlockBounds` returns the pixel rect
that covers the whole block, for overlays.

```ts
const fp = reelSet.getSymbolFootprint(reel, cell);
// { anchor: { reel: 2, cell: 1 }, size: { reels: 2, cells: 2 } }

const rect = reelSet.getBlockBounds(reel, cell);
// { x, y, width: 2*cellW + symbolGap.x, height: 2*cellH + symbolGap.y }
gfx.rect(rect.x, rect.y, rect.width, rect.height).stroke({ color: 0xff6b35, width: 4 });
```

Both return the same data for any cell of the block, anchor or not. For a
1x1 cell, `getBlockBounds` returns the same rect as `getCellBounds`.

#### Validation

During a spin, `setResult()` throws at once if a block does not fit:

- `"big symbol 'giant' (3x3) at (reel=4, cell=2) exceeds reel count 6."`
- `"big symbol 'tallBar' (1x3) at (reel=0, cell=3) extends past the bottom of the strip on reel 0 (anchor cell + h = 6 > visibleCells + bufferEnd = 4)."`

The check along the strip counts the visible cells plus the end buffer, not
the visible window alone, so a block may land partly in either buffer.

A `setResult()` with no spin in flight returns early and validates nothing.

Pinning a cell of a big symbol other than the anchor is not supported, and it
does not throw either. The engine repaints that cell as occupied at the next
`setResult()` and the pin is lost without a warning. Pin the anchor instead.
Its view spans the block, so the whole block looks pinned. `setSymbolAt()` on
a cell other than the anchor does throw.

The build-time check refuses a block wider than one reel with a non-zero
weight, with a message that starts `big symbol 'bonus' (size 2x2) must have
weight 0`. Random fill feeds one reel at a time and cannot place such a block,
so its weight would never be used. A block one reel wide may have a weight.

#### Partial landings

An anchor does not have to be in a visible cell. Put a tall block's anchor in
the start buffer and only its tail shows, at the top of the window. Anchor it
at the last visible cell and its head shows while the rest extends into the
end buffer.

Use the explicit `ColumnTarget` form to target buffer slots:

```ts
// 1x3 wild lands with its tail at visible cell 0; anchor + one stub are
// off-screen in bufferStart. Requires bufferSymbols(2) or more.
reelSet.setResult([
  { visible: [...], bufferStart: [undefined, 'tallWild'] },
  // ...
]);
```

For that reel, `getSymbolFootprint(reel, 0)` reports the anchor at cell -2.
The index is negative because the anchor sits before the window.
`getBlockBounds(reel, 0)` returns the whole block's rect, off-screen part
included, and the mask does the clipping. The
[partial landing demo](/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbol-partial-land) runs
this.

#### Masks for wide blocks

With a gap between reels, the default per-reel mask leaves that gap
unmasked. A big symbol's anchor view extends across several reels, and the
per-reel mask clips it at every gap, which shows as transparent strips
through the symbol.

The engine picks `SharedRectMaskStrategy` on its own when all three hold:

1. At least one registered big symbol is wider than one reel, or any symbol
   sets `unmask: true`.
2. The gap between reels is above 0: `symbolGap.x` on a vertical set,
   `symbolGap.y` on a horizontal one.
3. No explicit `.maskStrategy(...)` call was made.

It reports the choice on the notice channel, and `.maskStrategy(...)`
overrides it.

A stack one reel wide (`size: { reels: 1, cells: 3 }`) never crosses a gap,
so it keeps the per-reel mask. That mask also suits a reel that `setColumn()`
or `splitSymbol()` makes taller or shorter than the rest. With one shared box,
the buffer cells past the shorter reels would show. Art that extends past its
cell into the gap is clipped there. Pass the shared strategy yourself if you
want one box.

```ts
import { SharedRectMaskStrategy } from 'pixi-reels';

builder
  .symbolGap(4, 4)                                  // horizontal gap > 0
  .maskStrategy(new SharedRectMaskStrategy())       // explicit (or rely on auto-pick)
  // ...
```

`SharedRectMaskStrategy` draws one rect over the whole set. On a pyramid that
means the buffer cells past the ends of short reels become visible, the
"pyramid peek". Games usually cover it with frame art.

#### Draw order

By default an anchor renders at `symbolData.zIndex * 100 + arrayIndex`, about
500 with `zIndex: 5`. The 100x multiplier leaves room for per-cell order
inside one layer, so cells further along the strip still draw in front of
their neighbours.

When you want a different order, pass a resolver and the engine uses its
answer instead. For example, the symbol in the bottom row can always draw in
front of the one above it, whatever its type:

```ts
.symbolZIndex((ctx) => {
  if (!ctx.atRest || ctx.visibleCell === null) return ctx.defaultZIndex;
  const grade = GRADES[ctx.symbolId];
  return grade === undefined
    ? ctx.defaultZIndex
    : grade * 1000 + ctx.visibleCell * 10 + ctx.reelIndex;
})
```

The resolver receives the symbol id and data, the reel index and count, the
array index, the visible cell (`null` for a buffer slot), the visible cell
count, whether the reel is at rest, and the z-index the engine would have
used. The engine calls it again whenever a symbol's id, cell, reel shape or
rest state changes, so its answer is never overwritten. Order across reels only
exists for symbols that share a container: an `unmask: true` symbol at rest
sits in the viewport-wide unmasked container with every other lifted symbol,
while a masked one is bounded by its reel container's own z-index
(`reelStacking`). That is why the example grades at rest only and keeps the
engine's order in motion. Keep every value below `Z_INDEX_BUDGET.pinOverlay`.

Pin overlays render at z-index 10000 (`Z_INDEX_BUDGET.pinOverlay`;
`Z_INDEX_BUDGET.symbolLayer` is the 100x). So a big symbol that is also
pinned at its anchor gets its overlay above the cell. The overlay is sized to
a single cell, so while the reel spins it does not cover the rest of the
block. The block spans again once the frame commits at landing.

| Layer | zIndex | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1x1 symbol, default | `0 * 100 + arrayIndex` | `symbolData.zIndex ?? 0` |
| 1x1 symbol, elevated | `1 * 100 + arrayIndex` | `symbolData.zIndex: 1` |
| Big-symbol anchor (recipe convention) | `5 * 100 + arrayIndex` (~500) | `symbolData.zIndex: 5` |
| Pin overlay during spin | `10000` | internal (engine-managed) |
| Spotlight (winning symbols) | own container | `viewport.spotlightContainer` |

#### Constraints

- A block wider than one reel needs weight 0. Random fill cannot place it
  and the builder throws on a non-zero weight. The server places it through
  `setResult()`.
- A block wider than one reel exists only at landing. During the spin every
  cell is 1x1, and the block layout is applied at the stop. A block one reel
  wide with a weight can also scroll past during the spin, as the
  [tall blocks demo](/mechanics/big-symbols/#tall-symbols-in-spin) shows.
- Big symbols and MultiWays are rejected at build. See the
  [constraint table](/mechanics/big-symbols/#concept-per-reel-geometry).

#### See also

- [Per-reel geometry](/mechanics/big-symbols/#concept-per-reel-geometry): overview, constraints, mask strategy
- [MultiWays](/mechanics/big-symbols/#concept-multiways): cannot be combined with big symbols
- [Block shapes](/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbols-mxn): 1x3, 2x2, 3x3 and 2x4 blocks
- [Partial landing](/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbol-partial-land): tail-visible landings through the start buffer
- [Held respin](/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbol-held-respin): nudge to reveal, then hold across a respin
- [Nudge a big symbol](/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-big-symbol): a block through visible and buffer cells
- [Cell bounds](/mechanics/cells-and-banners/#cell-bounds): pixel rects for any cell

In a MultiWays slot each reel lands on a different cell count, every spin.
The reel's length is fixed and the cell size is derived from it: the extent
divided by that reel's cell count. A 2-cell reel has big cells and a 7-cell
reel has small ones.

#### Setup

```ts
const reelSet = new ReelSetBuilder()
  .reels(6)
  .multiways({ minCells: 2, maxCells: 7, reelExtent: 480 })
  .pinMigrationDuration(300)         // ms for the pin-overlay tween. 0 = snap
  .pinMigrationEase('power2.inOut')  // any GSAP ease
  .symbolSize(68, 68)                // the spin-time cell size
  .build();

const promise = reelSet.spin();
reelSet.setShape([3, 5, 7, 4, 6, 2]);  // before setResult
reelSet.setResult(serverGrid);          // serverGrid[i].visible.length === shape[i]
await promise;
```

#### Call order

1. `spin()`: the reels scroll at the previous shape's cell size.
2. `setShape(cellsPerReel)`: records the target, emits `shape:changed`, then
   migrates pins (`pin:migrated`). Call it before `setResult`. Called after,
   it throws, because the frames are already cached by then.
3. `setResult(grid)`: each column's visible length must equal that reel's
   entry in the shape.
4. The reshape runs between the spin and stop phases. Per reel it fires
   `adjust:start`, commits the geometry, refreshes pin overlays, and fires
   `adjust:complete`.
5. The stop phase lands at the new shape.

#### Pin migration

A pin remembers the cell it started in, its `originCell`. Every reshape moves
it according to its migration policy and fires `pin:migrated` with the old
cell, the new cell, the reel index, and whether it was clamped.

##### The origin policy

`'origin'` is the default. A pin that a shrink moved down to a lower cell
moves back when the reel grows again, which is what a sticky wild needs.

| Spin | Cells on reel 2 | originCell | Lands at | Clamped? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 | 4 | 4 | no |
| 2 | 3 | 4 | 2 | yes |
| 3 | 7 | 4 | 4 | restored |
| 4 | 4 | 4 | 3 | yes |

##### The frozen policy

With `'frozen'`, each clamp rewrites the origin cell, so the pin never moves
back. Use it for walking wilds, or anywhere the pin's current cell matters
and its old cell does not.

| Spin | Cells on reel 2 | originCell before | Lands at | originCell after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| 2 | 3 | 4 | 2 (clamped) | 2 |
| 3 | 7 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| 4 | 4 | 2 | 2 | 2 |

```ts
reelSet.pin(reel, cell, id, { migration: 'frozen' });
```

#### What animates

`pinMigrationDuration` and `pinMigrationEase` apply to pin overlays only. The
cells underneath snap, because the reel is still spinning at full speed
during the reshape, and a tween on a cell would conflict with the motion
layer over the same coordinate.

With no pins on a reel, no tween is built. `adjust:start` and
`adjust:complete` still fire around the reshape, because they come from the
reshape step and not from the tween. If the shape did not change, neither
fires.

`skipSpin()` skips the tween.

#### MultiWays events

- `shape:changed`: `setShape()` accepted a target
- `adjust:start` / `adjust:complete`: per reel, around the reshape
- `pin:migrated`: a pin moved because the shape changed

#### Limits

- No big symbols. A 2x2 cannot fit a reel that reshaped to 2 cells, so
  `build()` throws.
- No pyramid. `visibleCellsPerReel()` and `multiways()` both claim the cell
  count, so `build()` throws.
- `reelExtent` is fixed. To change it, rebuild.

Cascades do work with MultiWays (ADR 015). See the
[MultiWays cascade demo](/mechanics/big-symbols/#multiways-cascade).

#### See also

- [Per-reel geometry](/mechanics/big-symbols/#concept-per-reel-geometry): the overview
- [Big symbols](/mechanics/big-symbols/#concept-big-symbols): what cannot be combined with this
- [MultiWays demo](/mechanics/big-symbols/#multiways): the basic per-spin reshape
- [MultiWays cascade](/mechanics/big-symbols/#multiways-cascade): reshape plus tumble
- [Sticky wild on MultiWays](/mechanics/big-symbols/#sticky-wild-multiways): pin migration running

A reel has more cells than the player sees. `ColumnTarget` addresses all of
them.

#### Why buffers exist

Every reel keeps a few hidden cells past each end of the visible window.
They hold the next symbol about to wrap onto the strip, and they scroll
through view during a spin, so the motion looks continuous. They also let a
win animation move past the edge without showing an empty strip.

Set the count with `.bufferSymbols(n)`. Most slots use 1 or 2. More than 2
is unusual.

#### ColumnTarget

One object per reel. Hand an array of them to `setResult` on the reel set or
to `initialFrame` on the builder. Both take the same shape.

Start is the smaller screen coordinate: above on a vertical set, left on a
horizontal one. It does not follow the travel direction. See
[Orientation & direction](/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#concept).

#### Which index is which cell

One reel, with `bufferSymbols(2)` and `visibleCells(3)`, has seven cells:

The buffers hide behind the mask at rest and pass through view during a
spin.

#### Example

```ts
import type { ColumnTarget } from 'pixi-reels';

const grid: ColumnTarget[] = [
  { visible: ['A', 'B', 'C'], bufferStart: ['COIN', 'WILD'] },
  { visible: ['A', 'B', 'C'], bufferEnd: ['SCATTER'] },
];

reelSet.setResult(grid);
// Same shape at build time:
builder.initialFrame(grid);
```

Index 0 of a buffer array is the slot nearest the visible window and index 1
is one further out. An entry past the configured buffer count throws instead
of being dropped, so the mistake shows at the call.

#### Unset cells

Any cell you leave unset gets a random symbol, buffer cells included. By
default buffer cells draw from the same weight table as the strip. A pool
with `slots: 'buffer'` restricts the cells outside the window only:

```ts
// A coin may blur past mid-spin, but must never park half-visible
// above or below the grid.
reelSet.randomSymbols.set({ exclude: ['COIN'] }, { slots: 'buffer' });

// Same thing at build time, so even the initial strip obeys it.
builder.randomSymbols({ exclude: ['COIN'] }, { slots: 'buffer' });
```

Each end can have its own pool, named after its buffer:

```ts
// Nothing peeks in from above; the cell below the grid is left alone.
reelSet.randomSymbols.set({ exclude: ['COIN'] }, { slots: 'bufferStart' });
```

Add `{ reel: n }` to any of them for one reel only, so `{ reel: 2, slots:
'bufferEnd' }` is one end of one reel. A weight of 0 bans a symbol as surely
as `exclude` does. Each layer applies on top of the wider ones. A symbol the
strip may not show cannot appear in a buffer cell either, and a symbol a
`'buffer'` pool bans is banned at both ends whatever the pools for each end
say. An explicit buffer entry in a target always wins over a pool.

#### Big symbols in buffers

A big-symbol anchor can sit in the start buffer, or in a visible cell whose
block extends into the end buffer. Pass the anchor and the engine fills the
rest of the block.

The block must fit on the strip, not inside the visible window: the anchor
cell plus the block's height may not exceed the visible cells plus the end
buffer. That is what allows a block that is mostly hidden with one cell
showing.

#### See also

- [Peek symbol from the buffer](/mechanics/cascade/#peek-from-above): the smallest runnable version
- [Anticipation teaser](/mechanics/anticipation/#anticipation-teaser): a buffer symbol plus `setAnticipation`
- [Partial landing](/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbol-partial-land): a tail-visible wild
- [ReelSet reference](/reference/api-reelset/): the full `setResult` signature

##### Demos

The first half of this page covers big symbols, one symbol that covers a block of cells. It starts with blocks that land in full view and moves on to blocks that land partly hidden in a buffer or scroll past during the spin. The second half covers boards whose reels show different numbers of cells: a fixed pyramid and MultiWays.

#### Big symbols

##### Block shapes

Four shapes, one demo each: a 2x2 square, a 1x3 tall block, a 3x3 giant and a 2x4 wide block. The server places the anchor cell and the engine fills the rest of the block.

Live demo (big-symbols-mxn-square): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbols-mxn
Live demo (big-symbols-mxn-tall): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbols-mxn
Live demo (big-symbols-mxn-giant): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbols-mxn
Live demo (big-symbols-mxn-wide): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbols-mxn

##### Outline a block

`getBlockBounds` returns one rectangle around the whole block, whichever of its cells you pass. For a 1x1 cell it returns the same rect as `getCellBounds`.

Live demo (get-block-bounds): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#get-block-bounds

##### Spine art

The same 2x2 anchor mechanic with a Spine skeleton in every cell. The big wild reuses the wild rig, scaled to the size of the block.

Live demo (spine-big-symbols): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#spine-big-symbols

##### Horizontal reels

A 2x3 block on a set built with `.orientation('horizontal')`, outlined on landing with `getBlockBounds`. `size: { reels, cells }` is in index space and does not rotate. `reels` always counts across reels, and `cells` always counts along the strip.

The screen shape flips with the orientation. `{ reels: 2, cells: 3 }` is 2 wide and 3 tall on a vertical set, and 2 tall and 3 wide here. `getBlockBounds` works in screen space, so its rect flips too.

Live demo (big-symbols-horizontal-block): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbols-horizontal-block

#### Blocks in the buffer

A block's anchor can sit outside the visible window, so only part of the block shows when the reel lands. The game then brings the rest into view.

##### Land partly in the buffer

A 1x3 block lands with its anchor in `bufferStart`, so only its bottom cell shows, at cell 0. A downward nudge drags the rest into view.

Live demo (big-symbol-partial-land): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbol-partial-land

##### Nudge in, then hold for a respin

The partly hidden wild is nudged into full view. Then the other reels respin with `holdReels`, so the block stays where it is.

Live demo (big-symbol-held-respin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbol-held-respin

##### Reverse reels

The same partial landing on a reel built with `.direction('reverse')`, which rolls up. The block is anchored at the last visible cell with its body in `bufferEnd`, and a `'forward'` nudge, which moves up on this reel, drags it into full view.

Buffers are positional and do not follow the travel direction. `bufferStart` is above and `bufferEnd` is below in both directions, so a reel that feeds from the bottom shows its partial block out of `bufferEnd`.

Live demo (big-symbols-reverse-tail): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbols-reverse-tail

##### Fall into view in a cascade

A tall wild lands with its anchor in `bufferStart` and only its tail showing. The cells below it win, and the wild falls into full view as they clear. The second demo does the same with a 2x2 block across two reels.

The anchor's fall distance must equal the number of winning cells cleared below it, or the block snaps instead of falling.

Live demo (big-symbol-cascade-fall): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbol-cascade-fall
Live demo (big-symbol-cascade-fall-2x2): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbol-cascade-fall

#### Blocks during the spin

##### Tall blocks in the spin

A 1x3 block with a weight scrolls past on reel 0 while it spins, and a scatter only ever scrolls past on reel 4. Both weights are set in per-reel pools: `0` in the base `weights()` table, and raised on the one reel that may show the symbol. Only blocks one reel wide can have a weight. Wider blocks still appear only on landing, because the random fill feeds one reel at a time.

A narrower pool cannot lift an `exclude` set by a wider one, but it can raise a weight of `0`. To allow a symbol on one reel only, use weights, not `exclude`. A weighted block also needs `bufferSymbols({ start: size.cells })`, and the builder checks for it. The block enters a forward reel bottom first and leaves a reverse reel anchor first, and the buffer slots hold its covered cells while the anchor that draws them is off the strip.

Live demo (tall-symbols-in-spin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#tall-symbols-in-spin

##### Peek, then bring it up

Two scatters slow reel 4 into an anticipation crawl, and the weighted 1x3 keeps sliding past during it. The result lands the block with its head on the last visible cell and its body in `bufferEnd`, so the set uses `bufferSymbols({ start: 3, end: 2 })`: `start` for the weight and `end` for the peek. The two demos then bring the block up in different ways.

- Nudge up: `nudge(reel, { distance: 2, direction: 'reverse' })` moves the whole column, and the two cards above scroll out through the top.
- Expand up: the landed anchor is already one sprite three cells tall, with its body under the mask. Tween its view up two cells so it grows over the cards, then call `setColumn(reel, { visible: ['tall', ...] })` to commit the block at the top of the column. The rest of the board stays put. In engine terms this is an expanding wild.

`getBlockBounds` reports the whole block even while part of it is in a buffer. The mask does the clipping.

Live demo (tall-peek-nudge-up): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#tall-peek
Live demo (tall-peek-expand-up): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#tall-peek

#### Reel shapes

##### Pyramid

A set whose reels show 3, 5, 5, 5 and 3 cells. The shape is fixed at build time with `visibleCellsPerReel`.

Live demo (pyramid-shape): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#pyramid-shape

##### Pyramid with Spine

The same pyramid with a Spine skeleton in every cell. The rigs stay sharp at each reel's cell size.

Live demo (spine-pyramid-shape): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#spine-pyramid-shape

##### MultiWays

Each reel lands on a different cell count every spin, and the number of ways is the product of the cell counts.

Call `setShape(cellsPerReel)` before `setResult()` on every spin.

Live demo (multiways): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#spine-pyramid-shape

##### MultiWays cascade

A MultiWays shape on a normal strip landing, followed by a cascade that removes the ways winners and drops new symbols in from above.

Call `setShape` before `setResult`, and start the round with `spin({ mode: 'standard' })` so `AdjustPhase` reshapes the reels between the spin and stop phases.

Live demo (multiways-cascade): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#spine-pyramid-shape

##### Sticky wild on MultiWays

A pin keeps its place across reshapes through its remembered `originCell`, with the default `migration: 'origin'`. It moves in when the reel shrinks and returns when the reel grows back. With `'frozen'`, each clamp rewrites the origin, so the pin never moves back.

Live demo (sticky-wild-multiways): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/big-symbols/#sticky-wild-multiways

### Cascades
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/
Winning symbols burst, the rest fall into the gaps and new ones drop in, until nothing else wins.
Tags: cascade, tumble, refill, anticipation, spine, thunderkick, horizontal, reverse, orientation, gravity

A cascade round has two different moments. Keeping them apart makes
[`.tumble()`](/reference/api-builder/#tumble) and
[`refill()`](/reference/api-reelset/#cascade-tumble) easier to reason about.

#### The two moments

Moment A is the player pressing spin. Everything falls off the bottom, the
reels sit empty while the server thinks, and the new symbols drop in when the
answer arrives.

Moment B is a cascade refill. You clear the winning cells. Survivors above a
hole slide down into it, and new symbols drop in from off-window to fill the
gap at the top, as many per reel as that reel lost. The reels never re-spin.

The same animation engine runs both. The split matters because A is one beat
(fall, wait, drop) with the same shape as `spin()` followed by `setResult()`,
while B is as many beats as there are cascade levels, one per refill until
nothing wins, each starting on whatever the last one landed.

#### The three phases

The engine runs both moments with three `ReelPhase` subclasses:

| Phase | Fires on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `cascade:fall` | Moment A, the `spin()` call | Tweens every visible symbol off the bottom of the viewport, then waits at speed 0. |
| `cascade:place` | Both moments | Swaps the symbol identities for the new grid and snaps every view to its grid position. Survivors become visible at once. New arrivals stay at alpha 0 until `cascade:dropIn` moves them above the viewport. |
| `cascade:dropIn` | Both moments | Tweens each moving view from its origin (above the viewport for new symbols, its old cell for survivors) down to its grid position. Survivors that did not move skip the tween. |

The per-symbol events (`cascade:fall:symbol`, `cascade:dropIn:symbol`) fire
before the library's own tween, so a tween you start in the listener finishes
in step with it.

The chain and destroy events sit on the same bus:

| Event | When | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `cascade:chain:start` | A chain stage opens, after `detectWinners` and before `destroySymbols` | A per-chain sound cue, a chain counter, freezing the spin button. |
| `cascade:destroy:start` / `cascade:destroy:end` | Around every `destroySymbols(...)` batch, direct calls included | A shatter sound, a viewport dim independent of `destroyOptions.dim`. |
| `cascade:chain:end` | A chain stage closes, after the refill drop-in settled | Per-chain teardown, queueing the next decoration. |

`runCascade` emits the chain events. A loop you write yourself with bare
`refill()` calls only gets the per-phase ones.

You can override any phase by registering a subclass under its name:

```ts
builder
  .tumble({ /* ... */ })
  .phases((f) => f.register('cascade:fall', MyCometFallPhase));
```

The other two keep their defaults. Override a phase only when events and
config cannot do what you want. A per-symbol listener is usually enough.

#### Survivor order

The grid you pass to a refill follows one rule per reel. The first cells,
as many as that reel had winners, are new symbols. The rest are the
survivors in their original order. A server-side gravity simulation already
produces this.

Take the reel `['A','B','C','D','E']` with winners at cells 1 and 3:

A grid that follows the rule goes straight into `refill({ winners, grid })`.
One that does not needs a transform on the client first.

`computeDropOffsets` is exported. It is the algorithm the engine uses, so
you can check your server output against it offline.

#### The three calls

A cascade game needs three calls:

```ts
// 1. Fall, wait, drop. Symmetric to a normal spin.
const spinDone = reelSet.spin();                  // or spin({ mode: 'cascade' }) if you also use standard mode
reelSet.setResult(await server.spin());
await spinDone;

// 2. Clear winning cells. The library defers to each symbol's playDestroy().
const winners = detectWinners(reelSet.getVisibleGrid());
await reelSet.destroySymbols(winners);

// 3. Refill survivors + new symbols.
//    grid is ColumnTarget[]. For the common per-reel visible case, wrap
//    your server's string[][] with .map(visible => ({ visible })). For
//    big-symbol anchors that land into the buffer, use the full
//    ColumnTarget shape with bufferStart / bufferEnd.
const next: string[][] = await server.cascade(winners);
await reelSet.refill({ winners, grid: next.map((visible) => ({ visible })) });
```

That is one win and one refill. For a chain, loop it:

```ts
while (true) {
  const winners = detectWinners(reelSet.getVisibleGrid());
  if (winners.length === 0) break;
  await reelSet.destroySymbols(winners);
  await wait(PAUSE_AFTER_REMOVAL_MS);
  const next = await server.cascade(winners);
  await reelSet.refill({ winners, grid: next.map((visible) => ({ visible })) });
}
```

Or call `runCascade` with your two callbacks. It runs the same loop, fires
the per-stage chain events, and resolves with a `RunCascadeResult` summary.
Both callbacks may be async. `nextGrid` is where you await the server.

```ts
await reelSet.runCascade({ detectWinners, nextGrid });
```

#### Per-cascade options

The options a tumble game usually sets:

| Option | Default | When to set |
|---|---|---|
| `pauseAfterDestroyMs` | `250` | Lower it to 150 for a turbo mode, raise it to 500 for a slower round. |
| `maxChain` | `32` | A safety cap. Raise it only if your game can legitimately exceed 32 cascades. |
| `onCascade` | none | Runs once per cascade. Update a multiplier or play a sound here. Return a promise to delay the next refill. |
| `destroyOptions` | `{}` | Forwarded to `destroySymbols(...)`: per-cell stagger, lifted z-index, viewport dim. |
| `signal` | none | An `AbortSignal` that cancels the chain. See [cancelling a chain](#cancelling-a-chain-via-abortsignal). |

```ts
await reelSet.runCascade({
  detectWinners,
  nextGrid,
  pauseAfterDestroyMs: 180,        // snappy
  destroyOptions: {
    delay: (cell, i) => i * 0.03,  // left-to-right disintegration
    dim:   true,                   // dim the viewport while pops play
  },
  onCascade: async ({ chain }) => {
    bumpMultiplier(chain);
    await playWinSound(chain);     // delays the next refill until the sound resolves
  },
});
```

`DestroySymbolsOptions` has four fields: `delay`, `zIndex`, `dim` and
`signal`. The delay can be a function of the cell:

```ts
destroyOptions: {
  delay:  (cell, i) => i * 0.02,   // first-to-last stagger
  zIndex: 1500,                    // lift above the default 1000
  dim:    0.5,                     // custom viewport dim alpha
}
```

#### Cancelling a chain

`skipSpin()` slams the phase in flight, but it returns early when the engine
is idle, which it is between two refills and during the pause. A tap in that
window does nothing and the chain keeps going. Use an `AbortController` for
the chain:

```ts
const controller = new AbortController();
skipButton.addEventListener('click', () => controller.abort());

await reelSet.runCascade({
  detectWinners,
  nextGrid,
  signal: controller.signal,
});
// summary.wasSkipped === true after an abort
```

When the signal aborts, `runCascade` sets its skipped flag, calls
`slamStop()` if a refill is in flight so the await unblocks at once, exits at
the next await boundary, and resolves with `wasSkipped: true` in the result.

Wire both to the skip button: `skipSpin()` cuts the phase that is moving,
and the abort ends the chain.

#### `refill()` or `runCascade()`?

Start with `runCascade`. It is a short wrapper around `refill` and handles
the skip path for you. Use bare `refill` when the chain needs something the
options do not cover, such as different pauses per level, branching per
level, or a game loop that already owns the chain. Writing it yourself means the loop
above, plus the chain events and the abort handling if you need them.

#### Other features in a cascade

The rest of the reel set API keeps working during a cascade:

- `setDropOrder('all')` makes every reel drop together. Set it once before
  `runCascade` and it holds for every refill in the chain.
- `setStopDelays([...])` sets per-reel delays, for a V-shape or an
  outside-in reveal.
- `speed.set('turbo')` changes the strip-spin speed on standard rounds.
  Cascade phase durations are static (see [`TumbleConfig`](/reference/api-builder/#tumble)),
  so for fast cascades you swap the `.tumble({})` config or override the
  phase.
- `pin(...)` persists a cell across cascades. A pinned wild stays put through
  every refill in the round.
- `reelSet.viewport.showDim(alpha)` dims the whole board. Pair it with
  `destroySymbols(..., { dim: true })` to draw the eye to the winners.

#### The empty wait

Between `cascade:fall:end` and `cascade:dropIn:start` the board is empty and
the server has not answered. Show a spinner on fall end and hide it on the
first drop-in, or show nothing. A server reply under 100 ms is not noticed.
If the gap still shows, shorten `fall.duration`.

#### The pause matters

Leave a pause between the winners fading out and the refill starting.
Without it the refill begins on the frame the winners reach alpha 0, and the
symbols look like they teleported. With 150 to 500 ms between them the
player sees two events, the wins clearing and then the new symbols arriving.
The default is 250 ms. Around 120 ms feels fast, around 350 ms feels
relaxed. Set it with `pauseAfterDestroyMs` in `runCascade()`, or with your
own wait in your own loop.

#### Override a phase, or listen to events?

To run something alongside the library's tween, listen to
`cascade:fall:symbol` or `cascade:dropIn:symbol`. They fire first, so your
tween stays in step with theirs.

To decorate symbols after they land, listen to `cascade:place:end`. Its
`isInitial` and `winnerCells` fields let you skip survivors.

To hold a beat between fall and drop-in, override `cascade:place` and put the
beat in its `onEnter`. A listener cannot gate a phase.

To make symbols fly sideways instead of falling, override `cascade:fall`.

Override only when a listener cannot do it. A phase of your own has to
implement the whole `ReelPhase` contract, which is `onEnter`, `update`,
`onSkip` and `_complete`.
