#### Basic cascade

A 6x4 board where `runCascade` runs the loop. You pass `detectWinners` and `nextGrid`, and it destroys, refills and asks again until `detectWinners` returns no cells. The second canvas is the same recipe with Thunderkick Spine symbols; only the symbol registration differs.

Live demo (cascade-6x5): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-6x4-tumble
Live demo (cascade-6x5-spine): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-6x4-tumble

#### Removing winners

Each cascade step runs in a fixed order: present the win, destroy the winning symbols, refill the holes. Work out the winners from your match logic. Diffing the grid before and after does not work, because survivors slide past the cleared cells and a diff reads them as changed.

##### Present the win first

Two winning combinations share reel 2. `runCascade` hands them to a `WinPresenter` through its `presentWinners` hook, which shows each one in turn before the winners explode and the refill drops.

Live demo (destroy-winpresenter): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-wins-present-destroy-refill

##### Default destroy

No `out` animation is registered, so `destroySymbols` plays the engine's scale and fade implode. Use this when you have no destruction art.

Live demo (destroy-fade): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-wins-present-destroy-refill

##### Spine explosion

The same board with `outAnimation: 'explode'` set at registration. `destroySymbols` plays the skeleton's explosion instead of the implode.

Live demo (destroy-explode): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-wins-present-destroy-refill

#### Timing and motion

These demos run the same spin and the same win. Only the timing or the motion of the fall and the refill changes.

##### Delay before the fall

The pause between the spin press and the first frame of the fall: 0, 150, 350 and 700 ms. A longer pause adds suspense before the board clears.

Live demo (fall-delay-instant): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#lead-in-delay-before-the-fall
Live demo (fall-delay-subtle): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#lead-in-delay-before-the-fall
Live demo (fall-delay-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#lead-in-delay-before-the-fall
Live demo (fall-delay-suspense): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#lead-in-delay-before-the-fall

##### Refill order

The order the new symbols arrive in after a win. All reels at once with `setDropOrder('all')`, a left-to-right wave, and bottom-up, where the bottom cell lands first (`cellOrder: 'endFirst'`).

Live demo (refill-simultaneous): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-refill-orders
Live demo (refill-ltr-wave): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-refill-orders
Live demo (refill-bottom-up): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-refill-orders

##### Tumble motion

Five `.tumble({ fall, dropIn })` configs on the same round: classic, slow drop, slam, rain column and wave. They differ in durations, eases and per-cell stagger.

Live demo (tumble-classic): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#tumble-feels-every-preset
Live demo (tumble-cartoon-bounce): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#tumble-feels-every-preset
Live demo (tumble-slam): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#tumble-feels-every-preset
Live demo (tumble-rain-column): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#tumble-feels-every-preset
Live demo (tumble-wave): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#tumble-feels-every-preset

##### Two-stage refill

`refill({ mode: 'gravity-then-drop' })` splits the refill in two. Survivors slide down first, the engine holds for `gravityHoldMs`, then the new symbols drop in. Put a multiplier or a mascot beat in the hold. The second canvas drops the reels one after another instead of in a wave, with a longer hold.

Live demo (tumble-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-anticipation-refill
Live demo (tumble-anticipation-stagger): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-anticipation-refill

#### Opening the round with a spin

Many cascade games open each round with an ordinary strip spin and only cascade the follow-ups. The first canvas does that with `spin({ mode: 'standard' })`. The second opens with a cascade drop instead, so the old board falls out and the new one drops in. The third is the spin opener tuned for turbo: the strip spins on cached textures and the cascade uses a shorter drop-in and a faster explode.

Live demo (spin-then-cascade): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#spin-first-cascade-after
Live demo (cascade-open-drop): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#spin-first-cascade-after
Live demo (spin-then-cascade-turbo): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#spin-first-cascade-after

#### Gravity and orientation

By default a reel drains toward the edge it travels toward and refills from the other one. Gravity also decides the server contract. Survivors must be packed against the edge they drain through, and the engine animates the grid you send as it is. It never reorders it.

##### Sideways

The same tumble on `.orientation('horizontal')`. Reels are screen rows, the strip travels along X, and `tumble({ gravity })` stays on its default `'auto'`. Under forward gravity, `nextGrid` returns `[...fresh, ...survivors]`.

Live demo (cascade-horizontal-tumble): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-sideways

##### Upward

A `.direction('reverse')` set with no `gravity` key. Gravity follows travel, so the top cell falls and lands first and the column empties upward. The survivors now pack against the top, so `nextGrid` returns `[...survivors, ...fresh]`. If you reverse the reels and keep the old grid order, the board looks scrambled.

Live demo (cascade-drain-upward): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#drain-upward-gravity-follows-travel

##### Spin up, settle down

Reels built `.direction('reverse')` roll upward, and `tumble({ gravity: 'forward' })` makes the tumble settle downward anyway. Set `gravity` only when you want travel and settling to disagree.

The cell stagger follows gravity too. `cellOrder` defaults to `'auto'`, which starts at the end symbols leave through. Here the bottom cell still goes first; without the `gravity` override the top cell would lead. Pass `'endFirst'` or `'startFirst'` to fix the starting end whatever the gravity.

Live demo (cascade-reverse-gravity): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#spin-up-drop-down-explicit-gravity

#### Teaser in the buffer

A strip spin with no cascade. A symbol placed in the `bufferStart` slot sits above the window and scrolls through it at the start of the next spin, so the player sees it briefly before the random symbols take over.

Live demo (peek-from-above): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cascade/#peek-symbol-from-buffer-start

### Paylines and overlays
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cells-and-banners/
Find any cell on screen to draw paylines, badges and highlights over the board, or to make a cell tappable.
Tags: paylines, hit-areas, overlays, wins, horizontal, orientation

`reelSet.spotlight` dims the losing symbols, lifts the winners above the
mask, and can step through several lines in turn.

#### One win, one line

```ts
reelSet.events.on('spin:complete', async (result) => {
  const wins = detectWins(result.symbols);      // your logic
  if (wins.length === 0) return;

  // positions: [{ reelIndex, cellIndex }, ...]
  await reelSet.spotlight.show(wins[0].positions, {
    dimAmount: 0.3,
    playWinAnimation: true,
  });
});
```

#### Several lines in turn

```ts
await reelSet.spotlight.cycle(
  wins.map((w) => ({ positions: w.positions })),   // WinLine[]
  {
    displayDuration: 1000,   // ms per line. Default 2000
    gapDuration: 300,        // ms between lines
    cycles: 1,
    dimAmount: 0.3,          // losers fade to 30%
  },
);
```

#### Symbol animations

With `playWinAnimation: true` the spotlight calls `playWin()` on each
highlighted symbol. The three built-in symbol classes all implement it.

```ts
await reelSet.spotlight.show(wins[0].positions, { playWinAnimation: true });
```

`show()` resolves when the animation is done, so you can await it before
the next step.

#### Events

`spotlight:start` and `spotlight:end` bracket a `cycle()`. Use them to
disable the spin button while a win plays.

##### Demos

`reelSet.getCellBounds(reel, cell)` returns the screen rect of a visible cell. Paylines, win outlines and hit areas are all drawn from it, so they line up with the symbols. The engine itself draws no paylines. For a banner reel above the grid, see [Sideways and upward reels](/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#horizontal-banner).

#### Cell rects

The rect of any visible cell, used here to outline cells and draw a line through them.

Live demo (cell-bounds): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cells-and-banners/#cell-bounds-overlays-paylines--hit-areas

#### Paylines

##### From win events

`WinPresenter` animates the winning symbols and draws nothing else. Subscribe to `win:group` and draw each line from `getCellBounds`. `win:symbol` fires per winning symbol, for anything drawn per cell.

Live demo (paylines-events-only): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cells-and-banners/#draw-paylines-yourself-from-wingroup

##### With WinLines

`WinLines` from `pixi-reels/debug` draws the cells it is given. A payline is one stroke through one cell per reel. A payway joins every winning cell to every winning cell on the next reel. The demo alternates: one spin pays ten fixed lines and draws each as the presenter reaches it, the next pays ways and draws all of them at once.

Live demo (win-lines): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cells-and-banners/#paylines-and-payways-with-winlines

#### Tappable cells

One pointer target per cell, built from `getCellBounds`. Hover previews a cell, a click toggles a pick, and picks stay through spins.

Fill the hit rect with alpha 0 rather than setting `visible = false`. A transparent filled rect still receives pointer events; a hidden one does not.

Live demo (cell-hit-areas): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cells-and-banners/#cell-hit-areas-click-to-pick-hover-to-preview

#### Horizontal sets

##### Rects

`getCellBounds(reel, cell)` takes the same arguments on either axis, and (0, 0) is still the first cell of the first reel. The rect it returns is transposed: on a horizontal set the reel index goes down the screen and the cell index goes across it.

So a line through the same cell index on every reel runs vertically here, where the same code draws a horizontal line on a vertical set. Read the rects instead of working them out from the indices.

Live demo (cells-horizontal-bounds): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cells-and-banners/#cell-bounds-on-a-horizontal-set

##### Hit areas

The same loop over reels and cells as the vertical demo, with no orientation check. The rects are already in screen space, so the hit areas sit on the symbols either way.

Live demo (cells-horizontal-hit-areas): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/cells-and-banners/#hit-areas-on-a-horizontal-set

### Spin feel
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/feel/
Tune how a spin starts and stops: the stagger between reels, a wind-up, the kick on landing.
Tags: phases, steps, timing, fx, anticipation, speed, skip

A speed profile holds the numbers that decide how a spin feels, such as the
acceleration, the spin speed, the stagger between stops and the bounce.

#### The three defaults

```ts
import { SpeedPresets } from 'pixi-reels';

// SpeedPresets.NORMAL        relaxed feel
// SpeedPresets.TURBO         faster stop, short acceleration
// SpeedPresets.SUPER_TURBO   almost instant
```

A builder with no `.speed()` call gets `NORMAL` under the name `'normal'`.

#### Switch at runtime

```ts
reelSet.speed.addProfile('turbo', SpeedPresets.TURBO);
reelSet.setSpeed('turbo');
reelSet.events.on('speed:changed', (p, prev) => console.log(p.name, prev.name));
```

#### Custom profile

```ts
const CINEMATIC: SpeedProfile = {
  name: 'cinematic',
  spinDelay: 280,
  spinSpeed: 38,
  stopDelay: 180,
  anticipationDelay: 1200,
  bounceDistance: 14,
  bounceDuration: 260,
  accelerationEase: 'power3.in',
  bounceEase: 'elastic.out(1, 0.5)',
  accelerationDuration: 420,
  minimumSpinTime: 1400,
};

builder
  .speed('cinematic', CINEMATIC)
  .initialSpeed('cinematic');
```

The engine fires events for each moment of a round, and your audio engine
plays sounds. `attachReelSounds` connects the two with a table that says
which sound plays on which event, when a loop starts and when it fades out.

#### The cue table

```ts
import { createEngine } from '@schmooky/zvuk';
import { attachReelSounds, zvukPort } from 'pixi-reels';

const engine = createEngine({ buses: { reels: {}, anticipation: {}, wins: {}, ui: {} } });
await engine.unlock(); // from a gesture
await engine.loadSound('spin', ['/sfx/spin.webm', '/sfx/spin.m4a'], { bus: 'reels' });
await engine.loadVariants('reel-stop', [
  ['/sfx/reel-stop.1.webm', '/sfx/reel-stop.1.m4a'],
  ['/sfx/reel-stop.2.webm', '/sfx/reel-stop.2.m4a'],
], { bus: 'reels' });
// ... anticipation, skip, win, pop

const sounds = attachReelSounds(reelSet, zvukPort(engine), {
  spin: { play: 'spin' },
  reelStop: { play: 'reel-stop', pitch: { jitter: 0.04 },
              delay: ({ profile }) => profile.bounceDuration / 2000 },
  anticipation: { loop: 'anticipation', fadeIn: 0.12, fadeOut: 0.25,
                  pitch: ({ order }) => 1 + 0.08 * order },
  skip: { play: 'skip' },
  win: { play: 'win' },
  cascadeDestroy: { play: 'pop' },
});

sounds.destroy(); // when the reel set goes
```

The demos on this site run a table like this one. `reelSounds(reelSet)` from
`@pixi-reels/kit/sound` attaches it to a set, using one audio engine for the
whole page, and `boardSounds(board)` does the same for a Hold & Win board.
The Sound button under a demo mutes it. The files load on the first press.

The spin cue plays once per spin. A loop under every spin
(`spin: { loop: 'spin-loop', fadeIn: 0.05, fadeOut: 0.08 }`) is supported and
fades out on the last landing, but on a page with many demos it gets
tiring. The reel stop sounds are enough to mark the rhythm.

#### The beats

| Cue | Starts on | A loop ends on | Context |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spin` | `spin:start` | `spin:allLanded` | |
| `reelStop` | `spin:reelLanding`, on every landing path, cascade refills included | | `reelIndex` |
| `anticipation` | `anticipation:reel`, one per teasing reel | that reel's `anticipation:reelEnd` | `order`, `total`, `reelIndex` |
| `skip` | `skip:requested` | | |
| `win` | `spotlight:start`, and `win:group` per presented win | | |
| `cascadeDestroy` | `cascade:destroy:start` | | |
| `on[event]` | the named event | its `until` event | |

Every context also carries `speed` (the active profile's name), `profile`
(the profile itself) and `mode` (`'standard'`, or `'cascade'` for a tumble
and its refills).

The default table the demos run uses `on` for events outside the spin
lifecycle. It plays a shove on `nudge:start`, a tick on `column:set` when a
symbol splits or a column changes, a rising sweep when a set gains cells or
reels (`expand:stepAdded`, `reels:added`, `rows:added`), and a soft pop on
`pin:placed`.

#### A Hold & Win board

`attachBoardSounds(board, port, cues)` is the same table over a board's
beats: `featureEnter`, `respinStart` (a loop that runs until `respin:end`),
`cellLanded` (with `reelIndex`, `cell` and `hit`), `coinLocked`, `boardFull`,
`featureEnd`, and `on` for any other board event. The demos play a quiet
kick per respin, a thud when a coin lands, a ring a moment after it locks,
and the win sound once when the feature ends. Empty cells land without a
sound.

A cue is `{ play: name }` for a one-shot or `{ loop: name, fadeIn, fadeOut }`
for a bed. `volume` and `pitch` take a number, a `{ base, jitter }` spread so
repeated thuds do not sound cloned, or a function of the context. The tease
cue above climbs about a semitone per reel, and a spin cue can read `speed`
to pitch up in turbo. `delay` is the time in seconds between the event and the
sound. The demos delay the thud by half the profile's `bounceDuration`, which
is when the reel reaches the bottom of its bounce. Without the delay it would
play on the frame the reel snaps. `when(ctx)` keeps a cue quiet. On a tumble, where the
symbols drop in one by one, the demos play the kick and the thuds at half
level with no delay.

Loops are tracked per event, so there is one tease loop per reel. They fade out
when their beat ends and stop at once on `destroy()` or when the reel set is
destroyed.

#### Any engine

`attachReelSounds` only needs a `ReelAudioPort`: a `play(name, { bus, volume,
pitch })` method and a `loop(name, { ..., fadeIn })` method that returns
`{ stop({ fade }) }`. `zvukPort` is that port over a zvuk engine. A variants
set plays its next take, and a missing name is skipped with one warning. Wrap
Howler or raw Web Audio the same way.

##### Demos

These demos change how a spin starts and stops. The first two react to a reel landing. The rest edit the step lists the built-in phases run.

#### Landing

##### Landing events

`spin:reelLanding` fires on the frame a reel reaches its result: the strip has snapped, every symbol has been told it landed, and the bounce is about to start. `spin:reelLanded` fires once the bounce has settled, a whole `bounceDuration` later, or on the same tick after a slam. Hang anything tied to the landing itself on the first one. The demo grows a takeover plate over the copy reels on `spin:reelLanding` and prints the gap between the two events.

Live demo (landing-signal): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/feel/#landing-the-frame-and-the-beat

##### Spine landing animation

Each symbol hears the same moment through `onReelLanded(ctx)`, with the reel and cell it landed in. A Spine symbol's `autoPlayLanding` can be a function of that context. It returns `true` for the configured landing animation, `false` for none, or an animation name to play something else. Here the copy reels land with no animation, so nothing competes with the takeover, and the last two reels play a reveal as their landing.

Live demo (spine-landing-rule): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/feel/#spine-landing-rule

#### Editing the step lists

The built-in phases run named step lists. `StartPhase` runs `delay, launch, pull, accelerate, announce`, `StopPhase` runs `delay, spinOut, land, bounce`, and `AnticipationPhase` runs `tease`. Registering a phase with `f.register('stop', StopPhase, { steps })` passes you the list before it runs. Each demo below changes it with one `insertBefore`, `insertAfter` or `replaceStep` call, or builds the list by hand. Slam and quicken keep working because the waits stay marked `cut`. The step API is on the [Phases page](/reference/api-phases/#steps).

##### Landing kick

One step after `land` and before `bounce`. The reel set kicks and a puff of dust spreads under the reel, harder on the last one. The step returns nothing, so the bounce starts on the same frame. If it returned the tween, the phase would wait for it before bouncing. That return value is what decides whether a step is an effect or a beat.

A slam lands the reel through `onSkip`, not through the list, so a step after `land` does not run on a slam. Effects that must also play on a slam belong on `spin:reelLanded`. A quicken keeps the list.

Live demo (steps-land-impact): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/feel/#a-landing-kick-with-dust

##### Stagger curves

The flat stagger arrives as `ctx.config.delay`, and the `delay` step is the only place it is used. So a curve is one `replaceStep` per phase. Here the start ripples out from the middle reel, and the gaps between stops grow, so reels 1 to 3 land quickly and reel 5 hangs. The profile still sets the unit. The second line of the readout shows measured landings, not the schedule.

Keep `{ cut: true }` on the replacement. It is a wait, and a quicken press has to cut it the same way it cuts the flat one.

Live demo (steps-stagger-curve): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/feel/#steps-stagger-curve

##### Wind-up launch

The built-in `pull` moves the reel back two pixels. This demo replaces it with a pull of most of a cell, inserts a `hold` after it, and leaves `accelerate` as it is, so the reel accelerates from wherever the pull left it. Tap the readout to turn the wind-up off and compare.

Handle both motion models the way the built-in step does. Under the drive model, set a `targetSpeed` and wait. Under the tween model, tween `reel.speed`. `reel.hasDrive` tells you which one is active.

Live demo (steps-windup-start): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/feel/#a-wind-up-launch

##### Extra wait on the last reel

Every reel runs the same list, so a beat for one reel is a step that does nothing on the others. `suspense` waits 700 ms before reel 5's spin-out and returns at once on the other reels. The backlight pulses while it waits.

A step that starts something has to stop it on every way out. `ctx.wait` resolves early when the step is cut, and `ctx.signal` fires when it is cancelled, so one `stop` call covers the natural end, a quicken and a slam.

Live demo (steps-last-reel-suspense): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/feel/#one-extra-beat-on-the-last-reel

##### Spotlight around the tease

`AnticipationPhase` runs one step and is created only on the teased reel. To shade the other reels while the tease runs, build the list by hand around the built-in step: `[dim, ...steps, lift]`. Both added steps are awaited, 150 ms each, so the shade is on before the reel starts to crawl and off before the stop phase takes over.

A slam cancels the list in flight and `lift` never runs, so also clear the shades on `spin:complete`. A quicken cuts the `tease` step and `lift` still runs.

Live demo (steps-anticipation-spotlight): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/feel/#a-spotlight-around-the-tease

#### Steps that read the speed profile

##### Per speed mode

`ctx.profile` is the profile the game registered under the active speed name, custom fields included. A `breath` step before the spin-out and a `glow` step after `land` both read it, so normal gets both and turbo gets neither, and the glow's fade follows `bounceDuration`. Tap the readout to switch speeds. The skip button here calls `requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken', speed: 'turbo' })`, which switches the profile the same way.

Do not check for turbo inside a step. Put the decision on the profile, and every speed mode you add later carries its own setting.

Live demo (steps-fx-per-profile): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/feel/#beats-and-fx-that-follow-the-speed-mode

##### Profile sections

The demo above puts a step's settings on the profile as flat fields. That works, but every phase sees them and nothing says which phase they belong to. A section does. Both steps here are inserted into `StopPhase`, so their settings live under `stop`, keyed by step name. The `whenAnticipated` half is merged on top for a reel that teased, so reels 4 and 5 land with a deeper bounce and a heavier impact, and the same step draws them amber based on `ctx.anticipated`. Nothing checks the speed name.

```ts
stop: {
  steps: { breath: { duration: 140 }, impact: { lift: 8, duration: 420 } },
  whenAnticipated: { bounceDistance: 30, steps: { impact: { lift: 24 } } },
}
```

A step reads its own entry as `ctx.step`, in segment order. One object in the profile arrives as one entry; a list is for a step written to read several segments. Declare the two names once by merging them into `StopSteps`, and `stop.steps` is type-checked and autocompleted like the built-in steps.

`whenAnticipated` applies only to a tease that ran to the end. Press skip mid-tease and that reel uses the section's base settings (blue puff, small lift), because the press cut the tease the variant is there to follow.

Live demo (steps-profile-sections): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/feel/#a-step-you-added-tuned-from-the-profile

### Hold & Win
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/
Coins stick where they land and the empty cells respin until the counter runs out or the board fills.
Tags: hold-and-win, coins, collector, respin, spine, horizontal, reverse, orientation, rectangular, clovers

Hold & Win, also sold as Lock & Respin or Hold & Spin, is a feature where
coins land, stick, and refill a respin counter until the board fills or the
respins run out. pixi-reels ships it as a built-in board:

```ts
import { HoldAndWinBuilder } from 'pixi-reels';
```

The demos above each show one technique. This part explains how the board
works as a whole and how a game client drives it.

#### How the board is built

A Hold & Win board is a grid of cells that spin independently. The engine
spins in columns, each a `ReelSet`, but the mechanic works in cells. So each
cell is its own 1x1 reel set, and `HoldAndWinBuilder` lays out the grid and
runs the round across them.

The board does not know what a coin is worth. A coin is an opaque record:

```ts
{ cell: { reel, cell }, id: 'coin', data: /* anything you want */ }
```

The `id` picks the registered symbol art. The `data` belongs to you and can
hold values, jackpot tiers, multipliers or collector flags. The board never
reads it. Adders, doublers, collectors and flights to a meter are game logic
you write on top of the board, using these:

| API | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| `board.events` | each step of the round, with the coin payload |
| `board.symbolAt(cell)` | the live symbol instance, so you can call your own symbol's methods |
| `board.cellCenter(cell)` / `board.cellBounds(cell)` | exact pixel geometry for flights and trails |

With that split, a new Hold & Win variant is mostly game code and the board
stays the same.

#### The round

The board is a three-state machine. `board.phase` reports where it is:
`'idle'`, `'active'` or `'spinning'`.

1. `enter(seed)` seeds the board with the trigger coins. They lock at once,
   without a spin, and the respin counter arms. The board goes from idle to
   active.
2. `respin(hits)` spins each free cell. The cells named in `hits` land their
   coins and the others land blank. The board goes from active to spinning
   and back. If a coin landed in this wave the counter resets to full. If
   nothing landed it goes down by one.
3. The feature ends when the board fills or the counter reaches zero, and
   the board returns to idle. Then you collect.

##### Events in one respin

Events come in a fixed order. Cells land in stagger order, so the landing
and lock events arrive one at a time:

#### Driving it from your game client

The board runs the animation of each round. You own the loop and the source
of results, which can be an RGS, a mock server or an RNG. The driver is
short:

```ts
const board = new HoldAndWinBuilder<{ value: number }>()
  .grid(5, 3)
  .cellSize(72, { gap: 4 })
  .symbols((r) => r.register('coin', CoinSymbol, COIN_OPTS))
  .weights({ coin: 1, empty: 4 })   // how often coins flash past during the spin
  .respins(3)
  .ticker(app.ticker)               // required: drives every cell's reel
  .build();

app.stage.addChild(board.container);

// React to the round however your game presents it: HUD, sounds, flights.
board.events.on('coin:locked', ({ coin, locked, capacity }) => {
  hud.total += coin.data?.value ?? 0;     // you own the value; the board does not
  hud.text = `${locked} / ${capacity}`;
});

// 1. trigger
board.enter(await server.triggerCoins());

// 2. the respin loop: one round per iteration, you pace it
while (true) {
  const round = await server.nextRound(board.freeCells);   // your result source
  const result = await board.respin(round.hits);           // the board animates the wave
  if (result.done) break;                                  // full or out of respins
  // anything between rounds (celebrate, delay, play a teaser) happens here
}

// 3. collect: release the coins and fly them wherever you like
for (const coin of board.lockedCoins) flyToMeter(board.cellCenter(coin.cell), coin.data?.value ?? 0);
board.release(board.lockedCoins.map((c) => c.cell));
```

`respin()` resolves only after the whole wave has landed and the counter has
been updated, so the loop reads top to bottom.

For a [skip button](/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-skip), call
`board.skip()`. It slams each cell that is still spinning. The landing, lock
and feature-end events still fire, so the rest of your code does not change.
The quicken form, `board.skip({ mode: 'quicken' })`, lands the cells instead
of cutting them. Each spinning cell drops its minimum spin time, so the wave
lands together, and each cell still spins its symbol in and bounces. Add
`speed: 'turbo'` to land it on turbo, or make quicken the board's default
with `skipMode('quicken')` on the builder.

#### Events

Each event carries your `TData` on its coins.

| Event | Payload | Fires when |
|---|---|---|
| `feature:enter` | `{ seed, respins }` | `enter()` seeds the board |
| `respin:start` | `{ round, respinsLeft, spinning }` | a wave begins |
| `cell:landed` | `{ cell, coin }` (`coin: null` on a miss) | each cell settles, in stagger order |
| `coin:locked` | `{ coin, locked, capacity }` | a hit cell locks |
| `cells:activated` | `{ cells, capacity }` | `activate()` woke dormant cells; `capacity` is the new full-board count |
| `speed:changed` | `{ name, previous }` | `setSpeed()` moved every cell to another profile |
| `respins:changed` | `{ value, reason }` | the counter changed (`seed`, `hit-reset` or `miss`) |
| `respin:end` | `{ round, hits, respinsLeft }` | the wave finishes |
| `board:full` | `{ coins }` | the last free cell locks |
| `feature:end` | `{ coins, rounds, full }` | the feature is over and the board is idle |
| `coin:released` | `{ coin, remaining }` | `release()` removed a coin (the collect moment) |
| `feature:reset` | `{ clearedCoins }` | `reset()` hard-cleared the board |
| `feature:skip` | `{ inFlight, mode, speed?, payload? }` | `skip()` freed the in-flight cells, placed (`'slam'`) or landing through their stop (`'quicken'`). `speed` and `payload` are the press's options as given |

`release()` means "collect this coin" and fires `coin:released` once per
coin. `reset()` is a hard clear back to idle and fires a single
`feature:reset`, so a HUD that counts down on collect does not tick on a
reset.

`setSymbolAt(cell, id, data)` rewrites a locked coin in place, for example
a coin becoming MINI and then MAJOR, and keeps the board's ledger correct.
It throws on a free cell. New tracked coins are placed only by `enter` and
`respin`.

#### Other builder options

Production boards often need more than the square default. These builder
options cover cell shape, the lock animation and cells that start outside
the feature:

```ts
const board = new HoldAndWinBuilder()
  .grid(5, 3)
  // art is 202x170: a seam between columns, rows touching
  .cellSize({ width: 101, height: 85 }, { columnGap: 6, rowGap: 0 })
  // 'win' (default) plays playWin() on every lock; 'landing' plays the
  // symbol's playLanding() settle instead; 'none' plays nothing
  .lockAnimation('landing')
  // built, drawn as `sealed`, but outside the feature until activate()
  .inactive(row(0).concat(row(4)), 'sealed')
  ...
```

With `'landing'` or `'none'` the celebration is up to you.
`await board.playWin()` pulses each locked coin, and
`board.playWin(cells)` pulses a subset. Call it when the game decides, usually on `board:full` or after
`feature:end`.

Some coins start their own landing beat when they land, such as a Spine coin
with `autoPlayLanding` or a sprite that reports its settle through
`trackLanding`. They keep it. `'win'` waits for that beat before the
celebration, and `'landing'` does not play it a second time. The mode can
also be a function of the coin that locked, so a collector celebrates while
plain coins only settle:

```ts
.lockAnimation((coin) => coin.id === 'collector' ? 'win' : 'landing')
```

`board.activate(cells)` wakes dormant cells between waves. They show the
empty symbol, join the next respin and count toward `isFull` from then on.
`reset()` seals them again. The rectangular cells, landing only and growing
board demos above show each of these.

#### Draw order between cells

Each cell is its own reel set, so a coin's `zIndex` only sorts it against
its own cell's buffers. Art that the engine lifts above a cell's mask at rest
(`unmask: true`) renders in one layer above all cells, in attach order,
which is column by column. As a result the next column covers the overflow
of a lower coin. `cellZIndex` makes that layer sortable, and the board asks
it for each cell's order on each place and landing:

```ts
.cellZIndex(({ cell, symbolId, cols }) =>
  (symbolId === 'grand' ? 1000 : 0) + cell.cell * cols + cell.reel)
```

`board.liftedLayer` is that layer, for an effect that has to sit between the
cells and their lifted art. `symbolZIndex(resolver)` is the per-symbol form
from `ReelSetBuilder`, applied inside each cell. See
[big symbols](/mechanics/big-symbols/#zindex-layering).

#### Speeds

Each cell is its own reel set with its own `SpeedManager`. The board
registers speeds in all of them and switches all of them together:

```ts
const board = new HoldAndWinBuilder()
  .speeds({ normal: NORMAL, turbo: TURBO, superTurbo: SUPER_TURBO })
  ...
board.setSpeed('turbo');            // every cell, at once; fires speed:changed
board.addSpeed('cinematic', slow);  // one more, after build
```

Cells land in a diagonal wave, and the wave's step is the active profile's
`stopDelay`. On a reel set that value is the time between reels stopping. On
a board it is the time between steps of the wave. Each cell spins
`(reel + cell) * stopDelay` ms on top of the profile's `minimumSpinTime`, so
NORMAL's 140 ms steps the wave and TURBO's 0 lands all cells together.
`.stagger(fn)` replaces the shape of the wave. It receives the speed's name
and profile:

```ts
.stagger((reel, cell, speed, profile) => reel * profile.stopDelay) // column by column
.stagger((reel) => reel * 120)                                     // fixed, whatever the speed
```

The rule is the same as for `reelSet.setSpeed()`. A cell already in flight
finishes on the profile it started with, and the next wave runs on the new
one. To cut a wave in progress on a turbo press, call `board.skip()`. To
land it on turbo instead, call `board.skip({ mode: 'quicken', speed: 'turbo' })`.
Each speed name also gets a `name:tension` variant that the board uses for
an anticipating wave.

#### When the board does not fit

pixi-reels ships boards in two layers:

- `BoardGrid` is the primitive. It is a grid of cells that each spin
  independently. It knows geometry, instances and spinning, and nothing about
  coins, locks, respins or value.
- `HoldAndWinBoard` is one board built entirely on the primitive's public
  API. It adds the rules for locking, respins and collecting.

If the built-in board does not do what your game needs, these are the
options, from least to most work:

1. Configure it. Stagger, respins, weights, anticipation and cell chrome are
   all builder options. Most games stop here.
2. Build on the primitive. If your feature is not lock and respin at all,
   for example pick and reveal, cluster collect or a scratch card, skip
   `HoldAndWinBuilder` and use `BoardGrid` directly. The
   [board grid reveal demo](/mechanics/layers/#board-grid-reveal) is a board
   on the primitive that is not Hold & Win.
3. Fork the board. For lock and respin with different rules, copy
   `HoldAndWinBoard` and `HoldAndWinState` into your project and point their
   imports at `pixi-reels`. Everything they use (`BoardGrid`, `EventEmitter`,
   the `Hw*` types, `cellKey`, `HwEffect`) is public API, so the copy stays
   on supported ground. Then rewrite the reducer. The rule that a hit resets
   the respins and the rule that a full board ends the feature both live in
   `HoldAndWinState`.

The board never reads your `data` and has no paytable. What a coin means is
decided in your code, and the board only moves the reels.

#### Where to go next

- The [event trace](/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-trace) prints each event as it fires.
- The [respin round](/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win) is the smallest board.
- A coin's value can live [in the coin's data](/mechanics/hold-and-win/#coin-value-data) or [in a symbol class](/mechanics/hold-and-win/#coin-value-symbol).
- For collecting, see the [collector with flights](/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-collector) and [fly to a meter](/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-meter).
- For tension on the last cell, see [anticipation](/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-anticipation).
- To go from the base game into the feature and back, see [from the base game](/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-base-to-feature).

##### Demos

The demos start with the smallest board and add one idea at a time. The last sections cover draw order and dimming, which most boards only need once the art is in.

#### The basic board

##### Respin round

Coins lock where they land and the free cells respin until the grid fills or the respins run out. The board runs the round. The coin values belong to your game.

Live demo (hold-and-win): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win

##### Event trace

A board plays a whole feature while each `board.events` event prints to a log as it fires. Use it to see the order of the round before you hook your HUD and sounds onto it.

Live demo (hold-and-win-trace): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-trace

##### Sprite coins

The board built from TexturePacker sprites, with no Spine runtime. The numbers blur while they spin and each coin plays a 30-frame flip when it lands.

Live demo (hold-and-win-sprites): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-sprites

##### Spine coins

The board with production Spine coins. MINI and MAJOR tiers reveal on lock, plaques sit beside the grid, and the collect flies the coins into a counter.

Jackpot coins (MINI and MAJOR) are placed by the server only. Their weight is 0, so they never come up on a random strip.

Live demo (hold-and-win-spine): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-spine

#### Coin values

##### Value in the symbol class

A `ReelSymbol` written from scratch that draws a coin with a number on it. The value is read back off the landed symbol. Start here if you have not written a symbol class before.

Live demo (coin-value-symbol): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#coin-value-symbol

The same coin, with the number kept in `data` instead of the class. One generic coin then carries whatever value the server sends, and the number is painted from `coin:locked`.

Live demo (coin-value-data): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#coin-value-data

##### Number on existing art

When the coin art already exists as a sprite, keep it and add the number on top as a second child of the symbol's view.

Live demo (coin-value-overlay): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#coin-value-overlay

##### Coefficient values

Each coin carries a coefficient between x2 and x50 in `coin.data`. The board locks the hits and respins only the free cells. The total is summed from `board.lockedCoins`.

Live demo (value-coin-pin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#value-coin-pin

##### Count-up coin

Each coin's amount counts up from 0.00 to its value as it settles. The coins start in reading order, so the count runs across the board as a wave.

Live demo (hold-and-win-countup-coin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-countup-coin

##### Mystery value

Coins land blank. On lock, a strip of candidate amounts spins inside the coin face and slows down onto the real value.

Live demo (hold-and-win-mystery-coin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-mystery-coin

##### Upgrade in place

A held coin steps up the value ladder (5, 10, 25, 50, 100) with a flip and a pop. Nothing respins and no cell moves.

Live demo (hold-and-win-upgrade-coin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-upgrade-coin

##### Swap to a jackpot tier

`board.setSymbolAt(cell, id, data)` puts a different symbol in one cell and rewrites that cell's entry in the board's ledger. Here a coin turns into MINI, then MAJOR, and the neighbouring coins stay where they are.

Live demo (hold-and-win-tier-swap): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-tier-swap

##### Badge that survives a swap

An x100 badge is stored in `coin.data` and attached as a child of the symbol's view. Because it is rebuilt from the data, it comes back after an in-place swap and travels with the coin on a collect flight.

Live demo (hold-and-win-sticky-overlay): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-sticky-overlay

#### Collectors and special coins

#### Entering the feature

##### From the base game

A normal 5x3 spin that drops into the Hold & Win board when 3 BONUS symbols land, in the same chain, and switches back on `feature:end`.

Live demo (hold-and-win-base-to-feature): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-base-to-feature

##### Feature mode by middleware

This one does not use the board. It switches a plain `ReelSet` into a bonus mode at runtime by adding a frame middleware, and back by removing it, with no rebuild. In the bonus mode the middleware turns some visible cells into WILD.

Give your middleware a priority above 10, the priority of target placement, so it runs after the server's grid is placed and can react to it. The recipe uses 20.

Live demo (feature-mode-swap): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#feature-mode-swap

#### Pacing the wave

##### Last-cell anticipation

The `anticipateWhen` builder option slows the last spinning cell to a tension profile, for the moment when one more coin would fill the board.

Live demo (hold-and-win-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-anticipation

##### Skip

`board.skip()` puts each spinning cell at its landed position and fires `feature:skip`. `feature:end` is still the one event that says the feature is over.

Live demo (hold-and-win-skip): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-skip

##### Quicken

`board.skip({ mode: 'quicken' })` lands each spinning cell through its stop instead of placing it. The board's stagger lives in each cell's minimum spin time, so dropping it lands the whole wave together, and each cell still spins its symbol in and bounces. Add `speed: 'turbo'` to land the wave on the turbo profile, or call `HoldAndWinBuilder.skipMode('quicken')` to make quicken the default. `feature:skip` reports the count and the mode, and the landing events fire as usual.

Live demo (hold-and-win-quicken): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-quicken

##### One speed switch

`speeds(normal, turbo, superTurbo)` registers each profile in each cell's `SpeedManager`, and `board.setSpeed(name)` switches them all at once, the board's version of `reelSet.setSpeed()`. A wave already in flight finishes on its own profile, so a turbo press in the middle of a wave is `setSpeed` plus `skip()`. The landing wave steps by each profile's `stopDelay` (70, 25 and 0 ms here), so it tightens as the speed goes up and lands in one go on superTurbo, without a stagger function.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-speeds): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-speeds

##### One cell at a time

`board.reelAt(cell)` returns the cell's own 1x1 `ReelSet`. You can start it, slam-stop it and read the symbol in it without touching the other cells. Use this when a feature needs a cell to move outside the normal wave.

Live demo (hold-and-win-cell-control): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-cell-control

#### A clover game

These demos use the art of one real game, where the coins are clovers. Each clover is a Spine 4.2 skeleton.

##### Base game into the feature

A fruit base game. Gold clovers show bet-scaled money as they spin past, and the collect, multi, mystery and super clovers carry no amount. Three or more clovers on the stop hand their cells to the Hold & Win board.
