The feature on its own. Gold clovers lock with their amounts, the blank cells are the game's dark clover tile, and the 1 2 3 lamps below are the respin counter.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-bonus): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-bonus

##### Respin counter

Three lamps driven by `respins:changed` alone. Its `reason` says whether the count changed on seed, hit-reset or miss, so the lamps light or dim without the game working the count out again.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-respin-counter): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-respin-counter

##### Feature clovers

Clovers without an amount act on the held gold between waves. MULTI doubles each amount, MYSTERY becomes a gold clover with a revealed amount through `setSymbolAt`, and COLLECT adds the board up onto its own face.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-feature-clovers): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-feature-clovers

##### Lightning collect

Held clovers idle until the feature ends. When COLLECT locks, lightning strikes from it to each gold clover's number and the collect face counts the values into its own. The gold clovers keep their values, and the spent collector turns grey and stays held.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-collect): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-collect

##### Mystery jackpot capsule

The sealed capsule locks like a coin. Between waves the jackpot titles flick across its face through `setBadge` and stop on the tier the server sent. Then the plaque lights and the amount appears.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-mystery-capsule): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-mystery-capsule

#### Lock animation

##### Landing only

`lockAnimation('landing')` plays the landing settle on each lock and nothing more. `board.playWin()` is the single celebration, called when the game decides.

Live demo (hold-and-win-landing-only): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-landing-only

##### Per coin

`lockAnimation` can be a function of the coin that locked. Here gold clovers settle with their landing only and COLLECT also celebrates. The celebration waits for the skeleton's own landing beat (`symbol.landing`) instead of replacing its track, so the landing plays first and the win follows. The HUD prints when each one finishes.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-lock-rule): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-lock-rule

#### Board size and cell shape

##### Rectangular cells

Hold & Win art is usually wider than it is tall. `cellSize` takes a width and a height, plus a `columnGap` and a `rowGap`, so the board lays out to the art's own rectangle and the game's grid shows through the gaps. The clovers are the Spine 4.2 skeletons from the clover game, with idle, landing, win and blur tracks that the engine plays through `SpineReelSymbol`.

Live demo (hold-and-win-rect-cells): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-rect-cells

##### 5x5 board

The clover board with five rows, all cells live from the start.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-bonus-5x5): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-bonus-5x5

##### Growing board

Built 5x5 with the top and bottom rows inactive behind a purple sealed tile. Holding enough clovers opens a row with `board.activate()`, and the next respin spins it too.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-growing): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-growing

##### Background grid

Real gaps between the cells (`columnGap` and `rowGap`) and no cell chrome, so the background shows through. Behind the board is a gradient panel and one rounded frame per cell, drawn with plain `PIXI.Graphics` on each cell's exact bounds. A rounded cell mask cuts the tiles' corners to match.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-grid-bg): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-grid-bg

##### Rounded outer corners

Each cell has its own mask. `cellMask` takes a function that is called once per cell with its column, its row and the board size, and returns that cell's mask strategy. Here the cells clip to a plain rectangle, except the four corner cells, which each round their one outer corner through `RoundedRectMaskStrategy({ radius, corners })`. With no gap, the fifteen masks read as one rounded window with the panel's radius. The info argument also carries `corners`, that same per-cell object worked out for you.

Live demo (hold-and-win-outer-corners): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-outer-corners

##### Blur while spinning

Each skeleton has a blur animation that swaps its body to a motion-blur frame, and `SpineReelSymbol` plays it while the reel moves. The two rows are identical except that the second one opts out of the blur track.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-blur-strips): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-blur-strips

#### Travel direction

##### Sideways

The round on `.axis('horizontal')`. Each cell is its own 1x1 `ReelSet`, so the axis only decides which edge a coin scrolls in from. The board still lays out columns by rows, and a lock still claims one cell.

Don't build this on a plain `ReelSet` with `.orientation('horizontal')`. There a reel is a whole row, so the row moves as one strip across the gaps and past the cells that should be locked.

Live demo (hold-and-win-horizontal-lock): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-horizontal-lock

##### Upward

The round on `.axis('vertical', 'reverse')`. It also shows the hold that goes with it. `respin()` spins `board.freeCells` and nothing else, and `respin:start` reports which cells are in flight.

On a `ReelSet` the equivalent is `spin({ holdReels })`, which holds a whole reel. A board has no `holdReels` because Hold & Win holds single cells.

Live demo (hold-and-win-reverse-respin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-reverse-respin

#### Draw order and dimming

##### Cell draw order

Each cell is its own reel set, so the clovers the engine lifts above the cells at rest share one layer, drawn in attach order. That order is column by column, which lets the next column's clover cover a lower clover's glow. `cellZIndex` sorts the layer by whatever the board returns, here lower rows in front and the capsule above everything, and the board asks again on each place and landing.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-cell-order): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-cell-order

##### Lift one cell

`cellZIndex` is the order at rest, and the board asks for it again on each place and landing. A clover that must stay on top while it upgrades can't get there by returning a bigger number, because the next landing overwrites it during the animation. `board.lift(cell)` raises the cell on a separate channel and returns a release function. The refresh keeps running underneath without touching the lifted cell, and the release puts the cell back without recomputing anything.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-lift): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-lift

##### Lift and dim

`board.dim({ except })` goes with `lift()`. The dim draws above the clovers and below anything lifted, so a lifted cell stays in front of it whether or not it is in `except`. A dim covers cells, not symbol ids, so this collect works out which cells hold the gold clovers it is about to sweep and spares them. The money stays bright and the blanks go dark. The dim fades in and out over `fade` ms off the board's own ticker, and `fade: 0` cuts.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-lift-dim): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-lift-dim

##### Dim the cell or the art

There are two ways to push a board back. `dim()` lays a rectangle over each cell, so the clover goes dark along with the tile it sits in. `dimSymbols()` tints each symbol towards black instead, so the art sinks and the board stays lit. The same sweep runs twice in the demo, once with each. `amount` sets the strength on both, and both fade over `fade`.

This is a board method rather than a few lines of `gsap.to` because a dimmed cell that swaps its symbol has to keep its dim, and the symbol that left has to lose its tint before the pool gives it to another cell.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-dim-symbols): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-dim-symbols

##### Dimming one cell up close

One cell, scaled up, holding a fruit instead of a clover so the cell's background shows all around the symbol. The blue plate is drawn by `cellChrome()` on the board, not by a symbol, so `dimSymbols()` never touches it. `amount` steps through 0.3, 0.6 and 0.9 and the plate stays the same. Then the same 0.6 through `dim()` takes the whole cell down.

In the last step the cell is swapped to the empty id. There is no art left to dim, so `dimSymbols()` changes nothing, neither the symbol that has gone nor the plate.

Watch for this on a real board. If your blank tile is a registered symbol, as the dark tile is in the clover demos (the `empty` id), it is art and `dimSymbols()` dims it too. Draw anything that must stay lit in `cellChrome()`, or name its cell in `except`.

Live demo (hold-and-win-clover-dim-one-cell): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/hold-and-win/#hold-and-win-clover-dim-one-cell

### Infinity reels
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/infinity-reels/
The board gains reels on the right after the spin lands, as many as the result asks for.
Tags: expand, addReels, removeReels, addRows, multiways, ways, big-symbols, skip, win-lines

In an infinity reels slot the base spin lands, and while the win keeps going
the board grows sideways, a reel at a time, for as long as the server's
result says. In pixi-reels that is one call per round, `expand()`.

#### The server's result

The server decides the base board and every reel the board grows by, in
order. Each reel is one `ColumnTarget`, the same shape `setResult()` takes.

```ts
interface InfinityResult {
  base: ColumnTarget[];  // one per reel the builder made
  extra: ColumnTarget[]; // the reels the board grows by, in order; often none
}
```

#### Spin the base, then expand

```ts
const spin = reelSet.spin();
const res = await server.spin();
reelSet.setResult(res.base);
await spin;

await reelSet.expand({
  columns: res.extra,
  step: 1, // reels added and spun per step
  onStepAdded: () => camera.panTo(reelSet.viewport.maskWidth), // the board's new width
  onStepLanded: (step) => showWin(step.result.symbols),        // the whole board so far
});
```

Each step adds its reels, spins only those while every earlier reel is held,
and lands them on their columns. The call awaits your hooks, so a camera pan
or a win readout finishes before the next step. It validates every column
before the first reel is added, so a bad result throws before the board
changes.

#### Shrink back next round

```ts
reelSet.removeReels(); // back to the reels the builder made; a no-op when the board did not grow
```

#### Growing rows

`addRows(count, { cells })` makes every reel `count` rows taller at its own
cell size, and the viewport and mask grow with it. The `cells` option is what
the new rows show, one array per reel, from the server. Inside an expansion,
grow the rows between steps in `onStepLanded`. The reels after that arrive at
the new height. `removeRows()` goes back to the rows the builder made.

```ts
await reelSet.expand({
  columns: res.extra, // a column may be taller than the board once a row unlocks
  onStepLanded: (step) => {
    const row = res.rows[step.index]; // the server's cells for an unlocked row, or nothing
    if (row) reelSet.addRows(1, { cells: row });
  },
});
// next round
reelSet.removeReels();
reelSet.removeRows();
```

On MultiWays the rows are each reel's shape. The length of a column's
`visible` array is that reel's cell count, inside the fixed reel height.

#### Stacked symbols that split

Some infinity slots land a symbol stacked two to four cells tall. When it
wins, the stack splits into more single symbols than it had cells, and its
reel grows past the frame. A stack is a big symbol one reel wide, and the
server says what it splits into.

```ts
// .symbolData({ Q3: { weight: 0, size: { reels: 1, cells: 3 } } })
const { from, count } = reelSet.splitSymbol(reel, cell, res.split); // e.g. six 'Q's
```

The reel grows by the difference. The cells above and below keep their
symbols, and the board re-centres around the taller reel. Keep the other
reels still on screen while your camera eases out, or they jump. Split at
rest, or between steps in `onStepLanded`. Next round, `resetColumns()` puts
every reel back.

Any symbol one reel wide can split, a 1x1 too. To keep the reel's height
instead, with its cells shrinking to share it, pass `{ height: 'keep' }`.
That is the default on MultiWays, where a reel's height is fixed. For any
other change to one reel, `setColumn` shows a column of any length. The
[split symbols page](/mechanics/split-symbols/) compares the two modes and
has a demo where you tap to split and a demo of splits on MultiWays.

#### Counting and drawing ways

The library computes no wins (ADR 007). The server does. The library helps
you show them in two ways.

The board's ways is the product of the reels' row counts:

```ts
const ways = reelSet.reels.reduce((ways, reel) => ways * reel.visibleCells, 1);
```

Eight reels of three rows is 6,561 ways. Eight MultiWays reels of seven is
5,764,801.

`WinLines` in `pixi-reels/debug` draws a payway as a lattice: every winning
cell joined to every winning cell on the next reel. A win of millions of ways
is still a few dozen segments. It draws the cells you pass it.

```ts
import { WinLines } from 'pixi-reels/debug';

const lines = new WinLines(reelSet);
lines.ways(win.perReel); // winning cell indices per reel, from your server: [[0, 2], [1], [0, 1, 2]]
reelSet.events.on('spin:start', () => lines.clear());
```

The demos on this site use `evaluateWays()` and `countWays()` from
`@pixi-reels/kit/ways` in place of a server. Copy them if you want the same
left-to-right ways math in a prototype.

#### Skip

The steps count as one round. The first `skipSpin()` lands the step in flight
and speeds up the rest. In standard mode they run on the fastest profile, and
in cascade mode every later step lands at once. A press between steps, while
a hook runs, carries over to the next step. To land everything still to come
at once, abort the expansion's `signal`.

An aborted expansion lands the remaining reels in one step, at the height the
board has at that moment. If your rows grow during the expansion, slam each
step instead of aborting.

#### Events

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `expand:start` | The chain starts: the board grows from `from` reels to `to`. |
| `reels:added` | A step's reels are on the board. Move the camera here or in `onStepAdded`. |
| `expand:stepAdded` / `expand:stepLanded` | A step's reels arrived or landed, before its hooks. |
| `rows:added` / `rows:removed` | `addRows()` or `removeRows()` changed every reel's height. |
| `column:set` | One reel changed its cells: `setColumn()`, `splitSymbol()` or `resetColumns()`. |
| `expand:complete` | Every step landed. Carries the final board. |
| `expand:end` | Always last, with `'complete'` or `'failed'`. Put the UI back here. |

Each step also fires the usual `spin:*` events. `reelSet.isExpanding` tells
them apart from a new round.

##### Demos

The base spin lands, and then the board grows. `reelSet.expand({ columns })` adds the reels the server's result has beyond the base board, a step at a time, and spins only the new reels while the earlier ones hold. `addReels()` and `removeReels()` are the calls underneath it, and the next round shrinks the board back with `removeReels()`. The [infinity reels guide](/mechanics/infinity-reels/#concept) has the short version: what the server sends, the calls, and the events.

The first demo is the plain mechanic. The next ones change the board's shape during the expansion, and the last covers skipping.

#### Add one reel per step

While the win still reaches the last reel, the server adds another reel to its result. Each step pans the camera to the new reel in `onStepAdded`, spins and lands it, then counts the ways and draws them with `WinLines` in `onStepLanded`.

The steps count as one round for skipping. The first press slams the step in flight and switches the rest to turbo, the same boost `skipSpin()` gives the rest of any round. In cascade mode the later steps land at once instead, the way one press ends a cascade. The second press aborts the expansion's `signal`, which lands every reel still to come in one step.

Live demo (infinity-reels): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels

#### Board shape

##### Add rows

A wild on a new reel unlocks a row. `addRows(1, { cells })` in `onStepLanded` makes every reel one cell taller, with the server's cells for the new row, and the reels after it arrive at the new height. The camera zooms out to fit, reading the board's size from `viewport.maskWidth` and `maskHeight`. The next round goes back with `removeReels()` and `removeRows()`.

Rows change only between steps. Inside `onStepAdded` the step's reels are about to spin on columns sized for the board's old height, so `addRows()` throws there. A fast-forward, which aborts the `signal`, lands every remaining reel in one step at the board's height at that moment. That is why this demo's skip slams one step at a time instead.

Live demo (infinity-reels-rows): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-rows

##### MultiWays

The length of each column's `visible` array is that reel's cell count, applied with `setShape()` for its step, so every reel the expansion adds multiplies the ways. Eight reels of seven cells give 5,764,801 ways, and ten give 282,475,249. Each step here adds two reels (`step: 2`).

Live demo (infinity-reels-multiways): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-multiways

##### Big symbols

The steps add one reel each, but a 2x2 wild arrives in one of the columns. A step of one reel cannot land half a block, so that step adds two reels and the block lands whole. The step plan is read from the `symbolData` sizes, and every block is validated before the first reel is added.

A block has to end on a reel the expansion adds. A block that would run past the last of them, or past the bottom of a strip, throws before any reel is added.

Live demo (infinity-reels-big-symbol): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-big-symbol

##### Split stacked symbols

Q lands either one cell tall or stacked two to four cells tall. When Q wins on every reel, each stack splits into more single Qs than it had cells, and its reel grows past the frame in both directions. `reelSet.splitSymbol(reel, cell, ids)` places the server's split: the stack covering `(reel, cell)` becomes `ids`, one per cell, the cells above and below keep their symbols, and the board re-centres around the taller reel. While the win reaches the last reel, `expand()` adds another reel and the multiplier goes up by one. The next round goes back with `removeReels()` and `resetColumns()`. The [Split symbols](/mechanics/split-symbols/) page has a reel that keeps its height, splits on MultiWays and a playground where you tap to split.

Because the board re-centres around the taller reel, hold the other reels still on screen and let the camera ease out, or they jump. This demo moves its camera by the amount they shift.

Live demo (infinity-reels-split): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-split

#### Skipping steps

Press as often as you like and read the log. The base board is grouped, shown by the dashed boxes, so a press lands one group. Each step's reel teases "will the win continue?" with `anticipation: { protect: 'once' }`, so the first press during a tease is spent and the next one lands the reel. A press while the camera pans is queued for the next step. The button calls `skipSpin()` and nothing else.

Live demo (infinity-reels-skip): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-skip

##### Skip policies

- Turbo for the rest, the default. The first `skipSpin()` frees the step in flight and moves every later step to the fastest profile. The next round starts at normal speed again.
- Slam each step. Every press frees the step in flight. Presses made during `onStepAdded` or `onStepLanded`, for example while the camera pans or a win readout shows, are kept and free the next step as soon as it has its result.
- Fast-forward. Abort the expansion's `signal` and every reel still to come lands in one step. A quick-spin or autoplay mode can pass a signal that is already aborted, so the whole expansion lands at once, with the same events and hooks.
- Quicken. With `.skipMode('quicken')`, or `requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken', speed: 'turbo' })`, a press shortens the step's spin but keeps its spin-out and bounce, so a long chain never looks cut.
- One reel per press on wide steps. A step's reels arrive as one group. Call `setReelGroups()` in `onStepAdded` to split them so each press frees one, or use `slamStop({ reels: [...] })` to land part of a step and let the rest play.
- Keep the deciding tease. `anticipation: (step) => stillWinning ? { protect: 'once', duration: 900 } : false` keeps the "will it continue?" tease through the first press, only on the steps where it matters.

`slamStop()` between steps has nothing to land, and a press after the last step has no step left, so both do nothing. A named `setDropOrder('ltr' | 'rtl' | 'all')` follows the reels that spin, so it covers the added reels and orders a step by position. A sticky `setStopDelays()` array covers only the reels it was given, and reels past its end stop with no delay.

#### What carries across steps

- Events. Each step fires the usual `spin:*` events for its own reels, plus `reels:added`, `expand:stepAdded` and `expand:stepLanded`, and `rows:added` when a hook adds rows. The chain opens with `expand:start` and closes with `expand:complete` and then `expand:end`, which carries `'complete'`, or `'failed'` when the chain threw. `reelSet.isExpanding` is `true` in between, so a `spin:start` listener can tell a step from a new round.
- Stagger. Start and stop delays count a reel's position in its step, not its index, so reel 40 does not wait forty delays.
- Pins. A sticky pin's turns and an `'eval'` pin belong to the round, so a step does not use them up.
- Memory. Added reels are real reels while they are on the board. `removeReels()` destroys them and shrinks the viewport, mask and symbol pool back.

### Layers
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/layers/
Draw a symbol over its neighbours or outside the reel frame, and build your own board out of the same cells.
Tags: layering, zindex, unmask, spotlight, board

Every symbol lives inside its reel, and every reel sits under the viewport
mask. That works until a symbol's art is bigger than its cell, such as a
scatter with a glow, a wild with a crown, or a winning symbol that should
rise above the rest.

There are three ways out, from smallest to largest. A `zIndex` in the
symbol's data draws it above the other symbols in the same reel. Unmasking
moves it to the layer above every reel and above the mask, so it can spill
past the frame. Promoting raises one instance for as long as a win shows,
then puts it back.

`BoardGrid`, in the last demo, is the same cell layout without the reels: a
grid you fill and animate yourself.

##### Demos

The demos go from the smallest change to the largest: a `zIndex` inside one reel, unmasking above every reel, and raising one symbol while a win shows. The last demo builds a board out of cells with no reels.

#### Within one reel

A `zIndex` in `symbolData` draws the scatter above the other symbols in its reel, so its art is never covered by the cell below. The mystery bush keeps the default layer, and the cell below it draws over its leaves. This orders symbols within the reel only. Art that reaches over the next reel or past the frame needs `unmask`.

Live demo (layering-scatter-zindex): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/layers/#symbol-layering-zindex-unmask-promote

#### Above every reel

##### Unmasked symbols

`unmask: true` in `symbolData` moves a landed symbol into the viewport's `unmaskedContainer`, above every reel and outside the mask. The scatter's art now spills past the grid edge and over the reel to its right, with no code in the demo. It works on jagged boards with centred reels too.

Live demo (layering-unmask): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/layers/#symbol-layering-zindex-unmask-promote

##### Buffer cells stay masked

Only visible cells are unmasked. The same id in a buffer cell stays under the mask, so oversized art never hangs into the window from a cell the player should not see. The demo lands both at once and holds through a skip.

Live demo (unmask-stays-in-the-grid): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/layers/#symbol-layering-zindex-unmask-promote

##### Your own draw order

The engine orders symbols by type first: `symbolData.zIndex * 100` plus the cell's stacking index. Some art specs order by row first: within a grade the lower row is in front, then the reel to the right, and only then a higher grade. Pass that rule to `symbolZIndex(resolver)` and the engine applies it after every wrap, swap and landing.

Every mid and high symbol here is unmasked, so at rest they share one container and the resolver orders them against each other. While the reels move the resolver returns `ctx.defaultZIndex`, so the spin looks as it did before.

Live demo (layering-graded-zindex): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/layers/#layering-graded-zindex

#### One symbol at a time

##### With promote

`reelSet.promote(positions)` raises the symbols at those positions above the mask and above their neighbours, and returns a function that drops them again. It attaches the views to a render layer instead of reparenting them, so nothing moves and nothing has to be put back. Unlike `spotlight.show()` it does not dim, does not call `playWin()` and has nothing to await, so the game's own animation stays in control.

The same tween runs twice in the demo, once clipped and once promoted. Watch the top row swell past the grid edge.

Live demo (clover-promote-win-line): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/layers/#clover-promote-win-line

##### By hand

The older way to do the same thing. Each landed scatter's view is moved into `viewport.spotlightContainer`, the layer the win spotlight uses, and handed back to its reel on the next `spin:start`. The recipe stores each view's parent and position and restores them before the strip moves. Like `promote`, it raises one landed cell without making its id unmasked everywhere.

Live demo (layering-promote-jagged): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/layers/#clover-promote-win-line

#### Your own board

`BoardGrid` is a grid of cells that each spin on their own. Hold & Win is built on it. This demo uses it directly for a reveal and collect prize grid: every cell spins to a prize, the values add up and the top cell is highlighted. There is no locking and no respin, because those are Hold & Win's rules and this board has its own.

Live demo (board-grid-reveal): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/layers/#board-primitive-build-your-own-board

### Reel windows
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/masks/
Show the reels through a rounded window, a card per reel or any shape you draw.
Tags: mask, rounded, silhouette, pyramid, jagged, frame

The viewport clips the reels through a `MaskStrategy`, so buffer cells never
show past the grid. The default is `RectMaskStrategy`, and the strategies
below are options you add on top.

| Board | Strategy |
|---|---|
| Square frame art | `RectMaskStrategy` (default) |
| Rounded frame, reels flush | `RoundedRectMaskStrategy` (`scope: 'set'`) |
| Reels as separate cards, with a cross gap | `RoundedRectMaskStrategy` (`scope: 'reel'`) |
| Rounded frame, one rect per reel, any gap | `RoundedRectMaskStrategy` (`scope: 'outer'`) |
| Hold & Win board, a mask per cell | `cellMask((cell, { corners }) => ...)` |
| Pyramid or MultiWays, rounded, reels flush | `SilhouetteMaskStrategy` |
| Hexes, holes, cut-outs | `PathMaskStrategy` |

`inset(strategy, px)` shrinks any of them by a margin, and
`composeMasks(a, b, ...)` joins several, your own strategies included.

#### Writing your own

Implement `build(ctx)` and `update(g, ctx)`, set
`version = MASK_STRATEGY_VERSION`, and pass it to `.maskStrategy(...)`. Try
`PathMaskStrategy` first. A class is only worth it when it keeps state
between draws.

Two things to respect. `ctx.axis` matters because `rects` are in screen
space in every orientation (`axis.toLocal(w, h)` gives `{ cross, main }`).
`ctx.bleed` inflates the cross axis only. Add the optional `draw(g, ctx)`
and your strategy composes like the built-in ones.

##### Demos

Each demo passes a mask strategy to `.maskStrategy(...)`. Rounded windows come first, then the helpers that trim or combine a mask, then a mask drawn from your own path.

#### Rounded corners

##### The whole window

`RoundedRectMaskStrategy` with `scope: 'set'` rounds the corners of the box around all the reels. It works at any cross gap, which is why it is the default scope.

Live demo (mask-rounded-set): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/masks/#a-rounded-window

##### Each reel as a card

`scope: 'reel'` rounds every reel's box instead, so the reels read as separate cards.

It needs a cross gap above `0`. At gap `0` neighbouring reels share an edge, and rounding both sides of it cuts a notch into every seam. The strategy warns once when it sees touching reels.

Live demo (mask-rounded-reels): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/masks/#each-reel-as-its-own-card

##### Outer corners only

`scope: 'outer'` keeps one rect per reel, as the default mask does, so buffer cells past a short reel stay hidden. It rounds a corner only where it is also a corner of the box around all the reels: the outer pair on the first reel and on the last. The inner edges stay square, so it works at cross gap `0`, where `scope: 'reel'` notches. `corners: { topLeft: true, ... }` limits any scope to the named screen corners.

On a jagged set the corners of the box may not touch any reel, and then nothing is rounded. Use `SilhouetteMaskStrategy` there.

Live demo (mask-outer-corners): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/masks/#one-rect-per-reel-the-windows-corners-only

##### Jagged boards

A pyramid has no single rectangle to round. Rounding each reel notches the seams, and rounding the bounding box hides the staircase and shows buffer cells past the short reels. `SilhouetteMaskStrategy` follows the outline of all the reels together and rounds every corner of it. The inward corners, where a short reel meets a taller one, use `concaveRadius`. On a board with no steps it gives a plain rounded rect.

The reels must touch, at cross gap `0`. With a gap the strategy warns and falls back to a rounded rect per reel.

Live demo (mask-silhouette-pyramid): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/masks/#rounding-a-jagged-board

##### Hold & Win cells

Every Hold & Win cell is its own 1x1 reel set with its own mask. `cellMask` on the Hold & Win builder takes a function that is called once per cell with `{ reel, cell }` (column and row) and `{ cols, rows, corners }`, and returns that cell's strategy. Here every cell gets a plain rect except the four corner cells, which each round their one outer corner, so the gapless board clips as one rounded window made of fifteen masks. `corners` is the cell's corner set already worked out, for the short form `(_, { corners }) => new RoundedRectMaskStrategy({ radius, corners })`.

Live demo (hold-and-win-outer-corners): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/masks/#a-mask-per-hold--win-cell-from-its-row-and-column

#### Trimming and combining

##### Inset and compose

`inset(strategy, px)` shrinks what any strategy draws by `px` on every side, and a negative value grows it. Use it when the art shows a pixel past the frame. `composeMasks(a, b, ...)` joins several strategies into the viewport's one mask. Here a rounded window inset by 4px is joined with a banner strip above the reels.

`composeMasks` can only form a union, because a `Graphics` mask is the union of its filled shapes. To subtract, use `.cut()` inside a `PathMaskStrategy`.

Live demo (mask-inset-compose): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/masks/#insetting-and-composing

##### A different trim per side

Frame art rarely has four equal lips. `inset(strategy, { top, right, bottom, left })` trims each side by its own amount, for example `inset(new RoundedRectMaskStrategy({ radius: 43 }), { top: 4, bottom: 12 })`. Sides are screen sides in every orientation, and a side you leave out is not trimmed. Here the bottom lip is four times thicker than the top one.

Live demo (mask-inset-sides): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/masks/#mask-inset-sides

#### Any shape

`PathMaskStrategy` takes a `(graphics, context) => void` callback. The context carries `rects`, `width`, `height`, `axis` and `bleed`. Do not call `g.clear()`, because the strategy already has. The demo fills the board and cuts a hole in the middle, so only the outer ring of symbols shows.

`cut()` subtracts from the last shape filled, so fill first. If you draw the hole before filling, the mask is empty and the board disappears, with no error.

Live demo (mask-path-custom): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/masks/#any-shape-without-a-class

### Nudge
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/
Push a reel that has already stopped up or down a few places to pull a symbol into view.
Tags: nudge, stagger, spotlight, big-symbols, abort, skip, horizontal, reverse, orientation

A nudge moves one reel a few cells after it has landed, and brings in symbols
you choose. The classic use is a near-miss: the reels land one symbol short,
then one reel nudges by one cell to reveal the symbol that was missing.

```ts
await reelSet.spin();

await reelSet.nudge(2, {
  distance: 1,
  direction: 'forward',
  incoming: ['wild'],
});
```

Reel 2 moves one cell. Everything on it shifts along, the last symbol leaves
the window, and the wild arrives at the front.

Live demo (nudge): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/

#### The contract

```ts
interface NudgeOptions {
  /**
   * Number of full positions to shift. Positive integer, strictly less than
   * the reel's total strip capacity (bufferStart + visibleCells + bufferEnd).
   */
  distance: number;
  /**
   *  - 'forward': the way this reel travels; new symbols enter at its
   *    feed edge.
   *  - 'reverse': the other way; new symbols enter at the opposite edge.
   *
   * Relative to the reel, not the screen. On a reel built with
   * direction('reverse'), 'forward' nudges upward.
   */
  direction: 'forward' | 'reverse';
  /**
   * Symbol ids in top-down order of their final on-strip position,
   * including any overflow into the off-screen buffer. Length must equal
   * `distance` exactly.
   */
  incoming: string[];
  /** Tween duration in ms. Default: `200 * distance`. */
  duration?: number;
  /** GSAP ease name. Default: `'power2.out'` (smooth deceleration, no overshoot). */
  ease?: string;
  /** Delay before the tween begins (ms). Sugar for staggered Promise.all. */
  startDelay?: number;
  /** Abort the nudge mid-flight. Strip still snaps to landed position. */
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}

reelSet.nudge(reel: number, options: NudgeOptions): Promise<{ symbols: string[] }>;
reelSet.skipNudge(reel?: number): void;
```

The promise resolves with the reel's new visible cells, in order, which you
can feed straight into win detection. It rejects with an `AbortError` if the
signal aborts or the set is destroyed mid-tween.

#### How `incoming` lays out

For a 3-cell reel landed on `['A', 'B', 'C']` (first, middle, last):

| Call | New visible (first to last) |
| --- | --- |
| `nudge(r, { distance: 1, direction: 'forward', incoming: ['X'] })` | `['X', 'A', 'B']` |
| `nudge(r, { distance: 2, direction: 'forward', incoming: ['X', 'Y'] })` | `['X', 'Y', 'A']` |
| `nudge(r, { distance: 1, direction: 'reverse', incoming: ['X'] })` | `['B', 'C', 'X']` |
| `nudge(r, { distance: 2, direction: 'reverse', incoming: ['X', 'Y'] })` | `['C', 'X', 'Y']` |

The first entry always ends up nearest the start of the reel and the last
entry nearest the end.

A nudge further than the visible cell count pushes the overflow into the
buffer on the matching side. With `'forward'`, the trailing entries spill into
the buffer at the exit edge. With `'reverse'`, the leading entries spill into
the other one. Nothing is thrown away. Every entry stays on the strip, ready
for a follow-up nudge or the next spin's opening frame.

A distance equal to or larger than the strip capacity throws, because a full
rotation would silently overwrite a pre-placed buffer entry.

#### Sequential or parallel

One nudge moves one reel. When several reels nudge, you choose how to start
them. The engine output is the same either way; only the pacing differs.

##### Sequential

Live demo (nudge-sequential): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#sequential-three-separate-beats

```ts
for (const reel of [1, 2, 3]) {
  await reelSet.nudge(reel, { distance: 1, direction: 'forward', incoming: ['wild'], duration: 480 });
}
```

Each `await` waits for that reel to land, so the player sees reel 1's wild
before reel 2 starts. The total time is the number of reels times the
duration.

##### Parallel

Live demo (nudge-parallel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#parallel-one-synchronised-beat

```ts
await Promise.all(
  [1, 2, 3].map((reel) =>
    reelSet.nudge(reel, { distance: 1, direction: 'forward', incoming: ['wild'], duration: 480 }),
  ),
);
```

All the tweens start on the same frame and the whole line arrives together.
The total time is one duration, however many reels.

##### Stagger

The `startDelay` option gives you a wave without a loop:

```ts
await Promise.all(
  [1, 2, 3].map((reel, i) =>
    reelSet.nudge(reel, { ...opts, startDelay: i * 80 }),
  ),
);
```

The tweens start at 0, 80 and 160 ms and run concurrently. Validation still
throws synchronously at the call site. Only the movement is delayed.

#### Big symbols on the reel

A tall block moves as one piece, as long as the whole block is still on the
strip afterwards:

| Direction | Survival condition |
| --- | --- |
| `'forward'` | `anchorStripIdx + h - 1 + distance < total` |
| `'reverse'`   | `anchorStripIdx - distance >= 0` |

Here `total` is the strip capacity (buffer start plus visible cells plus
buffer end) and `anchorStripIdx` counts from 0 at the outermost start-buffer
cell, so the index of visible cell 0 equals the buffer start count.

A block may sit partly in a buffer and still render correctly. The engine
sizes the anchor to span the whole block wherever it lives, and the mask clips
the rest. This is how a tail reveal works: land a tall wild with its anchor in the
buffer, nudge, and the rest of it moves into view.

A block wider than one reel always throws. Nudging one reel would tear the
block off its cells on the next one.

```ts
// A 1x2 wild sits at visible cell 1 with its tail in bufferEnd.
// Nudge back by 1 and the whole block lands at cells 0 and 1.
await reelSet.nudge(2, { distance: 1, direction: 'reverse', incoming: ['filler'] });
```

#### Skip and abort

There are two ways to cut a nudge short.

```ts
// 1. Skip: fast-forward to landed. The promise resolves normally.
const p = reelSet.nudge(2, { ...opts });
button.onclick = () => reelSet.skipNudge(2);
const { symbols } = await p;
```

```ts
// 2. Abort: reject with AbortError. The strip still snaps to landed.
const controller = new AbortController();
const p = reelSet.nudge(2, { ...opts, signal: controller.signal });
button.onclick = () => controller.abort();
try { await p; }
catch (e) { if (e.name !== 'AbortError') throw e; }
```

The difference is what happens to the promise. `skipNudge` resolves it, so
your success path runs. An abort rejects it and fires `nudge:cancelled`, so
your error path runs. Skip when the win plays next, and abort when you are
tearing the feature down.

Either way the strip lands where it was going to land. A nudge never stops
half-tweened.

#### Events

| Event | Payload | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nudge:start` | `({ reelIndex, distance, direction })` | Pre-placement is done and the tween is about to begin. |
| `nudge:complete` | `({ reelIndex, distance, direction, symbols })` | The strip snapped to the post-nudge grid. `symbols` is the new visible column. |
| `nudge:cancelled` | `({ reelIndex, distance, direction, reason })` | The signal aborted or the reel was destroyed mid-tween. Never fires together with `nudge:complete`; the promise rejected instead. |
| `phase:enter` (per reel) | `('nudge')` | Mirror of `nudge:start`, on the affected reel's bus. |
| `phase:exit` (per reel) | `('nudge')` | Mirror of `nudge:complete`. |

The per-reel `landed` event does not fire on a nudge. It belongs to the spin
pipeline. Listen to `nudge:complete` instead.

```ts
reelSet.events.on('nudge:complete', ({ reelIndex, symbols }) => {
  console.log(`reel ${reelIndex} now reads`, symbols);
  // Re-run win detection on reelSet.getVisibleGrid() here.
});
```

#### When `nudge()` throws or rejects

Bad arguments throw at the call. Cancellation rejects later.

It throws synchronously when:

- The reel set is spinning, refilling, or in a cascade.
- `reel` is out of range.
- The target reel has an active pin. Call `unpin` first.
- `distance` is below 1, not an integer, or at least the strip capacity.
- `direction` is neither `'forward'` nor `'reverse'`.
- The length of `incoming` differs from `distance`.
- An incoming id is not registered, or is a big symbol.
- A block on the target reel would not survive the rotation.
- A cell on the target reel belongs to a block wider than one reel.

It rejects with an `AbortError` when:

- The signal aborts before or during the tween.
- `reelSet.destroy()` is called mid-tween.

A nudge touches one reel. The other reels, their pins and any spotlight are
left alone.

#### Recipes

- [Single nudge](/mechanics/nudge/), the smallest demo.
- [Spotlight after a nudge](/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-spotlight), a nudge that completes a line, then the win.
- [Big symbols](/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-big-symbol), the block survival rule and the tail reveal.
- [Land a big symbol partially in buffer](/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbol-partial-land), land with the tail showing, then nudge to reveal it.
- [Nudge a big symbol in, then hold it across a respin](/mechanics/big-symbols/#big-symbol-held-respin), reveal a buffer-anchored wild, then hold the reel while the others respin.

##### Demos

Each demo shifts a reel that has already landed by a few positions and brings in symbols you choose. The first one is a single nudge. The rest cover nudging several reels, presenting the win, big symbols, other reel directions and cutting a nudge short.

#### Single nudge

After the reels land, reel 1 nudges `'forward'` by one and a wild enters at the top, then reel 3 nudges `'reverse'` by one and a wild enters at the bottom. `incoming` lists the symbols in their final order on the strip, top to bottom on a vertical set.

Live demo (nudge): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-a-reel

#### Several reels

The same row of wilds nudged into reels 1 to 3 in three ways. The engine output is the same each time; only the pacing changes.

##### One after another

Each `await` waits for the previous reel to land, so the player sees three separate reveals. The total time is the number of reels times the duration.

Live demo (nudge-sequential): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-several-reels

##### All at once

`Promise.all` starts every tween on the same frame and the wilds arrive together. The total time is one duration.

Live demo (nudge-parallel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-several-reels

##### Staggered

`Promise.all` with a per-reel `startDelay`. The tweens run at the same time but start one after another, so the wilds arrive in a wave. Bad arguments still throw at the call; only the movement waits.

Live demo (nudge-stagger): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#staggered-nudge-wave-reveal

#### Spotlight after a nudge

The reels land one wild short of a line. Three reels nudge in parallel to complete it, then `SymbolSpotlight` presents the new winning cells.

Live demo (nudge-spotlight): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-spotlight

#### Big symbols

A 1xH block on the target reel moves as one piece. In the first demo a 1x2 wild nudges down by two, so its lower half moves into the buffer below the window, then up by one into full view. In the second the block nudges up so only its lower half shows, then back down into full view.

Only blocks one reel wide (`size.reels === 1`) can be nudged. A block that spans reels throws.

Live demo (nudge-big-symbol): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-through-a-big-symbol
Live demo (nudge-tail-reveal): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-through-a-big-symbol

#### Other reel directions

`direction` is relative to the reel's own axis, so the nudge code is the same on any set. What changes is where on screen the new symbol enters.

##### Horizontal set

On `.orientation('horizontal')` a reel is a screen row, so a nudge shifts it sideways. One press nudges row 0 `'forward'`, where a wild enters at the left edge, and row 2 `'reverse'`, where a wild enters at the right. `incoming` reads left to right here.

Live demo (nudge-horizontal): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-a-horizontal-set

##### Reels that spin up

Two wilds land on the middle line and the third stops one cell below it. On a `.direction('reverse')` reel a `'forward'` nudge travels upward, so the incoming symbol enters at the bottom cell and the wild rolls onto the line, which then lights up.

Live demo (nudge-reverse-rollup): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-on-a-roll-up-set

#### Cutting a nudge short

Both ways end with the strip where the nudge was going. They differ in what the promise does.

##### Skip

`reelSet.skipNudge(reel)` jumps a running nudge to its end. `nudge()` resolves as usual, so the success path still runs. Use it when the win plays next.

Live demo (nudge-skip): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#skip-an-in-flight-nudge

##### Abort

Abort through `NudgeOptions.signal`. The strip still snaps to its landed position, but `nudge()` rejects with `AbortError` and `nudge:cancelled` fires. Use it when you are tearing the feature down.

Live demo (nudge-abort): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/nudge/#abort-a-nudge

### Sideways and upward reels
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/
Reels that run sideways or upward, for banners and portrait layouts. The art stays upright.
Tags: horizontal, orientation, direction, reverse, roll-up, banner, ways, axis

A reel can travel down, up, or sideways. Two builder settings control that,
and they do not affect each other:

```ts
new ReelSetBuilder()
  .orientation('horizontal')   // which screen axis the strip travels along
  .direction('reverse')        // which way along it symbols move
```

That gives four combinations. The engine is written against the reel's
axis instead of against `y`, so anticipation, cascades, the spotlight, pins,
big symbols, pyramids and MultiWays work the same in all four.

| | `direction('forward')` | `direction('reverse')` |
|---|---|---|
| `orientation('vertical')` | symbols fall (the default) | symbols rise, a roll-up |
| `orientation('horizontal')` | symbols move right | symbols move left, a sideways banner |

#### Four separate concepts

The engine keeps these four apart:

- Orientation: which screen axis the strip runs on. Set for the whole set at
  build time.
- Direction: which way along that axis symbols travel. Per reel.
- Gravity: which way cascade symbols fall. By default it follows the reel's
  direction. `tumble({ gravity })` can pin it to `'forward'` or `'reverse'`
  so a reel spins one way and drops the other.
- Facing: which way is up for the art. Never touched by the other three.

Travel never changes facing. A reel can spin sideways and its art stays
upright. The engine never rotates a container to fake an axis, because that
would break sprite anchors, flip filters and draw third-party symbols on
their side. A test checks for zero rotation and unit scale on every symbol
in all four combinations, at rest, mid-spin and landed.

#### Main and cross

The main axis is the one the strip travels along: `y` when vertical, `x`
when horizontal. The cross axis is the other one, along which the reels are
laid out. On a vertical set the reels sit side by side across `x` and cells
scroll down `y`. On a horizontal set it is the opposite.

`Reel` exposes both for code that must not care which is which: `cellMain`,
`cellCross`, `mainGap`, `crossGap`, `extent` and `mainOffset`.

#### What stays in screen space

Your own symbol classes need no changes, because everything a symbol sees is
in screen space, whatever the orientation: `symbolSize(width, height)`,
`symbolGap(x, y)`, `ReelSymbol.resize(width, height)`, `CellBounds`,
`getCellBounds`, `getBlockBounds`, and the position of the `ReelSet` itself.

A horizontal set is the vertical one transposed. Swap width and height and
you have the same board on its side.

```ts
// A 5x3 vertical board.
.symbolSize(120, 100).symbolGap(8, 6)

// The same board, sideways.
.orientation('horizontal').symbolSize(100, 120).symbolGap(6, 8)
```

Indices do not move either. The same `ColumnTarget[]` goes into
`setResult()`, the same shape comes out of `getVisibleGrid()`, and a cell
address means the same cell whichever way the strip runs.

#### Start and end are geometric

The buffers are named `start` and `end`:

```ts
.bufferSymbols({ start: 1, end: 1 })
reelSet.setResult([{ visible: ['A','B','C'], bufferStart: ['COIN'] }]);
```

Start is the smaller screen coordinate: above on a vertical set, left on a
horizontal one. Direction does not change it.

A buffer symbol is placed against an edge of the window, like a coin
peeking above the top row or a big symbol's tail parked outside it. If start
and end followed travel, reversing a reel would move all of them to the
other side of the screen. So motion follows direction, and buffers follow
the screen.

The feed edge, the side new symbols arrive from, does follow travel. You do
not set it. The engine derives it, and you can read it as
`reel.axis.feedEdge`.

#### Per-reel direction

```ts
.direction('forward')                                        // every reel
.directionPerReel(['forward','reverse','forward','reverse','forward'])
```

Use it for alternating columns or a single reversed reel.

A big symbol wider than one reel cannot be combined with mixed per-reel
directions. The block coordinator assumes every reel a block covers feeds
from the same edge, and with mixed directions the block would split
mid-spin. So `build()` throws when the per-reel array holds more than one
distinct value. An array with one value throughout is fine. Keep blocks
inside one reel, or give the whole set one direction.

#### Render order

Direction does not change which symbol overlaps which:

```ts
.cellStacking('ascending')   // default: the cell at the larger coordinate draws in front
.reelStacking('ascending')   // default: the last reel draws in front
```

Stacking follows the screen, not travel. Art is lit from above, and
flipping the stacking on a roll-up would make that lighting read backwards.
A tease that reverses a reel for one spin would also re-layer the board in
front of the player. If your art needs the opposite order, pass
`'descending'`.

#### Nudge is relative

```ts
await reelSet.nudge(2, { distance: 1, direction: 'forward', incoming: ['wild'] });
```

Here `'forward'` means the way this reel travels, not down. On a reel built
with `direction('reverse')`, a vertical reel nudged forward moves upward and
takes its new symbols in from the bottom. The same call works on every reel.

#### Two sets in one container

A banner above a grid is two reel sets in one container. There is no
separate API for it.

```ts
const main = new ReelSetBuilder().reels(5).visibleCells(3)./* ... */.build();

const banner = new ReelSetBuilder()
  .orientation('horizontal')
  .reels(1)            // one reel...
  .visibleCells(5)     // ...of five cells, one above each main reel
  ./* ... */.build();

const stage = new PIXI.Container();
banner.y = 0;
main.y = CELL + GAP * 3;
stage.addChild(banner, main);
```

Lay each set out from its own top-left. Scale the container, never the sets
inside it. If you scale one set, the other keeps its old size and the two no
longer line up.

The [banner-ways](/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#banner-ways) demo is
the full version, with a banner wild that extends a ways win.

#### Seeing the axis

The debug overlay draws each reel's axis:

```ts
import { debugOverlay } from 'pixi-reels/debug'; // needs pixi-silk, a dev dependency

const overlay = debugOverlay(reelSet, { layers: ['axis', 'feed', 'thresholds', 'hud'] });
```

- `axis`: one arrow per reel, pointing the way it travels
- `feed`: the edge new symbols arrive at
- `thresholds`: the wrap lines. No symbol should ever be drawn past one
- `hud`: a line per reel, such as `r0 VF feed=start spd=... cells=3`

`overlay.describe()` returns the same information as plain JSON, for tests
and for anything that cannot look at a canvas. See [Debugging](/learn/debugging/).

- [Horizontal banner](/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#horizontal-banner) is a one-reel sideways strip.
- [Every reel upward](/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#roll-up) reverses the whole set.
- [Direction per reel](/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#roll-up-alternating) alternates the columns.
- [Banner in a ways win](/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#banner-ways) puts a banner above a 5x3 that joins the win.

    `#horizontal-banner` needs no anchor - the heading below auto-slugs to it. */}

#### Horizontal banner

A one-reel strip that scrolls sideways, such as a banner showing which symbols pay this round. It is `.orientation('horizontal')` on the normal builder, with the same spin lifecycle, events and speed profiles as a vertical set.

Live demo (horizontal-banner): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#static-spin-horizontal

#### Upward reels

##### Every reel

`.direction('reverse')` makes every reel spin upward. The spin, the events and the landing bounce are the same, run the other way.

Live demo (roll-up): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#roll-up-reverse-direction

##### Direction per reel

`.directionPerReel([...])` sets each reel's direction on its own. Here odd reels spin up and even reels spin down. Each reel still lands the exact result, because it feeds new symbols from its own edge.

Live demo (roll-up-alternating): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#mixed-direction-per-reel

#### Sideways with mixed direction

Orientation is set for the whole set at `build()`, and direction is set per reel, so the two combine. Here the strips run sideways, rows 0 and 2 scroll right, and rows 1 and 3 scroll left.

A big symbol wider than one reel (`size.reels > 1`) cannot be combined with mixed per-reel directions. A block assumes every reel it covers feeds from the same edge and would split mid-spin, so `build()` throws. A `directionPerReel` array with the same value throughout is fine.

Live demo (orientation-horizontal-per-reel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#both-knobs-at-once

#### Banner in a ways win

A horizontal banner above a 5x3 ways set. The banner acts as a sixth reel: a wild in the banner cell above a reel makes that reel count toward the way. These are two `ReelSet`s in one container. The engine spins and lands both. The recipe evaluates the ways and spotlights the cells, because pixi-reels never computes wins.

Live demo (banner-ways): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#banner-that-joins-a-ways-win

#### Reading the axis

Each reel has `reel.axis`, with `orientation`, `direction`, `polarity`, `mainProp`, `crossProp` and `feedEdge`. `axis.toScreen(0, axis.polarity)` turns one step of travel into a screen vector, so the arrows in the demo are drawn with no orientation check. The same code points down on a vertical forward reel and left on a horizontal reverse one.

`feedEdge` is the side new symbols arrive from. It is derived from `polarity`: `'start'` for forward, `'end'` for reverse. Read it when you need it instead of tracking it next to `direction`.

Live demo (orientation-axis-readout): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#read-the-axis-instead-of-remembering-it

### Curved reels
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/reel-curvature/
Bend the strip onto a drum so the top and bottom cells lean away, like a physical machine.
Tags: curve, curvature, perspective, projection, cylinder, drum, 3d

Curvature is presentation only. It never changes what lands where,
`getVisibleGrid()`, or any event payload.

#### Two drawing modes

```ts
builder.curve(0.45).curveMode('warp').renderer(app.renderer);
```

| | `'symbol'` (default) | `'warp'` |
|---|---|---|
| Spine and composites bend | no | yes |
| Atlas art keystones | no | yes |
| Motion follows the curve | no | yes |
| Cost | free | 1 render pass per reel per frame |
| Sharpness | native | one resample |
| Needs `renderer()` | no | yes, `build()` throws |

`'warp'` renders each reel to a texture and moves the vertices of a mesh, so
everything inside the reel bends without any help from the symbols.
`'symbol'` projects each cell on its own. It is sharper, but a `Container`
transform is affine, so it can only bend content that is a single texture.

#### Lifted symbols stay flat

Under `'warp'`, anything drawn outside the reel's texture is not bent:
`unmask: true` symbols, the win spotlight, pin flights and overlays all draw
flat over a curved board. The builder logs a warning when it sees `unmask`
with the warp. `'symbol'` mode has no such split. For art that overflows its
cell under the warp, use `curveBleed` instead of `unmask`.

#### Changing the curve at run time

```ts
reelSet.setCurve(0.4);
reelSet.setCurve([0.2, 0.35, 0.5, 0.35, 0.2]);
reelSet.setCurve(0); // flat
```

#### Extending `'symbol'` mode

This only matters if you do not use the warp. The engine hands each symbol a
projected quad through `ReelSymbol.applyCellQuad()`.

`SpriteSymbol` and `AnimatedSpriteSymbol` map it onto a `PerspectiveMesh`,
which keystones the art with no extra render pass, when the texture owns its
whole source. `canProjectTexture()` refuses atlas sub-frames: the mesh
addresses its source with 0..1 UVs, and remapping them onto the frame has not
produced a correct draw yet. Every other symbol gets a uniform scale that
fits inside the quad, so no cell overlaps its neighbour and a `7` is never
squashed.

In this fallback the engine owns `view.scale`. A win animation that tweens
`symbol.view.scale` overwrites the projection while it runs, so animate a
child of `view` instead. The warp has no such conflict.

For your own single-texture symbol, `PerspectiveCell` is exported and does
the mesh work. Art that does not fill its cell reports its real rect through
`ReelSymbol.cellInset`, which the sprite symbols derive from the texture's
trim.

##### Demos

`.curve(amount)` bends each reel onto a drum, so the outer cells lean away like the ones on a physical machine. Every demo here uses `.curveMode('warp')`, which bends whatever a reel contains. The Concept section below compares it with the default `'symbol'` mode.

#### A curved board

A slot reel is a drum. The middle cell faces you and the outer ones have turned away, so a camera draws them as trapezoids rather than smaller rectangles. The grid on the tiles shows it: the lines converge on the outer rows and stay parallel on the middle one.

`.curve(amount)` takes `0` for flat, the default, and `1` for a hard barrel. Most boards use `0.3` to `0.5`.

Live demo (curved-reels): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/reel-curvature/#one-number

```ts
builder.curve(0.45);                          // depth defaults to amount * 0.5
builder.curve({ amount: 0.45, depth: 0.35 }); // stronger perspective
```

`depth` is how much smaller an edge cell is than the middle one. At `0` the projection is orthographic: cells bunch up but nothing recedes. It is capped slightly under `cos(arc)`, past which cells would fold back over each other.

The middle cell is drawn at its authored size, so the drum cannot also fill a window sized for flat cells. The ends fall short, and the buffer cells show in that band. Cover it with a frame, as a cabinet bezel does. `reel.curve.mapMain(0)` is where the drum's top edge lands, so the frame can be measured.

#### Art that bends

##### Atlas sprites

Playson's Supercharged Diamonds 3, the sheet the sprite Hold &amp; Win recipes use. The frames are trimmed atlas frames, which `'symbol'` mode cannot keystone. Under `'warp'` they bend like everything else, and the blur during the spin still works.

Live demo (curved-reels-gems): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/reel-curvature/#on-real-art

##### Spine skeletons

Spine skeletons, which `'symbol'` mode cannot bend at all. Under `'warp'` they curve and keep animating, and the spin and the stop bounce follow the drum.

Live demo (curved-reels-warp): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/reel-curvature/#curved-reels-warp

Symbols that hang over their cell need two settings. `SymbolData.zIndex` stacks them within the reel, and `.curveBleed(px)` keeps the warp texture from cutting the overhang off at its edge. With `curveBleed` under `curveFocus('reel')`, also set `SharedRectMaskStrategy` yourself, or the per-reel mask clips the overhang.

```ts
builder.symbolData({ mystery: { zIndex: 2 } }).curveBleed(46);
```

##### Text

A value reel for prize pickers and jackpot ladders. The symbols are drawn at run time and the symbol id is the amount, so `setResult([['100.00', ...]])` lands the value you name. Each cell is a `PIXI.Text`, which has no texture of its own, so only the warp bends the digits.

Live demo (curved-value-reel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/reel-curvature/#numbers-not-art

#### The camera

##### One camera for the board

By default each reel has its own camera and is its own drum. `curveFocus('set')` puts one camera in front of the middle of the board, so the outer reels tilt toward the centre and the centre reel barely moves. `'set-lean'` is halfway between and usually looks best on a 5-wide board.

```ts
builder.curve(0.5).curveFocus('reel');     // default: five separate drums
builder.curve(0.5).curveFocus('set-lean'); // halfway
builder.curve(0.5).curveFocus('set');      // one camera, one wide cylinder
```

Leaning cells cross into the next reel's column, so any focus other than `'reel'` selects `SharedRectMaskStrategy`. Pass `.maskStrategy(...)` to override it.

Live demo (curved-reels-focus): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/reel-curvature/#where-the-camera-stands

##### A curve per reel

`.curvePerReel([...])` gives each reel its own curve. Bending the middle reels hardest and the outer ones least makes the board read as one wide drum. The array needs one entry per reel, matching `reels()`.

Live demo (curved-reels-per-reel): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/reel-curvature/#one-drum-not-five

#### Board shapes

##### A pay band in a taller drum

Five rows are drawn and the middle three pay. The outer rows are there to be curved, and they are what makes the board read as a cylinder. On a bare 3-row board the drum has to bend hard enough to distort the symbols people read. Here the bend goes into rows that do not pay, so this board can use a deeper `curve(0.62)`.

The dimming over the outer rows is drawn from `getCellQuad()`, the four corners the cell is drawn on. `getCellBounds()` returns the quad's bounding box, which is looser than the cell on a curved reel. Outline with the quad and hit-test with the box.

Live demo (curved-reels-payband): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/reel-curvature/#a-pay-band-inside-a-taller-drum

##### Cascades

The warp applies the bend to the rendered reel, so explosions, survivors sliding down and new symbols dropping in all follow the curve. The cascade code does not know the reel is curved.

A tumble board needs the frame over both ends. At the top the band would show the buffer cell, which holds the refill queue and does not move when survivors fall. At the bottom a pure tumble sets `bufferSymbols({ end: 0 })`, so there is nothing to show.

Live demo (curved-reels-cascade): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/reel-curvature/#cascades-on-a-drum

### Skip and slam
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/
Decide what a tap does mid-spin: stop every reel, land them one by one, or let a tease finish.
Tags: skip, slam, anticipation, tease, phases, timing, groups

A spin has three phases, and a fourth when you ask for it.

The start phase pulls back a little and then accelerates, like a lever. The
spin phase runs at full speed and waits for the server. The anticipation
phase is optional. It slows one reel to build tension, and it only runs if
you called `setAnticipation()` before the result arrived. Most scatter games
use it, so it ships with the library. The stop phase brakes onto the target
frame, overshoots, and settles.

#### What events the reel set fires

The reel set reports each step as an event, so you do not need to poll. One
`await reelSet.spin()` fires them in this order.

`spin:start` fires on every `spin()`, however the spin ends. The reels are
moving.

`spin:allStarted` fires when every reel except the held ones is at full
speed. This is the event that matters for timing. You can call `setResult()`
earlier, and the engine holds it until this event has fired.

`spin:stopping` fires once per reel, with its index, as the reel starts
braking. Held reels never fire it.

`spin:reelLanding` fires when a reel is on its result frame: the strip has
snapped, every visible symbol has been told it landed, and the bounce is
about to start. It carries the reel index and its symbols. Start anything
tied to the landing here, such as an overlay growing over the reel, a
per-reel sound, or a symbol takeover.

`spin:reelLanded` fires when that reel has settled, a full `bounceDuration`
after `spin:reelLanding`. On a slam, which has no bounce, the two fire on the
same tick. It carries the index and the symbols. Use it for per-reel effects
that should wait for the bounce, such as a scatter ping or a column glow,
without waiting for the whole grid.

Each symbol hears the landing too. `onReelLanded(ctx)` runs on every visible
symbol immediately before `spin:reelLanding`, and the context says which reel and
cell it landed in. A Spine symbol's `autoPlayLanding` option can be a
function of that context, returning `true`, `false` or an animation name. That
lets the symbols on a reel that a takeover is about to cover skip their
landing while the rest land as usual:

```ts
new SpineReelSymbol({
  spineMap,
  autoPlayLanding: ({ reelIndex }) => !copyReels.has(reelIndex),
});

reelSet.events.on('spin:reelLanding', (reelIndex) => {
  if (copyReels.has(reelIndex)) overlay.growOver(reelIndex);
});
```

A symbol that starts a landing animation this way exposes it as
`symbol.landing`, a promise that holds until the reel moves again. Code that
should play after the landing can await it instead of taking over the
animation track.

`spin:allLanded` fires when the last non-held reel is down, with the full
result attached.

`spin:complete` fires right after, with the same `SpinResult`, which already
carries `duration`. Start the win presentation here.

#### Fetch the result mid-spin

A slot calls the server while the reels spin.

```ts
const promise = reelSet.spin();
const response = await fetch('/api/spin').then((r) => r.json());
reelSet.setResult(response.symbols);
if (response.anticipationReels?.length) {
  reelSet.setAnticipation(response.anticipationReels);
}
const result = await promise;
```

Call `setResult()` while the reels are spinning. Calling it early is fine,
because the engine holds the stop until every reel is in the spin phase. If
you never call it, the promise waits forever.

#### The skip calls

There are three calls, and you pick one by what the player did.

`skipSpin()` is for a player press on the slam button. It knows about the
round. It throws if the result has not arrived yet, so use `requestSkip()` in
that window. The first press also raises the speed in standard mode, or makes
later refills slam on their own in cascade mode. It fires `skip:boosted` when
it raises the speed.

`requestSkip()` slams as soon as it can. It is safe to call before
`setResult()`: it queues and fires once, with no boost. Use it for a player
pressing the button before the server answers.

`slamStop()` lands the reels now, with no boost and no queueing.

All three land on whatever `setResult()` gave the engine and set
`result.wasSkipped` to `true`. Every lifecycle event still fires on the slam
path, so the win presenter needs no second code path.

`skipStage` tells you where the round is: 0 before any press, 2 after the
press that ended it, and 1 while a protected tease is still running (see
below). Drive the button's look from it.

#### Skip granularity

By default a slam lands every reel. It force-completes every active phase,
including the skippable anticipation phase, so a press on a teasing spin ends
the tease before the player sees it.

To land some reels and let others keep playing:

```ts
// The tease rule, applied by the engine.
reelSet.setAnticipation([2, 3, 4], { stagger: 'sequential', protect: 'once' });
// press 1 -> reels 0-1 land now, 2-4 keep teasing, skipStage becomes 1
// press 2 -> the tease ends too, skipStage becomes 2

// 'stepwise' releases the tease one reel per press instead.
reelSet.setAnticipation([2, 3, 4], { protect: 'stepwise' });
// press 1 -> reels 0-1;  press 2 -> reel 2;  press 3 -> reel 3;
// press 4 -> reel 4, and that press ends the round

// Or do it by hand, for your own rule.
reelSet.slamStop({ except: [3, 4] });
```

For a grouping the built-in modes do not cover, use `protect: 'always'`, so
no press can end a tease, and land your own groups with `slamStop({ reels })`
on each press.

`protect` applies to `skipSpin()` and `requestSkip()`, including a press
queued before the result arrived, which is the case it exists for. Call
`setAnticipation` before `setResult` so the queued press can see the tease.
A bare `slamStop()` always lands now.

`skip:requested` and `skip:completed` carry `{ reels, partial }`, so a
listener can tell a partial slam from the one that ends the round.

In a tumble cascade the initial spin protects the same way. Two things
change. The round's side effect is that refills slam on their own instead of
a speed boost, and refills carry no tease, since `refill()` clears the
anticipation set on entry. A Hold & Win board is one single-reel set per
cell, so a per-reel slam has nothing to divide there and
`BoardGrid.skipSpinning()` skips per cell instead. The
[cascade protect demo](/mechanics/skip/#skip-cascade-protect) and the section
after it cover both.

Two mid-spin calls look like they would help here and do not. Both are
covered by tests. Shrinking the set with `setAnticipation()` does not release
a reel that is already teasing, because the set is read once, when a reel
leaves the spin phase. And `setSpeed()` does not re-time the round in flight,
because `spin()` captures the active profile and hands that instance to every
phase. That is also why the `skipSpin()` boost takes effect on the next spin.

#### Spin floor

`minimumSpinTime` sets how long a reel spins before it may stop. It lives on
the speed profile, so it is one value shared by every reel. `setStopDelays()`
is per reel but cannot go under it, so on their own the two settings could
not make one reel land on arrival while another kept spinning.
`setMinimumSpinTime` overrides the floor per reel and covers that case.

```ts
reelSet.setMinimumSpinTime([0, 0, 0, 900, 900]); // last two hold longer
reelSet.setMinimumSpinTime(null);                // back to the profile
```

On teasing spins, use `protect` instead of a raised floor. If a scatterless
skip lands instantly but a teasing one settles slower, the response time
tells the player a feature is coming before the reels have landed.

#### Holding some reels

Expanding wilds and single-reel respins need some reels to stay put.

```ts

const spin = reelSet.spin({ holdReels: [0, 4] });
reelSet.setResult(serverGrid);
await spin;
```

A held reel does not spin and keeps what it is showing. It counts as already
landed, so `spin:allLanded` waits only on the others, and it fires neither
`spin:stopping` nor `spin:reelLanded`. `setAnticipation([...])` drops held
indices without an error.

#### Overriding the spin mode

Some slots spin first and then cascade. The `mode` spin option swaps the
phase chain for one call.

```ts
const reelSet = new ReelSetBuilder()
  // ...
  .tumble({
    fall:   { duration: 280, ease: 'power3.in',  cellStagger: 60 },
    dropIn: { duration: 450, ease: 'power3.out', cellStagger: 60, distance: 'perHole' },
  })
  .ticker(app.ticker)
  .build();

await reelSet.spin();                  // round 1: strip-spin (default mode)
await reelSet.spin({ mode: 'cascade' }); // respin: cascade drop-in
```

Picking `'cascade'` without `.tumble(...)` throws, and the error names the
missing method. See the [spin-then-cascade demo](/mechanics/cascade/#spin-then-cascade).

#### Nudge

After a spin lands, you can move one reel a few cells to reveal symbols you
choose. The spin pipeline is idle while this runs, and the nudge drives the
strip itself.

```ts
await reelSet.spin();
await reelSet.nudge(2, { distance: 1, direction: 'forward', incoming: ['wild'] });
```

The direction is relative to the reel's own travel, not to the screen. See
[Orientation & direction](/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#concept).
For several reels at once, run independent calls under `Promise.all`.

A nudge can be cancelled mid-tween through its `signal` option, which rejects
with an `AbortError` and fires `nudge:cancelled`, or finished early with
`skipNudge`, which resolves normally.

The [nudge page](/mechanics/nudge/#concept) has the full contract and these
demos: [nudge](/mechanics/nudge/), [skip](/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-skip),
[abort](/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-abort), [stagger](/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-stagger),
[spotlight after a nudge](/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-spotlight),
[big symbols](/mechanics/nudge/#nudge-big-symbol).

#### Full event map

| Event                  | Payload                                         | When |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ---- |
| `spin:start`           | none                                            | Any `spin()` call |
| `spin:allStarted`      | none                                            | Every non-held reel is in the spin phase |
| `spin:stopping`        | `(reelIndex)`                                   | A reel begins its stop (held reels never fire) |
| `spin:reelLanding`     | `(reelIndex, symbols)`                          | A reel is on its result frame, bounce not started, after every `onReelLanded()`. Every landing path, cascade refill stages included |
| `spin:reelLanded`      | `(reelIndex, symbols)`                          | A reel landed (held reels never fire) |
| `spin:allLanded`       | `(result)`                                      | The last non-held reel landed |
| `spin:complete`        | `(result)`                                      | Just after `spin:allLanded` |
| `skip:requested`       | `({ reels, partial })`                          | A slam fired, from `skipSpin()`, `requestSkip()` (after `setResult`) or `slamStop()`. `partial` is `true` when reels are still spinning after it |
| `skip:completed`       | `({ reels, partial })`                          | Those reels have been force-landed |
| `skip:boosted`         | `({ previous, current })`                       | First `skipSpin()` press of a standard-mode round. The engine bumped the speed to the fastest registered profile for the rest of the round. Cascade mode auto-slams refills instead |
| `speed:changed`        | `(profile, previous)`                           | `setSpeed()` called |
| `spotlight:start`      | `(positions)`                                   | `spotlight.cycle(...)` began |
| `spotlight:end`        | none                                            | The spotlight finished |
| `pin:placed`           | `(pin)`                                         | `reelSet.pin(...)` succeeded |
| `pin:expired`          | `(pin, reason)`                                 | A pin was removed by `unpin`, by its `turns` running out, by an `'eval'` reset, or by a `'collision'` (a reshape clamped it onto an occupied cell) |
| `pin:moved`            | `(pin, from)`                                   | `reelSet.movePin(...)` resolved |
| `pin:migrated`         | `(pin, info)`                                   | A MultiWays reshape moved a pin to a new cell |
| `pin:overlayCreated`   | `(pin, symbol)`                                 | A mid-spin overlay symbol was mounted for a pin |
| `pin:overlayDestroyed` | `(pin, symbol)`                                 | A mid-spin overlay was torn down on land |
| `shape:changed`        | `(cellsPerReel)`                                | MultiWays `setShape(...)` accepted |
| `adjust:start`         | `({ reelIndex, fromCells, toCells })`           | The adjust phase entered for a reel |
| `adjust:complete`      | `({ reelIndex })`                               | The adjust phase finished |
| `nudge:start`          | `({ reelIndex, distance, direction })`          | `reelSet.nudge(...)` pre-placement done, tween about to begin |
| `nudge:complete`       | `({ reelIndex, distance, direction, symbols })` | The nudged reel snapped to its new grid position |
| `nudge:cancelled`      | `({ reelIndex, distance, direction, reason })`  | The nudge signal aborted or the reel was destroyed mid-tween. Never fires together with `nudge:complete` |
| `destroyed`            | none                                            | `destroy()` called |

#### Reference

* [Phases](/reference/api-phases/): customize start, spin and stop timing
* [Events](/reference/api-events/): types and exact signatures
* [SpinOptions](/reference/api-builder/#spin-options): `holdReels`, `mode`

##### Demos
