A press during a spin is a skip. By default it force-completes every phase, `AnticipationPhase` included, so every reel lands at once and a tease ends before the player sees it. The first demos show that plain press. The later ones land only some reels, keep a tease on screen, and change how a phase answers a press.

#### The basic press

##### Land every reel now

The player presses and the reels land on the result. Call `requestSkip()` from the button. `skipSpin()` throws if the result has not arrived yet, while `requestSkip()` waits for it.

Live demo (slam-stop): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#slam-stop

##### Press before the result arrives

`skipSpin()` throws before `setResult()`, because there is nothing to land on yet. `requestSkip()` queues the press and fires it when the result arrives, with protection applied. The result in this demo is delayed on purpose.

A queued press can only protect a tease the engine already knows about, so call `setAnticipation` before `setResult`.

Live demo (skip-queued-request): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-queued-request

#### Land some reels

##### Leave some reels spinning

`slamStop({ except: [3, 4] })` lands reels 0 to 2 now and leaves 3 and 4 to stop on their own.

A partial slam does not end the round. The button stays live. Only a full slam moves `skipStage` to `2` and applies the speed boost.

Live demo (skip-partial-slam): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-partial-slam

##### Name the reels that land

`slamStop({ reels })` names the reels to land instead of the ones to spare. Here a plan of three presses lands the board from the outside in.

Neither form needs a guard. Out-of-range indices are ignored, and held or landed reels are never slammed.

Live demo (skip-reels-complement): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-reels-complement

#### Protect a tease

##### Keep the tease for one press

`protect: 'once'` makes the engine apply the partial slam for you. Press 1 lands every reel outside the tease and leaves the tease running, so the trigger symbols are on screen. Press 2 ends it.

Call `setAnticipation` before `setResult`. A press made before the result arrives is queued by `requestSkip()` and fires as soon as the result does, so the tease has to be registered by then.

Live demo (protected-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-tease-protect

##### One tease reel per press

`protect: 'stepwise'` applies the same rule reel by reel. Press 1 lands everything outside the tease, and each press after it releases the next tease reel, so the player sets the pace.

Release order follows the tease order you passed, not the reel index. `setAnticipation([4, 2, 3], ...)` releases reel 4 first.

Live demo (skip-stepwise-tease): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-stepwise-tease

##### A tease no press can end

With `protect: 'always'`, press 1 lands everything outside the tease, as with `'once'`, and every later press is ignored. Use it when the tease is the reward, such as a jackpot reveal or a bonus landing on the last reel.

A refused press emits no events and does not throw. `slamStop()` still lands everything, because the engine refuses the player's press and never your own code's.

Live demo (skip-always-protect): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-always-protect

##### Your own release order

For an order the built-in modes do not cover, use `protect: 'always'` and release the reels yourself with `slamStop({ reels })` from a queue in your code. `'always'` guarantees that no press ends a tease behind the queue's back. Here three teasing reels come down in two presses.

Live demo (skip-custom-plan): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-custom-plan

##### Button state

`reelSet.skipStage` is `0` before any press, `1` after a press that landed the reels around a protected tease and left it running, and `2` after the press that ended the round. Stage `1` only happens with protection, so a game without protected teases sees a button with two states. Read the stage off `reelSet.skipStage` every frame instead of counting presses.

Live demo (skip-stage-button): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-stage-button

##### Turbo has nothing to protect

The turbo profiles set `anticipationDelay: 0`. With a hold of `0` ms there is no tease, and `protect` does nothing. Protecting a tease that never plays would stall the reels and bring back the response-time tell. The spins here alternate on one turbo profile, and only `duration` differs between them. Pass `duration` to get a tease in turbo too.

Live demo (skip-turbo-inert): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-turbo-inert

##### Skip without a tell

This demo shows why you protect the tease instead of slowing the skip down. Spins alternate between no scatters and a tease, and both press at the same moment. The panel times the last reel outside the tease. The two times match, and the only difference is what happens on screen after the press.

Raising `minimumSpinTime` instead gets the pacing right but leaks the outcome through response time. The player can tell a feature is coming from how the button felt.

Live demo (skip-no-tell): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-no-tell

#### Stop and skip in groups

Reel index is the engine's only order by default. It cannot express "reels 1 and 2 land together, 3 and 4 tease one press each, reel 5 lands last". Reel 5 is index 4, so its stop delay comes due in the middle of the tease.

```ts
reelSet.setReelGroups([[0, 1], [2, 3], [4]]);
reelSet.setAnticipation([2, 3], { stagger: 'sequential', protect: 'stepwise' });
// Presses walk the board: [1,2] -> 3 -> 4 -> [5].
```

A group is a barrier for stopping and for skipping. When stopping, no reel starts its stop sequence, anticipation included, until every reel in the earlier groups has landed, and it keeps spinning at full speed while it waits. When skipping, a press releases the next group that has not landed, with protection still applied inside it. Stop delays count from the start of the group. An explicit `setStopDelays()` still wins.

You can set groups any time up to `setResult()`. The barrier is read as each reel's SpinPhase resolves, so a round can take its grouping from its own server response. Every reel must appear exactly once, and changing the layout after reels have begun landing throws. `null` clears it.

Live demo (reel-groups): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#reel-groups

#### Quicken

##### Land with a bounce

A slam places the frame and lands in the same tick, so the press reads as a cut. `requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken' })` frees the same reels a slam would, with protection, `'stepwise'` and groups all applied, and asks each one for its normal landing. The tease ends, the stop delay is cut, and the reel spins its frame in and bounces. `speed: 'turbo'` lands the quickened reels on the turbo spin-out and bounce. `builder.skipMode('quicken')` makes quicken the default mode.

A quicken is a skip. `skipStage` advances, `wasSkipped` is true, and `SpinResult.skipMode` says which mode ended the round. A `mode: 'slam'` press after it still cuts whatever is moving. Tapping the readout sends that slam press, so you can see the cut on the same spin.

Live demo (skip-quicken): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-quicken

##### Quicken with groups

A quicken walks the same groups a slam would and quickens each one instead of placing it. A freed group turns violet, which is the stop phase spinning in, instead of going straight to grey. The cards are `PhaseCardSymbol`, so each colour is a phase.

A quickened reel counts as released, so a quick second press is taken early. The reel behind the barrier still waits for the group before it to land: reel 5 stays blue until reel 4 is down, however fast you press.

Live demo (quicken-groups): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#quicken-groups

##### Quicken, then slam

One button with two presses. The first calls `requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken', speed: 'turbo' })` and the second calls `requestSkip({ mode: 'slam' })`. A quicken press passes over the reels it already quickened, and a slam press cuts them. Both are skips, and `SpinResult.skipMode` names the one that ended the round.

Each press carries a `payload` (`{ press: 1 }`, `{ press: 2 }`), and the HUD reads it back off `skip:requested`, along with the profile a quicken named as `speed.name`. The event carries the whole press, which is the same context every phase's `onSkip(ctx)` receives, and `SpinResult.skipContext` keeps the last one.

Decide whether the round has been quickened from `skip:requested` and its `mode`, not from a local counter. A press that freed nothing must not arm the slam.

Live demo (quicken-then-slam): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#quicken-then-slam

#### Minimum spin time

##### Per-reel floor

There is no slam in this demo. `minimumSpinTime` is one value on the speed profile, shared by every reel. `setMinimumSpinTime([0, 0, 0, 1000, 1000])` overrides it per reel, so reels 0 to 2 take the result as soon as it arrives while 3 and 4 spin for a full second.

The setting stays across `spin()` and `refill()` until you clear it with `null`, like `setStopDelays()`. Set it once at boot, not on every spin.

The floor only applies to natural landings. A slam ignores it, so a tap mid-spin lands all five reels together and the labels read `-> slam`.

Live demo (skip-min-spin-time): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-min-spin-time

##### One floor for every reel

A single number raises the floor on every reel. `null` hands the floor back to the speed profile, which is not the same as a floor of `0`. The spins alternate so you can compare the two back to back.

Live demo (skip-min-spin-uniform): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-min-spin-uniform

#### Other spin modes

##### Cascades

Anticipation runs before the cascade and standard paths split, so a cascade spin teases and protects the same way a strip spin does. What a press carries differs in three ways:

| | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Initial spin | `protect` applies unchanged. Press 1 lands the reels outside the tease, press 2 ends it. |
| Round side effect | In cascade mode the side effect is that later refills slam on their own, not a speed boost. A protected press does not spend it. The press that ends the tease does, and every refill after that lands instantly. |
| Refills | No tease. `refill()` clears the anticipation set on entry, so a press during a refill is an ordinary full slam. `slamStop({ reels })` still works per reel there. |

A partial slam does not abort the chain, but it does mark the whole result `wasSkipped: true`.

Live demo (skip-cascade-protect): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#skip-cascade-protect

##### Hold & Win

This section has no demo. A Hold & Win board is one single-reel `ReelSet` per cell, so `slamStop({ reels })` can only name reel `0`. To skip per cell, use `BoardGrid.skipSpinning()` or `HoldAndWinBoard.skip()`.

Protection on a cell's set behaves consistently but is rarely useful, because the set of reels outside the tease is empty:

- `'once'`: press 1 spends the protection and lands nothing, press 2 lands the cell. This is intended.
- `'stepwise'`: the release group is the tease reel, so one press lands it.
- `'always'`: do not use it here. No press can land the cell, and the recovery path in `BoardGrid.skipSpinning()` needs the cell to land or the next `respin()` throws.

#### Custom phases

Every built-in phase is exported, so you can subclass one or write your own. See [Phases](/reference/api-phases/) for the full extension contract.

##### Subclass a built-in phase

This `StopPhase` subclass adds a backlight on landing. It inherits the sequencer, the bounce and the skip pose. Register it under the same key to replace the built-in.

Call `super` from every hook you override. A reel whose `onEnter` never reaches `super` spins forever. Override `onSkip` too if the backlight should also show on a slammed reel.

Live demo (phase-subclass-stop): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#phase-subclass-stop

##### A spin floor computed by the phase

A `SpinPhase` subclass sets a per-reel floor in one line. `setMinimumSpinTime([...])` does the same from configuration. Subclass when the floor is computed instead of configured.

Merge the config instead of replacing it: `super.onEnter({ ...config, minimumSpinTime })`.

The staircase only applies to natural landings. A slam ignores the floor, so a tap mid-spin flattens it and the labels read `-> slam`.

Live demo (phase-subclass-spin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#phase-subclass-spin

##### A countdown during the tease

An `AnticipationPhase` subclass draws a countdown on each teasing reel. `onEnter` shows the label and then calls `super`, `update(deltaMs)` runs every frame, and `onSkip` clears the label when a press force-completes the phase.

`update` adds up ticker time, not wall-clock time, so it stays correct in a background tab. The active `SpeedProfile` is on `this._speed`.

Live demo (phase-subclass-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#phase-subclass-anticipation

##### A phase from scratch

Extend `ReelPhase` when you replace the whole behaviour instead of adjusting it. This one replaces `StartPhase` with a linear ramp and no step-back pull.

Register it under the lifecycle key it replaces. The controller only asks for lifecycle keys, so a phase registered as `register('myPhase', ...)` is never used. Call `this._complete()` exactly once, or the spin promise never settles.

Live demo (phase-from-scratch-start): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#phase-from-scratch-start

##### Phases with constructor arguments

The cascade phases and `AdjustPhase` take build-time config as extra constructor arguments, so a subclass needs `registerFactory` and must pass them on. `resolveTumbleConfig(config)` builds the shape they expect.

Here `.phases(...)` comes before `.tumble(...)` and still wins, because configurators are deferred to `build()` and applied after the built-in registrations.

Live demo (phase-subclass-cascade): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#phase-subclass-cascade

##### A phase that can be quickened

A custom phase hears a press in `onSkip(ctx)` and reads `ctx.mode` to decide what to cut. This instant stop holds its frame a tenth of a cell short for 900 ms before it slides in. Under `'quicken'` the hook drops the hold and slides at once. Under `'slam'` it rests on the frame. The class sets `quickenable = true` to say its hook handles the mode. Without the flag, a quicken leaves the phase alone: the reel still lands, and the press shortens nothing.

The quicken branch should cut a wait, never the landing. Keep `land()` and `bounce()` where the natural path calls them, or a quickened reel lands differently from one that was left alone.

Live demo (quicken-custom-phase): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/skip/#quicken-custom-phase

### Spinning art
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/spinning-art/
While a reel spins it shows a blurred still of each symbol, so heavy art costs nothing and reads as motion.
Tags: static-spin, motion-blur, spine

A symbol at rest can be anything: a Spine skeleton, an animated sprite, a
container of layers. Register it through `StaticSpinSymbol` and give it a
`createInner` that builds the real symbol. At rest the inner symbol is live,
so idle loops and win animations play as usual. When the reel starts, the
wrapper deactivates it and spins a plain sprite of it instead. On landing it
brings the inner symbol back with the final id.

The sprite's texture comes from a `SpinTextureCache` shared by the set, which
snapshots each id once. With `spinTexture: 'blurred'`, the default, it also
bakes a motion blur along the reel's travel and crossfades to it over
`blurRampMs`. `spinTexture: 'static'` spins the sharp snapshot instead. No
filter runs during the spin, and no skeleton updates while the strip moves.

`prewarmSpinTextures` bakes every id before the first spin. Without it, each
id is baked the first time it is needed. If you have hand-drawn blur frames,
`cache.setBlurred(id, texture)` makes the cache use them instead.

##### Demos

Each demo spins through `StaticSpinSymbol`. The first bakes the blur for plain cards, the second does the same for a Spine set, and the third uses blur frames drawn by hand.

#### Baked blur

The cache snapshots each card once and bakes a motion blur from the snapshot, and the reels spin on those textures. There is no blur art in the demo, and no filter runs during the spin. `prewarmSpinTextures` bakes every id before the first spin so it does not stall.

Live demo (static-spin-blur): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/spinning-art/#auto-baked-motion-blur-static-spin

#### Spine at rest

At rest every cell is a live Spine skeleton with its idle and landing animations. When the reels start, each cell switches to a cached snapshot and the skeleton is deactivated, so no skeleton updates while the reels spin. On landing the skeletons come back and play their landing animation.

Live demo (static-spin-spine): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/spinning-art/#spin-static-not-spine

#### Your own blur art

The round symbols use blur frames drawn in the atlas, handed to the cache with `cache.setStatic(id, texture)` and `cache.setBlurred(id, texture)`. The cache uses those as they are and never bakes or destroys them. The royal symbols have no blur frames, so the cache bakes theirs. Both kinds spin through the same `StaticSpinSymbol`.

Live demo (static-spin-provided-blur): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/spinning-art/#bring-your-own-blur-textures

### Split symbols
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/split-symbols/
A winning symbol breaks into two or more copies, and its reel makes room for them.
Tags: split, splitSymbol, setColumn, resetColumns, ways, multiways, stacked-symbols

When a symbol splits, the cell it stands on becomes two or more cells. The
server says what the symbol splits into. Pass that list to `splitSymbol` with
the symbol's reel and cell, and each id gets its own cell. The cells above and
below keep their symbols. Any symbol one reel wide can split, either a 1x1 or
a stacked big symbol in full view. The call returns the new cells, so the
game can animate them.

```ts
const { reelIndex, from, count } = reelSet.splitSymbol(reel, cell, ids, { height: 'grow' });
```

The `height` option sets what happens to the reel when it gains cells:

- `'grow'` is the default. The cells keep their size and the reel gets
  taller. The board re-anchors around it as the builder's `reelAnchor` says.
- `'keep'` keeps the reel's height, and every cell on it shrinks to share
  that height, as cells on a MultiWays reel do. Nothing else moves. This is
  the default on MultiWays, where a reel's height is fixed.

`resetColumns()` puts every reel back to the cells it was built with, at
their original size. Both calls are built on `setColumn`, which shows a
column of any length on one reel. The
[infinity reels page](/mechanics/infinity-reels/#stacked-symbols-that-split)
covers splits of stacked symbols on a board that grows.

##### Demos

`splitSymbol()` places the cells of a split. The animation in these demos is each demo's own code. The first demo compares the two `height` modes, the second lets you split cells yourself, and the third splits on MultiWays.

#### Grow or keep

Both boards land the same result and split the same cells, one copy at a time. On the left the reel grows. On the right the reel keeps its height and its cells shrink. The titles show each reel's cell count and height, read from the engine.

Under `'keep'` every symbol on the reel is resized, so its art has to draw at any cell height, as MultiWays art already does. These boards anchor their reels at the top with `reelAnchor('start')`, so a reel grows downward. With the default `'center'` a reel grows in both directions and the board re-centres.

Live demo (split-modes): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/split-symbols/#split-modes

#### Tap a cell to split it

Tap any cell to split it in two, and the readout prints the call the tap made. Choose `grow` or `keep` above the board. Spin to start over, which calls `resetColumns()` first.

Live demo (split-tap): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/split-symbols/#split-tap

#### Splits on MultiWays

On MultiWays a reel's height is fixed, so a split makes room inside the reel and the ways go up with the cell count. The server names the winning symbol and which of its cells split, into two or three copies each. `WinLines` draws the ways after every split.

The cell count stays within the set's `[minCells, maxCells]`, as it would after a `setShape()`. Raise `multiways({ maxCells })` to allow more splits. The next spin's `setShape()` reshapes every reel from the cell count its split left it with.

Live demo (split-in-place): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/split-symbols/#split-in-place

#### Stacked symbols on infinity reels

The [infinity reels page](/mechanics/infinity-reels/#infinity-reels-split) has a demo where a stack two to four cells tall splits into more single symbols than it had cells. Its reel grows past the frame in both directions while `expand()` adds reels.

A reel that a block wider than one reel covers cannot change on its own, or the block's reels would no longer line up, so `splitSymbol()` and `setColumn()` throw there. Every demo on this page splits a symbol one reel wide.

### Starters
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/starters/
Small complete slots to copy as a starting point, one for each common layout.
Tags: starter, 5x3, cascade, multiways, hold-and-win, horizontal, reverse, orientation

Starting templates. Copy one, swap in your art and your math, and build from
there.

##### Demos

Each starter is a small working slot. The line slots come first, then the other common layouts, then the symbol pools that control what the reels draw while they spin.

#### Line slots

##### Classic 5x3 slot

A 5x3 slot that pays lines from left to right. Most slot games start from this layout.

Live demo (classic-5x3): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/starters/#classic-5x3

##### Horizontal

The same template with the reels turned sideways. Three reels are stacked down the screen and each one scrolls along x. The change is one call, `.orientation('horizontal')`, plus the cell size you want on screen.

`symbolSize(w, h)` and `symbolGap(x, y)` stay in screen space. On a horizontal set the strip advances by the symbol width, `x` is the gap between cells and `y` is the gap between reels. Index space does not change, so `reels(3).visibleCells(5)` and the `ColumnTarget[]` you pass to `setResult()` stay the same.

Live demo (starter-horizontal-5x3): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/starters/#starter-horizontal-5x3

##### Reverse

The classic 5x3 with the reels running the other way. Symbols rise and each reel lands from below. The only change from the classic starter is `.direction('reverse')`.

Buffers stay geometric. `bufferStart` is still the slot above the window, so on a reverse reel the next symbol to come in sits in `bufferEnd`. Read `reel.axis.feedEdge` instead of assuming. See [orientation and direction](/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#roll-up) for per-reel and mixed-axis setups.

Live demo (starter-reverse-5x3): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/starters/#starter-reverse-5x3

#### Other layouts

##### Cascade 6x4

A tumble slot built on `runCascade`. The first demo uses card symbols. The second is the same build with Spine art.

Live demo (cascade-6x5): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/starters/#cascade-6x5
Live demo (cascade-6x5-spine): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/starters/#cascade-6x5

##### MultiWays

Each reel lands on its own number of cells between `minCells` and `maxCells` on each spin. The number of ways is the product of the per-reel cell counts.

Call `reelSet.setShape(rowsPerReel)` before `setResult()`, with `serverGrid[i].length === rowsPerReel[i]`.

Live demo (multiways): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/starters/#cascade-6x5

##### Hold & Win

Coins lock where they land and the free cells respin until the grid fills. Board events drive the HUD. The [Hold & Win page](/mechanics/hold-and-win/) builds on this board.

Live demo (hold-and-win): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/starters/#hold-and-win

#### Which symbols may spawn where

`weights()` is one table for the whole set. A pool is layered on top of it for a scope, which can be one reel, the buffer cells, or the buffer cells of one reel. A pool changes only the random draw. An explicit `setResult` target always wins.

##### Keep a symbol out of the buffers

Each spin moves to the next pool state. First there is no pool, then COIN is kept out of the buffers of reel 1 (the second reel, since indices start at 0), then out of the buffers above the window, then out of all buffers. The labels above and below the grid show what the hidden cells hold, so you can watch COIN stop parking there.

Live demo (buffer-pool-exclude): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/starters/#symbol-pools

##### A draw table per reel

Each reel can have its own draw table. Watch the spin, not the landing. Reel 0 draws low cards only, reel 2 is mostly wilds while it scrolls, and reel 4 never draws a wild. All five share the same `weights()` underneath.

Live demo (per-reel-symbol-pool): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/starters/#symbol-pools

### Symbol classes
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/symbols/
Pick or write the class that draws a symbol, from sprites to Spine, and animate it when it wins.
Tags: symbols, pools, buffers, weights, spine, horizontal, orientation

A symbol is what fills one cell. Three classes ship with the library, and
the abstract base class is there for your own.

| Class | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `SpriteSymbol` | Static images. One texture per id. |
| `AnimatedSpriteSymbol` | Sprite-sheet animation loops. |
| `SpineSymbol` | Skeletal animation via `@esotericsoftware/spine-pixi-v8`. |
| `ReelSymbol` (abstract) | Your own drawing. |

#### Register

The builder's `symbols()` call hands you a registry. You register a class
with its options, not an instance. The engine constructs the symbols and
pools them.

```ts
builder.symbols((r) => {
  r.register('cherry', SpriteSymbol, { textures: { cherry: cherryTex } });
  r.register('bar',    AnimatedSpriteSymbol, { frames: barFrames, animationSpeed: 1.5 });
});
```

#### Custom symbol

Extend `ReelSymbol`. A symbol is activated with an id, may then get
`playWin` or `stopAnimation`, and is deactivated when the pool takes it back.

`resize(width, height)` runs on every swap, so positioning belongs there and
not in the constructor. A symbol that positions itself in the constructor
ends up in the wrong place after the first swap.

```ts
import { ReelSymbol } from 'pixi-reels';
import { Graphics } from 'pixi.js';

export class BlockSymbol extends ReelSymbol {
  private _g = new Graphics();

  constructor(opts: { colors: Record<string, number> }) {
    super();
    this.view.addChild(this._g);
    (this as any)._opts = opts;
  }

  protected onActivate(symbolId: string): void {
    const color = (this as any)._opts.colors[symbolId] ?? 0x888888;
    this._g.clear().roundRect(0, 0, 140, 140, 10).fill(color);
  }

  protected onDeactivate(): void {
    this._g.clear();
  }

  async playWin(): Promise<void> {
    // pulse for 400ms
    this.view.scale.set(1.1);
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 400));
    this.view.scale.set(1);
  }

  stopAnimation(): void { this.view.scale.set(1); }
  resize(w: number, h: number): void { this._g.clear().roundRect(0, 0, w, h, 10).fill(0x333333); }
}

// Register:
builder.symbols((r) => {
  r.register('red',   BlockSymbol, { colors: { red: 0xff6d70 } });
  r.register('blue',  BlockSymbol, { colors: { blue: 0x4cc2ff } });
});
```

#### Weights

A symbol with no weight gets 10. Change it with `weights()` on the builder.

```ts
builder.weights({ cherry: 40, bar: 20, seven: 4 });
```

A bigger number comes up more often. Weights only affect the random fill,
which is the strip while it spins and the buffer cells. A grid from
`setResult()` ignores weights, because the server decides what lands.

`weights()` is one table for the whole set. To keep a symbol out of the
buffer cells, or to make one reel draw differently, add a pool on top:

```ts
builder.randomSymbols({ exclude: ['EMPTY'] });                     // every reel
builder.randomSymbols({ exclude: ['COIN'] }, { slots: 'buffer' }); // buffers only
builder.randomSymbols({ weights: { WILD: 40 } }, { reel: 2 });     // reel 2 only
```

The same pools are available at run time through `reelSet.randomSymbols`,
which is where a game-mode switch belongs. [Buffer indexing](/mechanics/big-symbols/#concept-buffer-indexing)
has the layering rules.

#### Headless testing

`HeadlessSymbol` draws nothing and needs no textures or canvas. Use it in
tests.

```ts
import { HeadlessSymbol } from 'pixi-reels/testing';

builder.symbols((r) => {
  r.register('a', HeadlessSymbol, {});
  r.register('b', HeadlessSymbol, {});
});
```

[Cheats & testing](/learn/cheats-and-testing/) has the full setup.

##### Demos

Production art comes first, then what you can do to a symbol after it lands. Placeholder classes and symbols for sideways sets are at the end. Art that overflows its cell is on [Layers](/mechanics/layers/). The blurred copies a reel shows while it spins are on [Spinning art](/mechanics/spinning-art/).

#### Production art

##### Sprites from an atlas

Sprite symbols loaded from one TexturePacker atlas, so every frame comes from one file and one texture upload. Each id is registered with `BlurSpriteSymbol` from `@pixi-reels/kit`, which shows the atlas's blur frame while the reel spins.

Live demo (texture-atlas-symbols): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/symbols/#texture-atlas-symbols

##### Spine skins

Each symbol tier is one Spine skeleton, and each id in the tier is a skin of it. The board is a gapless 3-4-4-4-4-3 grid. The skeletons are wrapped in `StaticSpinSymbol`, so the reels spin on blurred snapshots and no skeleton runs mid-spin.

Live demo (spine-skins-3-4-4-4-4-3): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/symbols/#multi-skin-spine-tiers-on-a-compact-grid

#### After the reels land

##### Your own win animation

`WinPresenter` takes a `symbolAnim` callback that runs instead of `playWin()`. It gets the symbol, its cell and the win, so the animation can differ per `win.id`. Here the top line bounces harder than the other two.

Live demo (paylines-custom-animation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/symbols/#custom-per-symbol-animation

##### Transform a symbol

A low symbol turns into a higher one after the reels stop. `reelSet.setSymbolAt(reel, cell, id)` swaps the one cell and leaves the rest of the reel alone. Call it after `spin:complete` or `spin:reelLanded`: it throws while the reel is spinning and on a big symbol's anchor.

Live demo (symbol-transform): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/symbols/#symbol-transform

#### Blank cells

`EmptySymbol` takes a slot on the strip and draws nothing. Register it under an id such as `'empty'` and weight it heavily, and most cells land blank. Hold & Win boards use it for the empty cells between coins.

Live demo (empty-symbol): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/symbols/#emptysymbol-render-nothing-for-a-registered-id

#### Prototype symbols

##### Cards without art

`CardSymbol` draws a coloured card with a label using `Graphics`, so it needs no assets and stays sharp at any cell size. The package exports it with a ready deck: `import { CardSymbol, CARD_DECK, WILD_CARD } from 'pixi-reels'`. Use it for prototypes and tests, and ship `SpriteSymbol`, `AnimatedSpriteSymbol` or `SpineSymbol` in the game.

Live demo (card-symbol-debug): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/symbols/#cardsymbol-debug--prototyping-helper

##### Phase colours

`PhaseCardSymbol` is a `CardSymbol` that is grey at rest and takes the colour of the phase its reel is in: sky for `start`, blue for `spin`, amber for `anticipation`, violet for `stop`, and green for a moment after landing. Use it to check phase timing by eye.

Register it like any symbol, then call `PhaseCardSymbol.watch(reelSet.reels)`. The watcher colours every card from the reels' `phase:enter`, `landed` and `symbol:created` events, custom phases included, and returns a function that stops it. A card does not know its reel, so without the watcher it stays grey. `setPhase()` is public if something else knows the phase. `colors` overrides or extends `PHASE_CARD_COLORS`, and a phase with no entry uses `other`.

Live demo (phase-colors): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/symbols/#phasecardsymbol-read-the-phase-off-the-board

#### Sideways sets

##### Writing a symbol class

A hand-written `ReelSymbol` on a horizontal set with wide cells. The class has no orientation code. `resize(width, height)` is in screen pixels whichever way the strip travels, so the plate's marker and glyph stay upright while the strip scrolls along x. The engine never rotates a symbol container, so third-party symbol classes work unchanged.

A symbol can read `this.mainAxis` (`'y'` vertical, `'x'` horizontal) for effects that follow travel, such as motion blur. Do not use it for layout.

Live demo (symbols-horizontal-resize): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/symbols/#authoring-a-symbol-for-a-sideways-set

##### One registration for both axes

Four reels of three cells, built once vertical and once horizontal, landing the same grid. Both sets use the same symbol registration. The builds differ only in `symbolSize`, whose two numbers swap, because a horizontal board is the vertical one transposed.

Live demo (symbols-transposed-pair): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/symbols/#the-same-symbols-on-both-axes

### Wilds and mystery symbols
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/
Wilds that stay, spread or walk between spins, and mystery symbols that all turn into the same one.
Tags: wild, sticky, multiplier, mystery, respin, cell-pin, horizontal, reverse, orientation

A pin keeps one cell on one symbol id across spins. Sticky, expanding and
walking wilds are all pins, and so are multiplier overlays and mystery
reveals. A pin works with any symbol class.

```ts
// Pin a cell. The id resolves through the SymbolFactory, like normal placement.
const pin = reelSet.pin(reel, cell, 'sticky-wild', { turns: 'permanent' });

// Move it to another cell with a tween.
await reelSet.movePin({ reel, cell }, { reel: reel - 1, cell }, { duration: 600 });

// Release it.
reelSet.unpin(reel, cell);
```

#### What a pin guarantees

- The cell shows the pinned symbol for as long as the pin exists.
- The pin survives `spin()`, `setResult()` and `setShape()`. While the reel
  spins, an overlay symbol holds the cell and the reel scrolls underneath it.
- On a MultiWays reshape the pin moves by its `migration` policy. With
  `'origin'` it returns to the cell it started on when the reel grows back.
  With `'frozen'` it clamps and forgets where it started.
- Pins and nudges do not mix. `spin`, `setResult`, `pin` and `setShape`
  all throw while a `nudge()` is in flight.

The [CellPin reference](/api/interfaces/index.CellPin/) has the full type.

#### Three symbol instances

One pin can be three different symbol instances at three different moments.
All three come from the pool and all three go through `onActivate(symbolId)`.

| Instance | When it exists | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Reel-cell symbol | At rest, idle or landed | `reel.container` inside `viewport.maskedContainer` |
| Overlay symbol | During a spin, one per active pin | `viewport.unmaskedContainer`, zIndex 10000 |
| Flight symbol | During a `movePin` tween | `viewport.unmaskedContainer` |

For a plain sticky cell this does not matter. It matters once you animate
the pinned symbol while the reel moves, because the three are separate
objects and animation state does not carry from one to the next.

#### Lifecycle

```
pin(reel, cell, 'wild', { turns: 'permanent' })
  The reel cell gets a fresh symbol from the SymbolFactory; onActivate runs.
  fires pin:placed(pin)

spin() begins
  For each active pin, an overlay symbol is acquired, positioned at the pin's
  cell, and added to unmaskedContainer.
  fires pin:overlayCreated(pin, overlay)   <- set the overlay animation here

  The reel scrolls underneath. The overlay is what the player sees.

spin lands
  fires pin:overlayDestroyed(pin, overlay) <- stop animations here
  The overlay goes back to the pool. The reel-cell symbol takes over.

movePin(from, to, opts)
  A flight symbol is acquired, positioned at `from`, added to unmaskedContainer.
  opts.onFlightCreated(flight) fires       <- start a motion animation here

  GSAP tweens the flight's world coordinates from source to destination.

  opts.onFlightCompleted(flight) fires     <- restore an idle animation here
  The reel cell at the destination is updated, the flight is released.
  fires pin:moved(newPin, oldCoord)

unpin(reel, cell)  (or the pin expires after `turns: N`)
  fires pin:expired(pin, reason)
```

#### Sprite symbol example

```ts
import { ReelSetBuilder, SpriteSymbol } from 'pixi-reels';

const reelSet = new ReelSetBuilder()
  .reels(5).visibleCells(3).symbolSize(140, 140)
  .symbols((r) => {
    r.register('wild', SpriteSymbol, { textures: { wild: wildTex } });
    // ...
  })
  .ticker(app.ticker)
  .build();

// Spin once, land, then pin a permanent wild at (2, 1).
const spin = reelSet.spin();      // do not await here: spin() does not
reelSet.setResult([/* ... */]);   // resolve until the result arrives
await spin;
reelSet.pin(2, 1, 'wild', { turns: 'permanent' });

// The next spin scrolls underneath the pinned wild.
await reelSet.spin();
```

Sprite symbols need no extra wiring. The pin creates the overlay, moves the
cell on a reshape, and cleans up on unpin.

#### Spine animation hooks

With Spine symbols, each of the three instances above runs its own
animation track. To show an `idle-sticky` track on the overlay and a `run`
track on the flight, set them from the pin lifecycle events.

The built-in `SpineSymbol` sets its `idle` and `win` tracks internally. A
walking wild needs a small subclass that exposes track control:

```ts
import { SpineSymbol, type SpineSymbolOptions } from 'pixi-reels';

export class WalkingSpineSymbol extends SpineSymbol {
  constructor(options: SpineSymbolOptions) {
    super(options);
  }

  /** Publicly swap the current animation track. */
  setAnimation(name: string, loop = true): void {
    const spine = (this as any)._spine;
    if (!spine) return;
    if (!spine.skeleton.data.findAnimation(name)) return;
    spine.state.setAnimation(0, name, loop);
  }
}
```

Then wire the hooks:

```ts
// Overlay: sticky idle while the reel spins underneath
reelSet.events.on('pin:overlayCreated', (_pin, overlay) => {
  (overlay as WalkingSpineSymbol).setAnimation('idle-sticky', true);
});

// Flight: run animation during movePin
async function walkLeft(pin: CellPin) {
  await reelSet.movePin(
    { reel: pin.reel, cell: pin.cell },
    { reel: pin.reel - 1, cell: pin.cell },
    {
      duration: 600,
      onFlightCreated: (flight) => {
        (flight as WalkingSpineSymbol).setAnimation('run', true);
      },
      onFlightCompleted: (flight) => {
        (flight as WalkingSpineSymbol).setAnimation('idle', true);
      },
    },
  );
}
```

The flight symbol is a fresh instance from the pool, not the reel-cell
symbol. Whatever you set on the cell (a track, a tint, a skin) is not on the
flight. The flight starts from what `onActivate` gives it, so set its
animation in `onFlightCreated` as above.

The overlay's animation does not carry over to the landed cell either. When
the reel lands, the overlay is released and the reel-cell symbol shows
whatever its own `onActivate` set, which is plain `idle`. If the landed cell
should keep the sticky animation, set it on the reel cell when the pin is
placed:

```ts
reelSet.events.on('pin:placed', (pin) => {
  if (reelSet.isSpinning) return; // the overlay handles it during a spin
  const sym = reelSet.getReel(pin.reel).getSymbolAt(pin.cell);
  (sym as WalkingSpineSymbol).setAnimation?.('idle-sticky', true);
});
```

An error thrown inside `onFlightCreated` or `onFlightCompleted` does not
stop the move. The engine catches it and reports it on the notice channel as
`pin-hook-threw`. The tween still runs, the pin moves and the flight symbol
is released, so a bug in animation code does not leave the pin half moved.

Every pooled symbol gets `resize(cellWidth, cellHeight)` when it is acquired.
For a Spine symbol that computes a scale from the skeleton's bounds. If the
skeleton data has not loaded yet, the first frame can show a zero-sized
symbol. Once the pool is warm the skeleton is normally ready. If a pinned
symbol pops in size, check this first.

#### Related

- [Walking wild](/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#walking-wild-pin), the movePin pattern above as a demo
- [Sticky wild](/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#sticky-wild-pin), the smallest pin
- [Expanding wild](/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#expanding-wild-pin), one pin per cell of a reel
- [Symbols](/mechanics/symbols/#concept), writing your own symbol class
- [Spin lifecycle](/mechanics/skip/#concept), the events around a spin

##### Demos

Most of these demos are built on a pin. You pin a cell once and the engine draws the pinned symbol over the spinning reel, counts down its turns and removes it when they run out. The wilds come first, then multipliers, held wins and mystery reveals.

#### Wilds

##### Sticky wild

The smallest pin. When a wild lands, pin its cell with `turns: N`. The engine keeps it on screen while the reel spins underneath and counts the turns down, so there are no extra sprites to manage and nothing to write into the next result grid.

Live demo (sticky-wild-pin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#sticky-wild-cellpin

##### Expanding wild

A wild lands and the whole reel turns wild for N spins. The pins expire on their own when the turn counter reaches zero.

Live demo (expanding-wild-pin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#expanding-wild-pin

##### Walking wild

A wild moves one reel left on each spin with `reelSet.movePin()`. The flight hooks are where a Spine symbol switches to its run animation.

Move pins one at a time with `await`, not with `Promise.all`. Two pins moving to the same cell throws.

Live demo (walking-wild-pin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#walking-wild-movepin

#### Multipliers

##### Multiplier wild

Each wild carries its own multiplier in the pin payload. A badge with the value sits over the cell, and the win evaluation reads `pin.payload.multiplier`.

Live demo (multiplier-wild-pin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#multiplier-wild-pin

##### Positional multiplier cells

The multiplier belongs to the cell, not the symbol. Any symbol that lands on a marked cell boosts the wins that pass through it.

Live demo (positional-multiplier-pin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#positional-multiplier-pin

#### Sticky win respin

Winning symbols lock for N respins while the rest of the grid spins. Pinning a cell that is already pinned resets its counter, so each new win restarts the window.

Live demo (sticky-win-respin-pin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#sticky-win-respin-pin

#### Mystery symbols

##### Mystery reveal

Mystery symbols land, then all of them turn into the same random symbol. The reveal uses `'eval'` pins, which clear themselves on the next spin.

Live demo (mystery-reveal-pin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#mystery-reveal-cellpin

##### Animated swap

`setSymbolAt` swaps a symbol at once. `swapSymbols` plays the old symbols out, swaps them, holds, and plays the new ones in, with a stagger on each side.

```ts
await reelSet.swapSymbols(
  [0, 1, 2].map((cell) => ({ reel: 1, cell, id: 'WILD' })),
  { outDelay: (_, i) => i * 0.06, holdMs: 200, inDelay: (_, i) => i * 0.09 },
);
```

It also handles the details a hand-written reveal tends to miss. It raises the zIndex so an entrance that overshoots its cell is not clipped by the next cell, and it hides the new symbol after the swap, because re-activation resets `alpha` to 1 and the new art would show for a frame before its entrance.

Each step can be left out. Pass `skipOut` when the art plays its own Spine `out` track, `skipIn` to leave the cells hidden and reveal them yourself, and `onSwapped` for a step in the middle that has to wait for an animation. `playIn()` and `playOut()` are the per-symbol hooks underneath, on the same contract as `playDestroy`. Override them for entrances and exits that suit your art.

Cells are checked before anything starts, and an abort still performs the swap, so the board always matches the result. It works only at rest and only on single-cell symbols. A big symbol covers cells the frame layer reserves, so revealing one is a `setResult` or `setShape` job.

Live demo (symbol-swap-reveal): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#reveal-a-mystery-symbol-out-swap-in

##### Spine mystery reveal

Mystery bushes land and burst. A Spine overlay plays the reveal while `activate()` swaps the symbol underneath, so the player never sees the swap.

Live demo (spine-mystery-reveal): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#reveal-a-mystery-symbol-out-swap-in

#### Other reel directions

Pins are in index space, so the pin code does not change when the reels run sideways or upward.

##### Expanding wild sideways

The expanding wild on `.orientation('horizontal')`. The code is the same as above. The expansion fills a screen row instead of a column.

Live demo (wilds-horizontal-expanding): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#expanding-wild-on-a-horizontal-set

##### Sticky wilds on reels that spin up

A `.direction('reverse')` set. The reels travel upward through three respins while the pinned wilds hold their cells, and new wilds that land on the way stick too.

Pin coordinates are geometric. Cell 0 is the top cell whichever edge the strip feeds from.

Live demo (wilds-reverse-sticky-respin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/mechanics/wilds-and-pins/#sticky-wilds-on-a-roll-up-respin

## Learn

### Cheats & testing
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/learn/cheats-and-testing/
Force outcomes with cheats and run full spins in Node, so mechanic tests give the same result every run.

pixi-reels is built so you can test mechanics without a canvas. Two tools
make that possible.

- `createTestReelSet` builds a headless reel set wired to a `FakeTicker`. No renderer, no DOM.
- `CheatEngine`, in the private `@pixi-reels/cheats` package, is a pluggable outcome source. It forces grids, scatters, lines and cascades on demand.

Together they let you assert things like "this mechanic produces exactly
3 scatters, triggers anticipation on reel 5, and emits `spin:complete`."

#### 1. Headless reel set

```ts
import { createTestReelSet, expectGrid } from 'pixi-reels/testing';

const { reelSet, spinAndLand, destroy } = createTestReelSet({
  reels: 5,
  visibleCells: 3,
  symbolIds: ['cherry', 'seven', 'wild', 'scatter'],
});

await spinAndLand([
  { visible: ['wild','wild','wild'] },
  { visible: ['wild','wild','wild'] },
  { visible: ['wild','wild','wild'] },
  { visible: ['wild','wild','wild'] },
  { visible: ['wild','wild','wild'] },
]);

expectGrid(reelSet, /* same 5x3 grid of 'wild' */);
destroy();
```

`spinAndLand()` calls `spin()`, then `setResult()`, then `slamStop()`. That
bypasses all timing and resolves on a microtask, which suits CI. Note that
`slamStop()` lands every reel outright. It does not go through the two-stage
`skipSpin()` boost.

#### 2. Force outcomes with cheats

Cheats are pure functions that take a context and return a grid.

```ts
import { CheatEngine, forceScatters, forceLine, holdAndWinProgress } from '@pixi-reels/cheats';

const engine = new CheatEngine({
  reelCount: 5, visibleCells: 3,
  symbolIds: ['a', 'b', 'scatter', 'coin'],
  seed: 42,
});

engine.register({
  id: 'scat3',
  label: 'Force 3 scatters',
  enabled: true,
  cheat: forceScatters(3, 'scatter'),
});

const { symbols, anticipationReels } = engine.next();
await spinAndLand(symbols.map((visible) => ({ visible })));
```

##### Built-in cheats

| Cheat | Effect |
|---|---|
| `forceGrid(grid)` | Every spin returns this exact grid. |
| `forceLine(cellIndex, id)` | Fills one cell index across every reel with `id`. |
| `forceScatters(n, id)` | Places exactly `n` of `id` at random cells. |
| `forceNearMiss(n, id, nearReel)` | `n-1` scatters, none on `nearReel`. Triggers anticipation there. |
| `forceCell(reel, cell, id)` | Places `id` at `[reel, cell]`. |
| `holdAndWinProgress(coinId, p)` | Keeps held coins, adds one new coin with probability `p`. |
| `cascadeSequence([g1, g2, ...])` | Emits grids in order. |
| `forceAnticipation(reels)` | Sets anticipation reels without constraining symbols. |

##### Write your own

A cheat is `(ctx) => { symbols, anticipationReels, meta } | null`. Returning
`null` passes the spin through, so the next cheat or the RNG handles it.

```ts
const forcePairWild: Cheat = (ctx) => {
  const grid = /* random grid */;
  grid[2][1] = 'wild';
  grid[3][1] = 'wild';
  return { symbols: grid, anticipationReels: [] };
};
```

#### 3. Assert events fired correctly

```ts
import { captureEvents } from 'pixi-reels/testing';

const log = captureEvents(reelSet, ['spin:start', 'spin:complete']);
await spinAndLand(grid);   // grid is ColumnTarget[]
expect(log.map((e) => e.event)).toEqual(['spin:start', 'spin:complete']);
```

#### 4. See a mechanic running

The standalone demo apps left this repo in 2.0 and live in a separate one.
The live, replayable mechanics are the [recipes](/mechanics/) on this site.
Each page runs the source it shows, so you can read the wiring and watch it
land.

### Debugging
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/learn/debugging/
Snapshot the reel state as JSON, render an ASCII grid, trace every event.

PixiJS draws to a canvas, so AI agents and automated tooling cannot see the
reels. For that, pixi-reels ships three utilities: `debugSnapshot`,
`debugGrid` and `enableDebug`. They return data only and live in the main entry.

Drawing the same state on the canvas (cell geometry, a per-reel hud, a metrics
plaque and a phase timeline for every spin) is the job of the `pixi-reels/debug`
subpath, described [further down](#the-visual-overlay).

#### One-liner: attach to window

```ts
import { enableDebug } from 'pixi-reels';
enableDebug(reelSet);
// window.__PIXI_REELS_DEBUG is now live
```

In Node, `enableDebug` does nothing. It checks `typeof window` and returns.

In the browser devtools console:

```js
__PIXI_REELS_DEBUG.log();
// [pixi-reels debug] spinning=false speed=normal
```

```js
const stop = __PIXI_REELS_DEBUG.trace();  // logs every event on the set bus from now on
stop();                                    // and stops

__PIXI_REELS_DEBUG.metrics();
// { rounds: [{ index: 1, profile: 'normal', duration: 2310, landOrder: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4],
//              reels: [{ phases: [{ phase: 'start', start: 0, end: 212 }, ...],
//                        stoppingAt: 820, landedAt: 1204, tease: null, ... }, ...],
//              skips: [], ... }],
//   totals: { rounds: 1, skipped: 0, averageDuration: 2310 } }
```

`metrics()` covers every spin since `enableDebug` was called. For each reel it
records when each phase started and ended, when the reel was asked to stop,
when it landed, and its tease window. For each round it records every skip
press, the landing order, and how many symbols were swapped into cells. Times
are in ms since the round's `spin:start`. It is the text half of the timeline
described below.

`trace()` is `reelSet.events.onAny(...)` with a `console.log` inside. The same
hook exists on every bus, and `onNotice` does the same for engine notices.

```ts
import { onNotice } from 'pixi-reels';

reelSet.events.onAny((event, ...args) => log.push({ event, args }));
reelSet.reels[4].events.onAny((event, info) => {
  if (event === 'phase:step') console.log(info); // { phase: 'stop', step: 'delay', status: 'cut' }
});
const off = onNotice(({ kind, code, message }) => telemetry.note(kind, code, message));
```

#### The events panel on the recipes site

Every live demo on this site has a Debug button under the canvas. It opens
the demo in Studio with debug on, at `/studio/#code=...&debug=1`. Studio is a
full-viewport workbench: the recipe's code on the left, the reels in the
middle, and the events panel on the right while debug is on. The panel lists
every event that every reel set, reel and board in the demo raised, as it
happens, with a timestamp relative to the round's `spin:start`. The payload
is unwrapped under the event, one member per line. The filter takes words and
`!words`, for example `skip !symbol:created`. Pause freezes the view while the
recorder keeps going. Copy puts the visible rows on the clipboard as JSON.
Engine notices show up as `notice` rows.

On a recipe that returns a reel set, Studio also draws the overlay described
below on it, with a toggle per group of layers: `info` (hud, metrics,
timeline), `grid` (mask, cells, blocks, pins), `motion` (axis, feed, buffers,
thresholds) and `bounds`.

#### Programmatic snapshot

```ts
import { debugSnapshot, debugGrid } from 'pixi-reels';

const snap = debugSnapshot(reelSet);
// snap: { timestamp, isSpinning, currentSpeed, availableSpeeds, spotlightActive,
//         reelCount, visibleCells, reels: [...], grid: [[...], ...] }

console.log(debugGrid(reelSet));   // ASCII table
```

`debugGrid` returns plain text, so you can log it, assert against it or paste
it anywhere.

The snapshot shapes are typed as `DebugSnapshot` and `DebugReelSnapshot`. They
contain no PixiJS objects, so `JSON.stringify()` always works, and they survive
`structuredClone` and `postMessage` without losing anything.

#### Using snapshots in tests

When `expectGrid()` fails, the test harness puts a snapshot into the error
message for you.

```
Grid mismatch:
  reel 0 cell 1: expected "seven" got "cherry"

Current grid:
```

#### Recording sessions

When a bug only reproduces across a whole spin, record it and read the
sequence back offline.

Recording is driven by events rather than frames. `startRecording` listens for
`spin:start`, `spin:reelLanded`, `spin:allLanded` and `spin:complete`, and
captures a snapshot at each. It also detaches itself when the reel set emits
`destroyed`. A spin yields a handful of frames.

```ts
import { startRecording, stopRecording, getFrames, clearFrames } from 'pixi-reels';

startRecording(reelSet, 'spin-1');   // (reelSet, tag?, { maxFrames? })
await reelSet.spin();
reelSet.setResult([/* ... */]);
await /* the spin */;
stopRecording(reelSet);

const frames = getFrames('spin-1');  // RecordedFrame[]
console.log(`captured ${frames.length} frames`);
clearFrames();
```

Each `RecordedFrame` is `{ tag, trigger, snapshot }`: the tag you passed,
the event name that triggered the capture, and the `DebugSnapshot`. The
timestamp lives inside `snapshot`.

Two things to know about the buffer.

- It is shared by the whole process and is not cleared between sessions, so
  a bare `getFrames()` returns every take since the page loaded. Pass the tag.
- It is a rolling window of 1000 frames by default (`maxFrames`). A long
  session drops the oldest frames without telling you.

#### The visual overlay

`debugSnapshot` tells you what the engine thinks. `debugOverlay` draws it on
top of the canvas, so you can see whether the picture agrees. It lives at the
`pixi-reels/debug` subpath and draws with
[pixi-silk](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev), an optional peer dependency that
renders every shape as an exact distance field, so a 1px outline stays a clean
1px line at whatever scale the reel set is fitted to.

```bash
pnpm add -D pixi-silk
```

```ts
import { debugOverlay } from 'pixi-reels/debug';

const overlay = debugOverlay(reelSet, {
  layers: ['cells', 'hud', 'timeline'],  // or 'all'
  live: true,                            // redraw each tick; false = follow the spin events
  ticker: app.ticker,                    // drive the live redraw off your ticker
});

overlay.setLayers(['cells', 'pins']);
overlay.redraw();
overlay.destroy();
```

A build that never imports `pixi-reels/debug` never needs `pixi-silk`. The
overlay draws through WebGL. On a WebGPU renderer its shapes draw nothing, so
debug on `app.init({ preference: 'webgl' })`. Building one in a headless test
needs a canvas stand-in; the [4.0 migration guide](/reference/migrating-to-4-0/)
has it.

| Layer | Draws | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| `mask` | Mask box and per-reel rects | Pyramid peek; a mask strategy clipping on the wrong axis |
| `cells` | Every visible cell, with `reel,cell` labels | Off-by-one in cell indexing |
| `buffers` | The off-window strip cells, dimmer | Buffer targets and big-symbol tails, which are otherwise invisible |
| `axis` | One arrow per reel, pointing the way it travels | A reverse direction or a horizontal orientation, at a glance |
| `feed` | The edge new symbols arrive at | Confirms `feedEdge` follows from the direction |
| `thresholds` | The wrap lines | A symbol drawn past one |
| `bounds` | Real `view.getBounds()` per symbol | Spine overrun past its cell |
| `blocks` | `getBlockBounds` outline for big symbols | 2x2 anchors, and block/screen transposition |
| `pins` | Pin cells and pin-overlay positions | A pin overlay drifting off its cell |
| `hud` | A row per reel, `r0 VF feed=start spd=0.0 idle cells=3`, with a phase swatch and a speed meter | Reading state without opening the console |
| `metrics` | A plaque under the mask for the current round: its length, time to the first stop, landing order and the largest gap, tease windows, the last skip press, symbols built, events, fps | Why a spin felt slow, in numbers |
| `timeline` | Every reel's phases for the round on one time axis, the speed trace on top, a tick at the stop request, a dot at the landing, a dashed line per skip press | Stagger, tease holds and a slam that cut a stop short, as shapes |

The overlay draws into the `ReelSet` itself, so it renders above the viewport
and above the spotlight container. The geometry and the hud stay inside the
mask. `metrics` and `timeline` sit under it, side by side when the set is wide
enough, so they add to the reel set's bounds. Fit your camera after enabling
them. The overlay is dev-only. It reads internals, it is not semver-protected,
and it must not reach a production bundle.

##### How to read the timeline

Each lane is one reel. The colored blocks are its phases, in the colors
`PhaseCardSymbol` paints: sky for `start`, blue for `spin`, amber for
`anticipation`, violet for `stop`. The white line on top is `speedNormalized`,
so a surge-then-crawl tease shows as a bump and a slope. The white tick is when
the controller asked the reel to stop, the green dot is when it came to rest,
and the amber underline is its tease window. A red dashed line is a slam press,
a yellow one a quicken. While the round runs, a cursor marks now.

##### Recording from the start

The `metrics` and `timeline` layers read a `SpinMetrics`. By default the
overlay starts its own, so they show the rounds from the moment it was
created. To see the spin before that, keep a recorder running and hand it
over.

```ts
import { SpinMetrics, debugOverlay } from 'pixi-reels/debug';

const metrics = new SpinMetrics(reelSet, { ticker: app.ticker }); // at boot
// ... later, when something looks wrong:
debugOverlay(reelSet, { layers: ['timeline', 'metrics'], live: true, ticker: app.ticker, metrics });
```

`metrics.current` is the latest round, `metrics.rounds` the last 20, and
`metrics.snapshot()` a plain-JSON copy. Without a `ticker` it still records
every event-driven time; the ticker adds the speed trace. It lets go of the
buses when the reel set is destroyed.

##### DebugPlaque

Every panel is built from this plate, and it is exported for your own
readouts. It shows rows of monospace text on a smooth rounded plate, with an
optional title, swatches for a legend, and meters for a speed or a progress.
It sizes itself from the character count, so it is exact without measuring
text and cheap to update every frame.

```ts
import { DebugPlaque } from 'pixi-reels/debug';

const hud = new DebugPlaque({ text: 'press spin', minWidth: gridWidth });
hud.position.set(0, gridHeight + 10);
reelSet.addChild(hud);

hud.text = `landed ${count} reels`;             // like a Text
hud.update({ rows: [{ text: 'spin', swatch: 0x2563eb, meter: reel.speedNormalized }] });
```

`minWidth` and `reserveRows` fix its size up front, and `maxWidth` wraps long
rows, so a readout never outgrows a camera that was fitted to it once.

Every status line, label and legend in the recipes on this site is one of
these. Its companion for dashed boxes is `roundRectPath(g, x, y, w, h, r)`.
pixi-silk dashes paths but strokes `roundRect` solid, so this helper traces the
box as one path. A following `.stroke({ dash: [7, 5] })` then dashes it round
the corners.

##### The overlay as data

A canvas is opaque to CI and to AI agents, and a screenshot loses some of what
the overlay draws anyway. A travel arrow pointing up has the same bounding box
as one pointing down. So the overlay also hands back plain JSON.

```ts
const info = debugOverlay(reelSet, { layers: 'all' }).describe();
// info.round is the round the metrics and timeline panels show, as plain JSON

info.reels[0];
// {
//   reel: 0,
//   orientation: 'vertical', direction: 'reverse', feedEdge: 'end',
//   axisArrow: { fromMain: 249.6, toMain: 62.4 },   // signed: to - from is the direction
//   feedMain: 187.2,
//   thresholds: { start: -124.8, end: 249.6 },
//   visibleCells: 3,
//   phase: 'idle',
// }
```

The signed span of `axisArrow` is the assertion worth making. It is the one
thing that tells a reverse reel from a forward one, and a bounding box cannot
see it.

#### Console notices

Separate from the debug tooling above, the library talks to you through one
channel, for things a developer should act on: a call that will not do what
you meant, a hook of yours that threw, a value that had to be clamped. It
never reports per-frame state, and nothing in it runs in the hot path.

Every notice carries a stable code, so you can grep for it, search for it in
these docs, or quote it in a bug report.

```
pixi-reels  quicken-cascade      requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken' }) has nothing to quicken in
                                 cascade mode: a tumble reel lands by placing its symbols...
```

##### Levels

One knob, four settings. Each level includes the ones before it.

| Level | Prints | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| `'info'` | everything | The default. Advisory notices (the mask-strategy auto-pick, warp/unmask caveats) plus every problem. |
| `'warn'` | errors + warnings | You have read the advisories and want them out of the way, but still want to hear about problems. |
| `'error'` | errors only | Something the library could not do, and recovered from. Nothing else. |
| `'silent'` | nothing | Production, once you have read the warnings at least once. |

```ts
import { setLogLevel, getLogLevel } from 'pixi-reels';

setLogLevel('silent');
getLogLevel(); // 'silent'
```

The default is `'info'` rather than something quieter because several
notices, the mask-strategy auto-pick in particular, used to print
unconditionally. A quieter default would have removed advice the engine had
always given, without telling anyone.

##### What it looks like where

In a browser a notice renders as a styled badge: a `pixi-reels` pill, then the
code, then the message. Everywhere else (Node, a test runner, CI) `%c` styling
does not exist and the console would print the style directives literally, so
the notice degrades to a plain line.

```
[pixi-reels] warn(quicken-cascade) requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken' }) has nothing to quicken...
```

Notices go out on `console.warn`, `console.error` and `console.info` rather
than through one `console.log`. That keeps devtools level filtering, stack
capture and the browser's own warn/error styling working. Any extra detail is
passed straight through, so an `Error` argument keeps its stack instead of
being stringified.

A few notices fire only once per process (`buffer-clamped`, for instance), so a
builder constructed in a loop cannot flood the console.

The full list of codes lives in the [events reference](/reference/api-events/).

#### The DEFAULTS constant

`DEFAULTS`, exported from `pixi-reels`, holds five of the engine's defaults:
`bufferSymbols`, `symbolGap`, `initialSpeed`, `maxPoolPerKey` and `zIndexStep`.
Read it when you want to set a value relative to one of those, for example
`builder.bufferSymbols(DEFAULTS.bufferSymbols + 2)`. Other defaults live with
the feature that owns them: tumble's in `TumbleConfig`, stacking and pin
migration on the builder.

### Getting started
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/learn/getting-started/
Install pixi-reels and get a 5x3 reel set spinning in a PixiJS v8 app.

pixi-reels is a reel engine for a PixiJS v8 app. You add it to the stage like any other container.

#### You need

- Node 20 or newer, and pnpm, npm or yarn
- A PixiJS v8 app. The engine runs off `app.ticker`
- For Spine symbols, `@esotericsoftware/spine-pixi-v8` as well

#### Install

```bash
pnpm add pixi-reels pixi.js gsap
# only if you want Spine symbols
pnpm add @esotericsoftware/spine-pixi-v8
```

#### Boot Pixi, build a ReelSet

```ts
import { Application } from 'pixi.js';
import { ReelSetBuilder, SpriteSymbol } from 'pixi-reels';
import { cherryTex, sevenTex, barTex } from './textures';

const app = new Application();
await app.init({ width: 900, height: 540, background: '#0a0d14' });
document.body.appendChild(app.canvas);

const reelSet = new ReelSetBuilder()
  .reels(5)
  .visibleCells(3)
  .symbolSize(140, 140)
  .symbols((r) => {
    r.register('cherry', SpriteSymbol, { textures: { cherry: cherryTex } });
    r.register('seven',  SpriteSymbol, { textures: { seven: sevenTex } });
    r.register('bar',    SpriteSymbol, { textures: { bar: barTex } });
  })
  .weights({ cherry: 40, seven: 10, bar: 20 })
  .ticker(app.ticker)
  .build();

app.stage.addChild(reelSet);

const result = await reelSet.spin();
console.log(result.symbols);
```

#### Did it work

The reels spin, then stop on three rows of random symbols.

If nothing happened, it is usually one of these.

| You see | Do this |
|---|---|
| Blank canvas | Set `reelSet.x` and `reelSet.y`. The set sits at (0,0) until you move it. |
| `ticker() must be called` | Add `.ticker(app.ticker)` to the builder. |
| Symbols invisible | The texture never loaded, or `symbolSize()` does not match your art. The engine calls `resize()` on every symbol swap. |

#### Where next

- [Your first reelset](/learn/your-first-reelset/) builds a real slot step by step
- [Spin lifecycle](/mechanics/skip/#concept) explains the spin API
- [Cheats & testing](/learn/cheats-and-testing/) shows how to test a mechanic
- [Recipes](/mechanics/) shows what the engine can do

### Recipe previews
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/learn/recipe-previews/
How to give a recipe a card thumbnail and inline body images. Drop a file in public/; a missing one falls back to a generated placeholder.

Every card on the recipes index and every topic page can carry preview media: a gif, an animated webp, a static screenshot, or a short clip. Nothing is required. Drop a file in the right place and it shows up. Anything missing renders a generated placeholder built from the title, so the index and the pages always look finished.

#### Card thumbnails

Each card on the [/mechanics/](/mechanics/) grid is one topic page, and it shows a 16:10 thumbnail. The card looks for its media in this order.

1. A hand-drawn cover for the slug, from `components/recipes-index/covers.ts`. Every topic page has one at the moment, so the index shows these.
2. An explicit `image` path from the topic page's frontmatter, if that file exists under `public/`. See [Non-conventional paths](#non-conventional-paths).
3. A file at the conventional path.
4. The generated placeholder.

The conventional path is:

```
public/recipes/<slug>/card.<ext>
```

where `<slug>` is the topic page's file name under `src/content/recipes/`, which is also its URL. There is no registry to edit. The card picks the file up on the next build.

Supported extensions, in priority order:

```
gif  webp  avif  png  jpg  jpeg  mp4  webm
```

Animated formats win over static ones, so if both `card.gif` and `card.png` exist, the gif is used. `mp4` and `webm` render as a muted, looping, autoplaying `<video>`. The image is `object-cover`, so any source proportion works, but compose for about 16:10 so nothing important sits where the crop bites.

When nothing is found, the card shows a placeholder: a tinted faux-reel board with a monogram from the title. The same title always gives the same tint, so the grid stays varied rather than blank.

#### Inline body images

Inside a topic page's MDX body, use the `Image` component for figures (it is `RecipeImage.astro` under the hood): gifs of a mechanic mid-motion, before and after stills, a frame breakdown. The same component is available on the Learn and Reference pages.

```mdx

<Image
  src="/recipes/hold-and-win-spine/jackpot-reveal.gif"
  alt="A MINI coin lands wearing its tier word, spins, and settles on the gold face"
  caption="The tier reveal, frame by frame"
/>
```

| Prop | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `src` | no | Public URL, e.g. `/recipes/<slug>/foo.gif`. Omit to force a placeholder. |
| `alt` | yes | The accessible name, and the placeholder's caption when `src` is missing. |
| `caption` | no | Figure caption under the media. |
| `ratio` | no | Placeholder box ratio, default `16/10`. Real media uses its own size. |

Add as many as you like. They follow the same rule as cards: if the file exists under `public/`, it renders. If not, you get a placeholder that shows the `alt` text and the exact path to provide, so an unfinished page reads as "art pending here: `public/recipes/x/foo.gif`" and never as a broken image. Write the `alt` as if the image were already there, since it does both jobs.

#### Non-conventional paths

If a card asset lives somewhere other than `public/recipes/<slug>/card.*`, set `image` in the topic page's frontmatter (`src/content/recipes/<slug>.mdx`):

```yaml
image: /shared/my-shared-preview.gif
```

An `image` that points at a real file wins over the conventional lookup. One that points at nothing falls through to the convention, then to the placeholder. A hand-drawn cover still wins over both.

#### Tips

- Keep gifs small. A card is shown at about 370px wide, so an 800px source is plenty. Trim to 2 to 4 seconds and a tight loop. Prefer animated `webp` over `gif` for the same motion at a fraction of the bytes.
- Capture from the live demo. Every recipe ships a runnable demo, so record the canvas region for a 1:1 preview of what the reader will run.
- Compose for the crop. Cards are `object-cover` at 16:10. Center the board and leave a little room around it.
- Use a light background. The site card is light, so export with an opaque light backdrop (or composite onto one) so transparent canvases do not read as gray.

The [Hold & Win](/mechanics/hold-and-win/) page has captured `card.png` files under `public/recipes/` from before the covers existed. The index shows its hand-drawn cover instead. Browse the rest of the [grid](/mechanics/) to see the covers and the placeholder they would fall back to.

### Build your first cascade slot
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/learn/your-first-cascade/
A tutorial that builds a 6x5 cascade slot in about 80 lines of TypeScript, for readers new to pixi-reels.

This tutorial builds a 6x5 cascade slot in about 80 lines of TypeScript. A click drops the symbols in, the game detects 3-in-a-row wins, the winners vanish, new symbols refill from above, and that repeats until there are no more wins. You need no prior `pixi-reels` knowledge. PixiJS basics help.

If you already know `pixi-reels`, skim the [cascades guide](/mechanics/cascade/#concept) for the mental model and the [API reference](/reference/api-reelset/) for the verbs.

#### Step 0. Install

```bash
npm install pixi-reels pixi.js gsap
```

`pixi-reels` requires PixiJS v8 and uses GSAP for its tweens. Both are peer dependencies.

#### Step 1. Boot PixiJS

```ts
import { Application } from 'pixi.js';
import { gsap } from 'gsap';

const app = new Application();
await app.init({ background: 0xffffff, resizeTo: window, antialias: true });
document.body.appendChild(app.canvas);

// Sync GSAP to PixiJS so tweens run in hidden tabs / iframes.
gsap.ticker.remove(gsap.updateRoot);
app.ticker.add(() => gsap.updateRoot(app.ticker.lastTime / 1000));
```

The two GSAP lines are required. Without them GSAP freezes in background tabs and your cascade animations stall mid-drop. See [the GSAP gotcha section in CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-reels/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#known-gotchas).

#### Step 2. Wire the reel set

```ts
import { ReelSetBuilder, SpriteSymbol, SpeedPresets, enableDebug } from 'pixi-reels';

const SYMBOLS = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'wild'];

const reelSet = new ReelSetBuilder()
  .reels(6)
  .visibleCells(5)
  .symbolSize(95, 95)
  .symbolGap(5, 5)
  .symbols((r) => {
    for (const id of SYMBOLS) {
      r.register(id, SpriteSymbol, { textures });  // your loaded sprite textures
    }
  })
  .weights({ A: 18, B: 14, C: 10, D: 6, wild: 2 })
  .speed('normal', SpeedPresets.NORMAL)
  .tumble({
    fall:   { duration: 280, ease: 'sine.in',       cellStagger: 40 },
    dropIn: { duration: 480, ease: 'back.out(1.6)', cellStagger: 50, distance: 'perHole' },
  })
  .ticker(app.ticker)
  .build();

app.stage.addChild(reelSet);
enableDebug(reelSet);   // exposes window.__PIXI_REELS_DEBUG, used in Step 7
```

The `tumble` call switches the default spin mode to cascade and wires the three cascade phases (`cascade:fall`, `cascade:place`, `cascade:dropIn`). Its config is animation parameters only. Multipliers, sound and win clearing are your code, listening to events.

#### Step 3. A fake server

In production you call your real backend. For this tutorial, a function returns a random grid, and a second one returns a cascade refill that follows the gravity convention.

```ts
function randSymbol(): string {
  const weights: Record<string, number> = { A: 18, B: 14, C: 10, D: 6, wild: 2 };
  const total = Object.values(weights).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  let r = Math.random() * total;
  for (const [id, w] of Object.entries(weights)) {
    r -= w;
    if (r <= 0) return id;
  }
  return 'A';
}

import type { Cell } from 'pixi-reels';

const server = {
  spin: async (): Promise<string[][]> => {
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 400 + Math.random() * 600));
    return Array.from({ length: 6 }, () => Array.from({ length: 5 }, randSymbol));
  },

  cascade: async (prev: string[][], winners: Cell[]) => {
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 120));
    const winnersByReel = new Map<number, Set<number>>();
    for (const w of winners) {
      if (!winnersByReel.has(w.reel)) winnersByReel.set(w.reel, new Set());
      winnersByReel.get(w.reel)!.add(w.cell);
    }
    return prev.map((column, reel) => {
      const losers = winnersByReel.get(reel);
      if (!losers || losers.size === 0) return [...column];
      const survivors = column.filter((_, cell) => !losers.has(cell));
      const fillers = Array.from({ length: losers.size }, randSymbol);
      // Convention: top losers.size cells = new, rest = survivors in original order.
      return [...fillers, ...survivors];
    });
  },
};
```

The cascade function follows the [gravity convention](/mechanics/cascade/#refill-geometry-the-survivor-convention). If you have a real server, its response must follow the same convention.

#### Step 4. Detect winners

This is game-rule code. A left-anchored run of 3 or more matching symbols at the same cell index counts as a win, and `wild` matches anything.

```ts
import type { Cell } from 'pixi-reels';

function detectWinners(grid: string[][]): Cell[] {
  const winners: Cell[] = [];
  for (let cell = 0; cell < 5; cell++) {
    const head = grid[0][cell];
    if (head === 'wild') continue;
    let run = 1;
    for (let reel = 1; reel < 6; reel++) {
      if (grid[reel][cell] === head || grid[reel][cell] === 'wild') run++;
      else break;
    }
    if (run >= 3) {
      for (let reel = 0; reel < run; reel++) winners.push({ reel, cell });
    }
  }
  return winners;
}
```

#### Step 5. Drive a round

`runCascade` replaces a hand-rolled `while` loop with one call. It does the following.

1. Calls `detectWinners(grid)` with the current visible grid.
2. If the list is empty, ends the chain and resolves with a `RunCascadeResult` (`{ chainLength, totalWinners, finalGrid, wasSkipped }`).
3. Otherwise fires `cascade:chain:start`, calls `reelSet.destroySymbols(winners)`, then `nextGrid(grid, winners)`, then `reelSet.refill(...)`, then fires `cascade:chain:end`.
4. Loops back to step 1 with the post-refill grid.

It also takes an `AbortSignal`, so a button tap mid-round can end the chain cleanly. Step 6 wires that up, so the signature accepts one from the start.

```ts
async function playRound(signal: AbortSignal): Promise<void> {
  // Moment A: fall, wait, drop in.
  reelSet.setDropOrder('ltr');                  // left-to-right reveal
  const spinDone = reelSet.spin();
  reelSet.setResult((await server.spin()).map((visible) => ({ visible })));
  await spinDone;

  // Moment B: the cascade refill loop. runCascade owns the orchestration;
  // your two callbacks own the game rules.
  reelSet.setDropOrder('all');                  // all columns drop together on refills

  const { chainLength, totalWinners, wasSkipped } = await reelSet.runCascade({
    detectWinners: (grid) => detectWinners(grid),
    nextGrid:      (prev, winners) => server.cascade(prev, winners),
    onCascade:     ({ chain, winners }) => {
      console.log(`cascade ${chain}: ${winners.length} winners`);
    },
    signal,                                     // honors player slam between refills
  });

  console.log(
    `round done: ${chainLength} cascades, ${totalWinners} total winners` +
    (wasSkipped ? ' (slammed)' : ''),
  );
}
```

#### Step 6. Wire the button

```ts
const button = document.createElement('button');
button.textContent = 'SPIN';
button.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;bottom:20px;left:50%;transform:translateX(-50%);padding:16px 32px;font-size:18px;';
document.body.appendChild(button);

let isPlaying = false;
let cascadeAbort: AbortController | null = null;

button.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  if (isPlaying) {
    reelSet.requestSkip();       // slam now, or queue it if the result hasn't landed
    cascadeAbort?.abort();       // end the cascade chain at the next await boundary
    return;
  }
  isPlaying = true;
```
