```ts
  cascadeAbort = new AbortController();
  try {
    await playRound(cascadeAbort.signal);
  } finally {
    cascadeAbort = null;
    isPlaying = false;
  }
});
```

The slam handler does two things, and both are needed.

- `reelSet.requestSkip()` slams the engine's in-flight motion. If `setResult()` has not arrived yet, it queues the press until it does. That window is real here, because the mock server waits 400 to 1000 ms. Use `requestSkip()` rather than `skipSpin()`, which throws when called before the result lands, since there is nothing to land on yet. Both do nothing when the engine is idle.
- `AbortController.abort()` flips a flag that `runCascade` checks at its next await boundary. It works whether the engine is mid-refill or idle.

Together, the engine slams its in-flight motion and the cascade chain ends. See [the cancellation section in the cascades guide](/mechanics/cascade/#cancelling-a-chain-via-abortsignal) for the reasoning.

#### Step 7. Try it

Click SPIN. The reels fall, the reels stay empty during the server round trip (400 to 1000 ms), then new symbols drop in. If `detectWinners` finds a 3-in-a-row, the winners disintegrate and the survivors slide down. That loops until there are no more wins.

Step 2 called `enableDebug(reelSet)`, so the browser console has
`window.__PIXI_REELS_DEBUG.log()`. It prints the visible grid and engine
state, which helps when something looks wrong.

#### What you didn't have to do

Compared with hand-rolling cascades:

- No tween bookkeeping. `tumble({ fall, dropIn })` owns the animation timing.
- No survivor or gravity math. `refill({ winners, grid })` reads the gravity convention from your `grid` and animates the right offsets.
- No "fade then drop" choreography. `destroySymbols` defers to each symbol's `playDestroy()`, and the engine sequences `place` and `dropIn` for you.
- No slam state machine. `skipSpin()` is round-aware, and `wasSkipped` propagates through the chain.

#### Next steps

Now that the slot works:

- Pick a feel. [Tumble feels](/mechanics/cascade/#tumble-feels) shows five preset `tumble({...})` shapes side by side.
- Tune the lead-in, the pause between the SPIN click and the first frame of the fall. See [fall delays](/mechanics/cascade/#fall-delays).
- Add a cascading multiplier by bumping a meter inside `onCascade`. See the [cascade-6x5 recipe](/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-6x5).
- Use Spine symbols with custom disintegration. Your `SpineReelSymbol` subclass overrides `playDestroy()` to play the `out` animation, and everything else stays the same. See [cascade wins: present, destroy, refill](/mechanics/cascade/#cascade-destroy-and-present) for the Spine wiring.
- Spin first, cascade after. Open with a strip-spin landing, then cascade. See [spin then cascade](/mechanics/cascade/#spin-then-cascade).

If you get stuck, read [the cascades guide](/mechanics/cascade/#concept). The mental model is what makes the verbs make sense.

### Your first reelset
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/learn/your-first-reelset/
Build, spin, and react to a reel set from scratch.

This page builds a 5x3 fruit slot from nothing.

#### 0. Before you start

You have a Pixi app already. Install the engine with `npm i pixi-reels`.

#### 1. Make a builder

```ts
import { ReelSetBuilder } from 'pixi-reels';
const builder = new ReelSetBuilder();
```

You configure the builder, then build the reel set from it at the end.

#### 2. Set the grid

```ts
builder
  .reels(5)
  .visibleCells(3)
  .symbolSize(140, 140)
  .symbolGap(4, 4)           // optional
  .bufferSymbols(1);         // optional, default 1
```

Nothing is on screen yet. The builder does nothing until you call `.build()`.

#### 3. Register symbols

Every symbol needs an id and a class. Three classes ship with the engine.

- `SpriteSymbol` draws one static texture
- `AnimatedSpriteSymbol` plays a sprite-sheet animation
- `SpineSymbol` plays a Spine skeleton

For anything else, extend `ReelSymbol` and draw what you like.

```ts
import { SpriteSymbol } from 'pixi-reels';

builder.symbols((r) => {
  r.register('cherry', SpriteSymbol, { textures: { cherry: cherryTex } });
  r.register('seven',  SpriteSymbol, { textures: { seven: sevenTex } });
  r.register('wild',   SpriteSymbol, { textures: { wild: wildTex } });
});
```

If you register nothing, `.build()` throws with `symbols() must register at least one symbol.`

#### 4. Weights, ticker, build

`app` is your Pixi app.

```ts
builder
  .weights({ cherry: 40, seven: 8, wild: 5 })
  .ticker(app.ticker);

const reelSet = builder.build();
app.stage.addChild(reelSet);
```

You now see a 5x3 grid of random symbols, standing still.

Real slots do not open on random symbols. They open on a chosen frame, or on
whatever the player left behind last round. Set that with `initialFrame`.

```ts
builder.initialFrame([
  { visible: ['cherry', 'seven', 'cherry'] },
  { visible: ['wild', 'cherry', 'seven'] },
  { visible: ['seven', 'seven', 'cherry'] },
  { visible: ['cherry', 'wild', 'cherry'] },
  { visible: ['seven', 'cherry', 'cherry'] },
])
```

It takes buffer symbols too, if you want something peeking in from off-window.

#### 5. Spin

```ts
const promise = reelSet.spin();
```

The reels spin and keep spinning.

Do not call this straight from a button click. Call it from the state that
opens a round and sends the server request. The button starts a round, and the
round starts the reels.

#### 6. Stop

The spin promise does not resolve on its own. It waits until you say what to
land on.

```ts
const promise = reelSet.spin();

reelSet.setResult([
  { visible: ['wild','seven','wild'] },
  { visible: ['seven','wild','seven'] },
  { visible: ['wild','seven','wild'] },
  { visible: ['seven','wild','seven'] },
  { visible: ['wild','seven','wild'] },
]);

await promise;
```

The reels stop and show your grid.

The classic mistake is `await reelSet.spin()` on its own. It never resolves,
because nothing told it where to stop. Hold the promise, set the result,
then await.

#### What next

* React to events: [Spin lifecycle](/mechanics/skip/#concept)
* Go faster: [Speed modes](/mechanics/feel/#concept-speed-modes)
* Animate wins: [Win animations](/mechanics/cells-and-banners/#concept)

## Reference

### ReelSetBuilder
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-builder/
The fluent builder for ReelSet. Each method sets one part of the configuration, and build() checks it and returns the set.

Every method returns `this`, so calls chain. `build()` validates the configuration and returns a [`ReelSet`](/reference/api-reelset/). If a required call is missing, it throws one error that lists every problem.

#### Required

| Method | |
|---|---|
| `.reels(n)` | Number of columns. |
| `.visibleCells(n)` or `.visibleCellsPerReel([n,...])` or `.multiways({...})` | One of these picks the row layout. |
| `.symbolSize(w, h)` | Per-symbol dimensions in px. |
| `.symbols((r) => { r.register(...) })` | At least one symbol id. |
| `.ticker(pixiTicker)` | Drives frame updates. |

Missing any of these throws at `.build()` with a readable list of problems.

#### Optional

| Method | Default |
|---|---|
| `.symbolGap(x, y)` | `{ x: 0, y: 0 }` |
| `.bufferSymbols(n)` or `.bufferSymbols({ start, end })` | `1`. Values below 1 are clamped to 1, because the motion layer needs one buffer cell on each side to detect wraps. `start` is the end at the smaller main coordinate (above for vertical, left for horizontal), whichever way the reel travels. |
| `.weights({ id: n })` | `10` for each registered symbol |
| `.randomSymbols(pool, scope?)` | No pools. Narrows the random draw on top of `weights()`. `pool` is `{ weights?, exclude? }`; `scope` is `{ reel?, slots?: 'spinning' \| 'buffer' \| 'bufferStart' \| 'bufferEnd' }` (default: every reel, every random cell). Each layer narrows the wider ones, so a side pool narrows what `'buffer'` already allows. The same pools are available at run time as `reelSet.randomSymbols`. |
| `.symbolData({ id: { zIndex, unmask, size, weight } })` | Per-symbol metadata. Routes `unmask` for you. `size: { reels, cells }` beyond 1x1 declares a big symbol; `reels` spans the cross axis and `cells` the main axis, in every orientation. A big symbol defaults to weight `0` (it only lands); a tall one (`reels: 1`) given a weight also streams past during the spin. |
| `.reelExtents([n,...])` | Per-reel main-axis extents for pyramid layouts (pixel height when vertical, width when horizontal). Derived from the cell count if unset. |
| `.reelAnchor('start' \| 'center' \| 'end')` | `'center'`. How short reels align along the main axis, inside the longest reel's extent. |
| `.speed(name, profile)` | `SpeedPresets.NORMAL` under `'normal'` |
| `.initialSpeed(name)` | `'normal'` |
| `.offsetConfig(config)` | `{ mode: 'none' }` |
| `.spinningMode(mode)` | `new StandardMode()` |
| `.frameMiddleware(mw)` | *(none)*. Add as many as you need. They run sorted by priority. |
| `.phases((f) => { f.register(...) })` | Built-in `START`/`SPIN`/`STOP`/`ANTICIPATION` (plus the cascade phases when `.tumble()` is used). `f.register(key, Class, options)` re-registers a built-in with options; `{ steps }` edits its step list, see [Phases](/reference/api-phases/#steps). |
| `.skipMode('slam' \| 'quicken')` | `'slam'`. What a skip press does to the reels it frees when `requestSkip()` / `skipSpin()` do not say. See [ReelSet](/reference/api-reelset/). |
| `.tumble({ fall, dropIn })` | *(unset)*. Required for `spin({ mode: 'cascade' })` and `reelSet.refill(...)`. See [the Tumble section](#tumble) below. |
| `.multiways({ minCells, maxCells, reelExtent })` | *(unset)*. Required for `setShape(...)`. `reelExtent` is a main-axis extent. |
| `.orientation('vertical' \| 'horizontal')` | `'vertical'`. Which screen axis the strip travels along. See [Sideways and upward reels](/mechanics/orientation-and-direction/#concept). |
| `.direction('forward' \| 'reverse')` | `'forward'`. Which way along that axis symbols move. `'reverse'` on a vertical set is a roll-up. |
| `.directionPerReel([d,...])` | *(unset)*. A per-reel override. The array length must equal `reels()`. Cannot be combined with cross-reel big symbols. |
| `.cellStacking('ascending' \| 'descending')` | `'ascending'`. Which cell draws in front. This is geometric, so `direction('reverse')` does not flip it. |
| `.reelStacking('ascending' \| 'descending')` | `'ascending'`. Which reel draws in front. |
| `.pinMigrationDuration(ms \| fn)` | `200` (MultiWays only) |
| `.pinMigrationEase(ease)` | `'power2.out'` (MultiWays only) |
| `.maskStrategy(strategy)` | Per-reel `RectMaskStrategy`. Switches to `SharedRectMaskStrategy` on its own when big or unmasked symbols are registered and the cross-axis gap is above 0. A custom strategy takes one `MaskContext` and must declare `version = MASK_STRATEGY_VERSION`. |
| `.gsap(instance)` | The package's own `gsap` import. Use this when your app and the engine resolve to different `gsap` instances (symlinked workspaces, npm link, a misconfigured `dedupe`). Bound per set at `build()`; pass the same instance to `driveGsapWithTicker(ticker, instance)`. |
| `.initialFrame(ColumnTarget[])` | Random per `weights()`. One `ColumnTarget` per reel: `{ visible, bufferStart?, bufferEnd? }`. |
| `.rng(fn)` | `Math.random`. The source for every symbol the engine picks itself: the strip you watch scroll, and any buffer padding. Must return a number in `[0, 1)`. A server-authoritative outcome does not make that visible sequence reproducible. Pass a seeded, audited PRNG if you need to replay a spin from its seed. |
| `.poolCapacity(n)` | The whole strip (visible plus buffer) per symbol id, so a grid that briefly shows one symbol everywhere still recycles. Lower it to cap memory on very large grids. Raise it for unusually heavy simultaneous swaps. |

#### .build()

Validates every required field, instantiates every subsystem and returns a `ReelSet`. If anything is wrong it throws synchronously with the full list of problems, so you never get a half-built reel set.

#### Minimal example

```ts
import { ReelSetBuilder, SpriteSymbol, SpeedPresets } from 'pixi-reels';

const reelSet = new ReelSetBuilder()
  .reels(5)
  .visibleCells(3)
  .symbolSize(140, 140)
  .symbolGap(4, 4)
  .symbols((r) => {
    r.register('cherry', SpriteSymbol, { textures: { cherry: cherryTex } });
  })
  .weights({ cherry: 40 })
  .speed('turbo', SpeedPresets.TURBO)
  .ticker(app.ticker)
  .build();
```

#### Tumble

`.tumble(config?)` enables cascade mechanics. It replaces the strip-spin and bounce-stop chain with three phases, `cascade:fall`, `cascade:place` and `cascade:dropIn`, and makes `'cascade'` the default spin mode for that builder.

```ts
.tumble({
  fall:   { duration: 280, ease: 'sine.in',       cellStagger: 40 },
  dropIn: { duration: 480, ease: 'back.out(1.6)', cellStagger: 50, distance: 'perHole' },
})
```

##### TumbleFallConfig

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | `number` (ms) | `300` | Each symbol's fall-out tween length. |
| `ease` | GSAP easing string | `'sine.in'` | The gravity feel. Any [GSAP easing](https://gsap.com/docs/v3/Eases) works. |
| `cellStagger` | `number` (ms) | `0` | Delay between successive rows starting their fall. `0` means every row falls together. |
| `cellOrder` | `'auto' \| 'endFirst' \| 'startFirst'` | `'auto'` | Which row begins first. `'auto'` starts at the end gravity exits from, so the default pairs with `setDropOrder('ltr')` for the usual bottom-left first, top-right last order, and it inverts on its own when gravity does. `'endFirst'` and `'startFirst'` pin a geometric end. |

##### TumbleDropInConfig

| Field | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | `number` (ms) | `600` | Each symbol's drop-in tween length. |
| `ease` | GSAP easing string | `'power2.out'` | A clean deceleration with no overshoot, which matches commercial slots that play a landing Spine animation after the drop. Use `'back.out(1.5)'` for a soft overshoot, `'bounce.out'` for a cartoon bounce, `'expo.out'` for a slam. |
| `cellStagger` | `number` (ms) | `60` | Delay between successive rows starting their drop. `0` means all rows drop together, the usual choice for a refill. |
| `cellOrder` | `'auto' \| 'endFirst' \| 'startFirst'` | `'auto'` | Which row arrives first when `cellStagger > 0`. `'auto'` fills from the end gravity exits from, the way a stack settles from its floor up. |
| `distance` | `'perHole' \| 'auto' \| number` | `'perHole'` | `'perHole'` drops each symbol exactly its own offset, which is what gravity would do. `'auto'` makes every symbol travel the full column together, the rain-column look. A number forces one pixel distance for all of them. |

##### Picking a feel

Five presets you can copy as they are. The [tumble feels recipe](/mechanics/cascade/#tumble-feels) shows them side by side.

| Feel | fall.ease | dropIn.ease | dropIn.cellStagger | When to use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Classic | `sine.in` | `back.out(1.6)` | 50 ms | Default. Start here. |
| Cartoon bounce | `sine.in` | `bounce.out` | 70 ms | Multi-bounce landing. |
| Slam | `power4.in` | `expo.out` | 25 ms | Turbo mode, with tumbles under half a second. |
| Rain column | `sine.in` | `sine.in` | 0 ms (+ `distance: 'auto'`) | Match-3, puzzle and chess-board grids. |
| Wave | `sine.in` | `back.out(2.0)` | 110 ms | Strong per-row stagger, so rows arrive one at a time. |

##### Overriding a phase

`.tumble()` registers three named phases (`cascade:fall`, `cascade:place`, `cascade:dropIn`). Each is a `ReelPhase` subclass you can override on its own:

```ts
builder
  .tumble({ /* ... */ })
  .phases((f) => f.register('cascade:fall', MyCometFallPhase));
```

See [`docs/recipes/tumble-cascade.md`](https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-reels/blob/main/docs/recipes/tumble-cascade.md) for the phase contract and an override example.

#### Spin options

`reelSet.spin(options?)` accepts `SpinOptions`. All fields are optional.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `holdReels` | `number[]` | Reel indices to hold still for this spin. Held reels skip `START`, `SPIN` and `STOP` and stay on their current symbols. They count as already landed for `spin:allLanded`. Out-of-range, duplicate and non-integer entries are dropped without an error. `setAnticipation([...])` and `setStopDelays([...])` drop held indices too. |
| `mode` | `'standard' \| 'cascade'` | Which phase chain this spin runs. Overrides the builder default. `'cascade'` requires `.tumble(...)` on the builder; without it the cascade phases are not registered and `spin()` throws. |

```ts
// Hold reels 0 and 4; only the middle three reroll.
const spin = reelSet.spin({ holdReels: [0, 4] });
reelSet.setResult(serverGrid); // entries at 0/4 are ignored
await spin;

// Per-spin cascade override on a builder that registered both modes.
await reelSet.spin({ mode: 'cascade' });
```

See the [spin lifecycle guide](/mechanics/skip/#concept) for how these options interact with the event timeline, and the [cascades guide](/mechanics/cascade/#concept) for the cascade-specific orchestration.

### Events
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-events/
The typed events on reelSet.events and reel.events, when each one fires, and what its payload holds.

Two emitters:

- `reelSet.events`, a typed `EventEmitter<ReelSetEvents>`. Domain events for the whole board.
- `reel.events`, a typed `EventEmitter<ReelEvents>`. Per-column phase, symbol and land events.

On both, `on(name, cb)` returns the emitter, so subscriptions chain. Unsubscribe with `off(name, fn)`, which needs a reference to the same function. The library cleans up its own listeners on `destroy()`. An exception thrown inside a listener stops the remaining listeners for that event and propagates out of `emit()` into the engine. `emit()` has no try/catch and logs nothing, so wrap anything that can throw.

#### Quick map

| Family | Events | Fires from |
|---|---|---|
| Spin lifecycle | `spin:start`, `spin:allStarted`, `spin:stopping`, `spin:reelLanded`, `spin:allLanded`, `spin:complete` | Every `spin()` |
| Nudge | `nudge:start`, `nudge:complete`, `nudge:cancelled` | `nudge()` |
| Skip / slam | `skip:requested`, `skip:completed`, `skip:queued`, `skip:boosted` | `skipSpin()`, `requestSkip()`, `slamStop()` |
| Speed | `speed:changed` | `setSpeed()` |
| Cascade | `cascade:chain:start`, `cascade:chain:end`, `cascade:fall:start`, `cascade:fall:symbol`, `cascade:fall:end`, `cascade:place:end`, `cascade:dropIn:start`, `cascade:dropIn:symbol`, `cascade:dropIn:end`, `cascade:destroy:start`, `cascade:destroy:end`, `cascade:gravity:start`, `cascade:gravity:symbol`, `cascade:gravity:end`, `cascade:gravity:error` | `.tumble()` plus `spin({mode:'cascade'})`, `refill()`, `runCascade()` or `destroySymbols()` |
| Spotlight | `spotlight:start`, `spotlight:end` | `spotlight.cycle(...)` |
| Wins | `win:start`, `win:group`, `win:symbol`, `win:end` | `WinPresenter.show(...)` |
| Pins | `pin:placed`, `pin:moved`, `pin:expired`, `pin:migrated`, `pin:overlayCreated`, `pin:overlayDestroyed` | `pin()`, `unpin()`, `movePin()`, a MultiWays reshape |
| MultiWays | `shape:changed`, `adjust:start`, `adjust:complete` | `setShape()` |
| Growing the board | `reels:added`, `reels:removed`, `rows:added`, `rows:removed`, `column:set`, `expand:start`, `expand:stepAdded`, `expand:stepLanded`, `expand:complete`, `expand:end` | `addReels()`, `removeReels()`, `addRows()`, `removeRows()`, `setColumn()`, `splitSymbol()`, `resetColumns()`, `expand()` |
| Lifecycle | `destroyed` | `destroy()` |

Every cascade event has the same three-part name, `cascade:<scope>:<step>`. The scope is `chain` (one stage inside the `runCascade` loop), `fall`, `place`, `dropIn` or `gravity` (a phase-level animation), or `destroy` (one batch of `destroySymbols`). The step is `start`, `symbol` or `end`. `:symbol` exists only on the per-cell variants of fall, dropIn and gravity. `:place` has only `:end`, because placement is a one-moment swap with no animation. The chain itself has no event; the returned promise marks its end, so `await` the call.

#### Spin lifecycle

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `spin:start` | none | Any `spin()` or `refill()` call. Cascades emit this per refill. |
| `spin:allStarted` | none | Every non-held reel is in the `SPIN` phase. Cascade refills skip this event. |
| `spin:stopping` | `(reelIndex: number)` | A reel begins `STOP` (held reels never fire). |
| `spin:reelLanded` | `(reelIndex: number, symbols: string[])` | One reel landed. `symbols` is its full visible column. |
| `spin:allLanded` | `(result: SpinResult)` | The last non-held reel landed. |
| `spin:complete` | `(result: SpinResult)` | Immediately after `spin:allLanded`. |

##### Anticipation

These fire only for reels that tease: reels in the anticipation set whose hold
is above 0.

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `anticipation:reel` | `{ reelIndex, order, total }` | That reel starts teasing. `order` is 0-based within the tease set, so `order / (total - 1)` drives a pitch ramp without re-deriving anything from `spin:stopping`. |
| `anticipation:reelEnd` | `{ reelIndex }` | That reel's tease is over. |

```ts
interface SpinResult {
  symbols: string[][];              // final visible grid [reelIndex][cellIndex]
  wasSkipped: boolean;              // true if skipSpin() / requestSkip() / slamStop() ended the spin
  skipMode: SkipMode | null;        // the mode of the last press that freed reels
  skipContext: SkipContext | null;  // that press: { mode, speed?, payload? }; { mode: 'slam' } for an engine slam
  duration: number;                 // ms from spin:start to spin:complete
}
```

#### Skip / slam

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `skip:requested` | `(info: SkipInfo)` = `({ reels: number[], partial: boolean, mode: SkipMode, speed?: SpeedProfile, payload?: unknown })` | A press freed reels, from `skipSpin()`, `requestSkip()` (once `setResult` has arrived) or `slamStop()`. `reels` is what this press frees. `partial` is `true` when reels are still spinning after it (a protected tease, a reel group, or `slamStop({ reels })` / `slamStop({ except })`). `mode` says what freeing means: `'slam'` places them now, `'quicken'` asks each for its landing sooner, and that landing arrives as the usual `spin:reelLanding` / `spin:reelLanded`. `speed` and `payload` are the press's own, the same `SkipContext` every phase's `onSkip(ctx)` saw; keys the press did not set are absent. An engine slam (abort, timeout, `slamStop()`) is a bare `mode: 'slam'`. |
| `skip:completed` | `(info: SkipInfo)` | The same press, once its reels are down: in the same tick for a slam, as the last freed reel lands for a quicken (however it got down, its own stop or a later slam). The same `info` its `skip:requested` carried. |
| `skip:queued` | `(info: SkipContext)` = `({ mode, speed?, payload? })` | `requestSkip()` came before `setResult()`, or a press came between two `expand()` steps. The press is kept and fires the moment the result (or the next step's result) arrives. The same context its `skip:requested` will carry, minus the reels, which are not known yet. |
| `skip:boosted` | `({ previous: SpeedProfile, current: SpeedProfile })` | The first `skipSpin()` press of a standard-mode round. The engine bumped to the fastest registered profile for the rest of the round. Cascade rounds set the auto-slam-refills flag instead and never emit this. The restore on the next `spin()` does not emit it again. |

```ts
reelSet.events.on('skip:boosted', ({ previous, current }) => {
  hud.flash(`SPEED: ${previous.name} → ${current.name}`);
});
```

#### Speed

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `speed:changed` | `(profile: SpeedProfile, previous: SpeedProfile)` | `setSpeed()`, or the round-end restore after `skip:boosted`. |

#### Cascade (tumble)

Available only when the builder used `.tumble({...})`. The per-symbol events fire before the library starts its own `view.y` tween, so a listener can run a parallel tween that finishes on the same beat.

##### Chain-scoped (one stage inside the loop)

`runCascade(...)` returns `Promise<RunCascadeResult>`. Await the call to know when the chain is over and to read the summary. There is no separate round-start or round-end event, because a round is not a reel-engine concept. The slot industry uses "round" for one bet-to-payout transaction. For the engine, a round runs from the press to the last stop, which `spin:start` and `spin:allLanded` already cover.

```ts
interface RunCascadeResult {
  chainLength: number;     // refill stages that ran (0 = no wins on the initial grid)
  totalWinners: number;    // sum of winners.length across every refill
  finalGrid: string[][];   // grid after the last refill
  wasSkipped: boolean;     // true if the player slammed mid-chain
  skipContext: SkipContext | null;  // the press that ended it, or null; an abort is { mode: 'slam' }
}
```

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `cascade:chain:start` | `{ chain: number, winners: readonly Cell[], currentGrid: string[][] }` | A chain stage opens inside `runCascade()`: winners were detected and destroy is about to run. `chain` is 1-indexed. |
| `cascade:chain:end` | `{ chain: number, winners: readonly Cell[], nextGrid: string[][] }` | A chain stage closes: both the destroy and the refill drop-in have finished. The loop goes back to `detectWinners` next, or exits if winners came back empty. |

##### Phase-scoped (animation events on each refill or initial drop)

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `cascade:fall:start` | `{ reelIndex: number }` | A reel's fall-out begins (Moment A only; a refill has no fall). |
| `cascade:fall:symbol` | `{ symbol: ReelSymbol, view: Container, reelIndex: number, cellIndex: number, duration: number, ease: string, distance: number, signal: AbortSignal }` | One symbol's fall tween is about to start. Read `symbol` / `view` to attach a parallel tween. |
| `cascade:fall:end` | `{ reelIndex: number }` | A reel's last fall tween settled. |
| `cascade:place:end` | `{ reelIndex: number, placedSymbols: readonly ReelSymbol[], isInitial: boolean, winnerCells: readonly number[] }` | New identities are placed and snapped to the grid, before the drop-in starts. This is the place to decorate symbols. `isInitial` is `true` on Moment A; on a refill it is `false` and `winnerCells` is filled in. Place has no `:start` because it is a synchronous swap. |
| `cascade:dropIn:start` | `{ reelIndex: number }` | A reel's drop-in begins. |
| `cascade:dropIn:symbol` | `{ symbol: ReelSymbol, view: Container, reelIndex: number, cellIndex: number, duration: number, ease: string, offsetCells: number, signal: AbortSignal }` | One symbol's drop-in tween is about to start. `offsetCells` is the number of cells this symbol traverses (1 for top-row refills, more for survivors sliding past larger holes). |
| `cascade:dropIn:end` | `{ reelIndex: number }` | A reel's last drop-in tween settled. |
| `cascade:gravity:start` | `{ reelIndex: number }` | Two-stage refill only (`mode: 'gravity-then-drop'`). A reel's survivor-settle stage begins, before new symbols enter. Not emitted when the refill is `'combined'`. |
| `cascade:gravity:symbol` | `{ symbol: ReelSymbol, view: Container, reelIndex: number, cellIndex: number, duration: number, ease: string, offsetCells: number, signal: AbortSignal }` | One survivor's settle tween is about to start. Same payload shape as `dropIn:symbol`, scoped to survivors only. |
| `cascade:gravity:end` | `{ reelIndex: number }` | A reel's survivor settle landed. The library now waits for both `gravityHoldMs` and `gravityHold` (in parallel, under `Promise.all`) before the drop-in stage begins. Use it as the cue for anticipation visuals during the hold. |
| `cascade:gravity:error` | `{ error: unknown }` | Your `gravityHold` promise rejected, or `onGravityComplete` threw. The cascade still settles. This event is the only place the reason survives, so forward it to your logger. Typed `unknown` because user code can throw anything. |

##### Destroy-batch-scoped

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `cascade:destroy:start` | `{ cells: readonly Cell[] }` | `destroySymbols(...)` is about to start. Fires from every call, direct or inside `runCascade`. A call with an empty batch does not emit. |
| `cascade:destroy:end` | `{ cells: readonly Cell[], failed?: readonly Cell[] }` | `destroySymbols(...)` finished: every `playDestroy()` resolved and the viewport dim, if any, was restored. |

##### Event order inside one `runCascade()` call

Combined-mode refill (the default, `refillMode: 'combined'`):

```text
for each chain stage with winners:
  cascade:chain:start
    cascade:destroy:start
      (destroy tweens, one per cell, parallel)
    cascade:destroy:end
    onCascade callback (optional)
    pause (pauseAfterDestroyMs)
    (refill, per reel:)
      cascade:place:end
      cascade:dropIn:start
      cascade:dropIn:symbol, one per symbol
      cascade:dropIn:end
  cascade:chain:end
// then the awaited runCascade promise resolves with RunCascadeResult
```

Two-stage refill (`refillMode: 'gravity-then-drop'`) splits the refill into a gravity stage and a drop-in stage with an anticipation window between them:

```text
for each chain stage with winners:
  cascade:chain:start
    cascade:destroy:start
      (destroy tweens, one per cell, parallel)
    cascade:destroy:end
    onCascade callback (optional)
    pause (pauseAfterDestroyMs)
    (gravity stage, per reel:)
      cascade:place:end
      cascade:gravity:start
      cascade:gravity:symbol, one per survivor
      cascade:gravity:end
    hold (Promise.all of the `gravityHoldMs` timer and the caller's `gravityHold` promise)
    onGravityComplete callback (optional)
    (drop-in stage, per reel:)
      cascade:dropIn:start
      cascade:dropIn:symbol, one per symbol
      cascade:dropIn:end
  cascade:chain:end
```

##### Common patterns

```ts
// Lock auto-play around the call itself. `await` IS the lifecycle.
hud.lock();
try {
  await reelSet.runCascade({ detectWinners, nextGrid });
} finally {
  hud.unlock();
}

// Per-chain SFX cues.
reelSet.events.on('cascade:chain:start', ({ chain }) => sfx.play(`chain_${Math.min(chain, 5)}`));

// Destroy cue, even when consumers call `destroySymbols` outside runCascade.
reelSet.events.on('cascade:destroy:start', ({ cells }) => sfx.play('shatter', cells.length));

// Decorate ONLY new arrivals (skip survivors).
reelSet.events.on('cascade:place:end', ({ placedSymbols, isInitial, winnerCells }) => {
  const newRowSet = new Set(isInitial ? placedSymbols.map((_, i) => i) : winnerCells);
  for (const [row, sym] of placedSymbols.entries()) {
    if (newRowSet.has(row)) addMultiplierBadge(sym);
  }
});

// Squish each symbol on land, in sync with the library's drop-in tween.
reelSet.events.on('cascade:dropIn:symbol', ({ view, duration }) => {
  // Library will animate view.y; you can animate view.scale on the same beat.
  gsap.to(view.scale, { x: 1.1, y: 0.9, duration: duration / 2000, yoyo: true, repeat: 1 });
});
```

#### Nudge

Fired by `reelSet.nudge(reel, opts)`. `landed` does not fire for a nudge; it
belongs to the spin pipeline.

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `nudge:start` | `{ reelIndex, distance, direction: 'forward' \| 'reverse' }` | Pre-placement is done and the tween is about to begin. |
| `nudge:complete` | `{ reelIndex, distance, direction, symbols: string[] }` | The strip snapped to the post-nudge grid; `symbols` is the new visible column. |
| `nudge:cancelled` | `{ reelIndex, distance, direction, reason: string }` | The signal aborted or the reel was destroyed mid-tween. Does not fire alongside `nudge:complete`. |

#### Spotlight

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `spotlight:start` | `(positions: SymbolPosition[])` | `spotlight.cycle(...)` began. |
| `spotlight:end` | none | The spotlight finished. |

#### Wins (WinPresenter)

Emitted by `WinPresenter` only. If you do not use it, these never fire.

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `win:start` | `(wins: readonly Win[])` | A presenter sequence began. The list is sorted by `value` descending by default. |
| `win:group` | `(win: Win, cells: readonly SymbolPosition[])` | One win. Fires once per win, before its cells animate. |
| `win:symbol` | `(symbol: unknown, cell: SymbolPosition, win: Win)` | Each cell, one at a time when `WinPresenter.stagger > 0`. Cast `symbol` to your concrete `ReelSymbol` subclass. |
| `win:end` | `(reason: 'complete' \| 'aborted')` | The sequence finished, on its own or through an abort. |

#### Pins

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `pin:placed` | `(pin: CellPin)` | `reelSet.pin(...)` succeeded. Replacing an existing pin does not fire `pin:expired` for the old one; only this event fires. |
| `pin:moved` | `(pin: CellPin, from: { reel: number; cell: number })` | `reelSet.movePin(...)` resolved. The pin's `reel`/`cell` are already at the destination; `from` carries the origin. |
| `pin:expired` | `(pin: CellPin, reason: PinExpireReason)` | A pin was removed. `'explicit'` (via `unpin`), `'turns'` (the numeric counter hit zero), or `'eval'` (a round-scoped pin reset on the next spin). |
| `pin:migrated` | `(pin: CellPin, info: { fromCell: number; toCell: number; clamped: boolean; reelIndex: number })` | A MultiWays reshape moved a pin to a new row inside the same reel. `clamped: true` when the origin row no longer fits the new shape. Never emitted on non-MultiWays slots. |
| `pin:overlayCreated` | `(pin: CellPin, overlay: unknown)` | A mid-spin overlay symbol was mounted. Cast `overlay` to your concrete symbol class (typed as `unknown` to keep this module free of symbol-layer imports). |
| `pin:overlayDestroyed` | `(pin: CellPin, overlay: unknown)` | A mid-spin overlay was torn down on land, unpin or replacement. Fires before the symbol returns to the pool, so you can stop animations on a still-valid instance. |

#### MultiWays

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `shape:changed` | `(cellsPerReel: number[])` | `setShape(...)` accepted. Fires before any geometry change; pin migrations and `AdjustPhase` happen later in the spin. |
| `adjust:start` | `({ reelIndex: number, fromCells: number, toCells: number })` | A per-reel `AdjustPhase` entered. |
| `adjust:complete` | `({ reelIndex: number })` | A per-reel `AdjustPhase` finished. |

#### Growing the board

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `reels:added` | `({ from: number, count: number })` | `addReels()` or an `expand()` step appended reels `from .. from + count - 1`. They are in `reelSet.reels` and the viewport covers them. Move a camera here; `reelSet.viewport.maskWidth` is the new board width. |
| `reels:removed` | `({ from: number, count: number })` | `removeReels()` destroyed reels `from .. from + count - 1`. |
| `rows:added` | `({ count: number, rows: number[] })` | `addRows()` grew every reel by `count` rows below the last one. `rows` is each reel's row count now. The viewport covers them; `reelSet.viewport.maskHeight` is the new height. |
| `rows:removed` | `({ count: number, rows: number[] })` | `removeRows()` took `count` rows off every reel. |
| `column:set` | `({ reelIndex: number, fromCells: number, toCells: number })` | One reel changed its cells at rest: `setColumn()`, `splitSymbol()` (a symbol split into more cells) or `resetColumns()`. Under `height: 'keep'` the reel's height does not change; read its `cellMain` for the new cell size. The viewport already covers it. |
| `expand:start` | `({ from: number, to: number, steps: number })` | `expand()` validated its columns and is about to add the first step. |
| `expand:stepAdded` | `(step: ExpandStep)` | A step's reels are on the board; they spin next. Fires before `onStepAdded`. |
| `expand:stepLanded` | `(step: ExpandStepLanded)` | A step's reels landed. Fires before `onStepLanded`. |
| `expand:complete` | `(result: ExpandResult)` | Every step landed, the fast-forward step included. |
| `expand:end` | `(reason: 'complete' \| 'failed')` | The expansion is over, either way: `'complete'` right after `expand:complete`, `'failed'` when it threw. This is the one place to put a UI back. `reelSet.isExpanding` is `false` again by then, so a listener here can start the next round. |

Each step is a spin of its own reels with every earlier reel held, so the usual `spin:*` events fire for it too, and `spin:reelLanded` fires only for the reels the step added.

#### Lifecycle

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `destroyed` | none | `reelSet.destroy()` was called. Listeners attached before this fire one last time, then the emitter clears every listener. |

#### Per-reel events

`reel.events` is a smaller surface scoped to one column.

Every bus (`reelSet.events`, `reel.events`, a board's `events`) also takes `onAny((event, ...args) => ...)` and `offAny(fn)`. An `onAny` listener gets every event, name first, after the event's own listeners. It is meant for a trace, an events panel or a recorder; game logic should subscribe to the events it needs by name. Engine notices are not events. `onNotice(fn)` hears them the same way, whatever the log level.

```ts
type ReelEvents = {
  'phase:enter':     [phaseName: string];
    // 'start' | 'spin' | 'stop' | 'anticipation' | 'adjust' | 'nudge'
    // (+ 'cascade:fall' | 'cascade:place' | 'cascade:dropIn' on a tumble set)
    // | 'cascade:fall' | 'cascade:place' | 'cascade:dropIn'
  'phase:exit':      [phaseName: string];
  'phase:step':      [{ phase: string, step: string, status: PhaseStepStatus }];
    // a step of a phase on runSteps(): 'start' | 'end' | 'skipped' (a cut
    // step a quicken never started) | 'cut' (the cut step a quicken stopped
    // in flight) | 'cancelled' (the step a slam or a destroy stopped)
  'symbol:created':  [symbolId: string, stripIndex: number];
  'landed':          [symbols: string[]];
  'destroyed':       [];
};
```

```ts
reelSet.getReel(4).events.on('phase:enter', (name) => {
  if (name === 'anticipation') playTensionMusic();
});
```

#### Listener etiquette

- Subscribe once at startup. For hot-swap modules keep the function reference and call `off(name, fn)`.
- Async listeners are fire and forget. If you must await per-event work, queue it yourself; the engine does not.
- The library emits `cascade:*:symbol` events before it starts its own tween. Your listener can read the same `view` and queue a parallel tween, and the two run together.
- The `Cell` type used in cascade payloads is `{ reel: number; cell: number }` (`reel` is the column, `cell` the visible cell). Same shape as the `destroySymbols` input.

#### Console notices

Everything the library prints goes through one channel, so notices all look the
same and all carry a stable code you can grep for, search the docs for, or
quote in a bug report.

```ts
import { setLogLevel } from 'pixi-reels';

setLogLevel('warn');   // drop the advisory notices, keep problems
setLogLevel('silent'); // production
```

The levels are `'silent' | 'error' | 'warn' | 'info'`, and each includes the
ones before it. The default is `'info'`, everything. The
[debugging guide](/learn/debugging/#console-notices) says what each level
covers and why the default is not quieter. In a browser a notice prints as a
styled badge: `pixi-reels`, then the code, then the message. Elsewhere it prints
as `[pixi-reels] warn(code) message`, since `%c` is a browser console feature.

Notices keep using `console.warn` / `console.error` / `console.info` rather
than one `console.log`, so devtools level filtering and stack capture still
work, and detail arguments pass through untouched (an `Error` keeps its stack).

| Code | Level | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `quicken-cascade` | warn | A `mode: 'quicken'` press in cascade mode. A tumble reel lands by placing its symbols, so there is nothing to spin out; the press slammed. |
| `phase-chain-threw` | error | A reel's phase chain rejected. The engine slammed to recover so the spin still settles. |
| `refill-threw` | error | A two-stage refill rejected, usually from a caller's `gravityHold` / `onGravityComplete`. Slammed to recover. |
| `pin-hook-threw` | error | A `movePin` flight hook threw. The flight continues so the flight symbol is not leaked. |
| `destroy-rejected` | warn | A cell's `playDestroy()` rejected during `destroySymbols()`. Reported per cell on `cascade:destroy:end` as well. |
| `buffer-clamped` | warn | `bufferSymbols()` was given less than 1 and was clamped. Once per process. |
| `hw-coin-win-failed` | warn | A Hold & Win coin win animation rejected. |
| `mask-auto-shared` | info | The builder selected `SharedRectMaskStrategy` on its own. Pass `.maskStrategy(...)` to override. |
| `warp-skips-unmask` | info | `curveMode('warp')` does not bend `unmask: true` symbols, the win spotlight or pin overlays. |

### Phases
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-phases/
START, SPIN, ANTICIPATION, STOP: the four lifecycle phases and how to extend them.

A phase is one slice of a reel's lifecycle. To write one, extend
`ReelPhase<TConfig>` and implement three hooks.

Every phase runs on one reel. Five reels in `StopPhase` are five instances.
`SpinController` builds them per reel, per spin, through the `PhaseFactory`, so
no phase object lives long enough to hold state across spins.

#### Built-ins

Every one of these is exported, so you can subclass it as well as replace it.
The key is the name to register under. Registering a different class under an
existing key swaps the built-in out.

| Class | Key | Config | Role | Skippable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `StartPhase` | `'start'` | `StartPhaseConfig` | Accelerate from rest, with a step-back pull | yes |
| `SpinPhase` | `'spin'` | `SpinPhaseConfig` | Full speed until the result arrives | no |
| `AnticipationPhase` | `'anticipation'` | `AnticipationPhaseConfig` | Slow hold, for tension | yes |
| `StopPhase` | `'stop'` | `StopPhaseConfig` | Decelerate onto the target frame, bounce | yes |
| `CascadeFallPhase` | `'cascade:fall'` | `CascadeFallPhaseConfig` | Tumble fall-out; replaces `StartPhase` | yes |
| `CascadePlacePhase` | `'cascade:place'` | `CascadePlacePhaseConfig` | Tumble identity swap | yes |
| `CascadeDropInPhase` | `'cascade:dropIn'` | `CascadeDropInPhaseConfig` | Tumble drop-in and gravity slide | yes |
| `AdjustPhase` | `'adjust'` | `AdjustPhaseConfig` | MultiWays reshape; tweens pin overlays | yes |

`SpinPhase` is the one phase that cannot be skipped. It animates toward
nothing; it waits for `setResult()`, and a slam resolves it from the outside.
The floor that decides how early a reel may stop also lives here, which is why
a per-reel `minimumSpinTime` matters.

The bottom four are wired only when you ask for them: the three cascade phases
by `builder.tumble(...)`, `AdjustPhase` by `builder.multiways(...)`. A plain
slot never sees them.

#### Register a custom phase

```ts
import { ReelPhase } from 'pixi-reels';

class FlashPhase extends ReelPhase<{ duration: number }> {
  readonly name = 'flash';
  readonly skippable = true;
  private _elapsed = 0;
  private _duration = 0;

  protected onEnter(cfg: { duration: number }): void {
    this._elapsed = 0;
    this._duration = cfg.duration;
  }

  update(deltaMs: number): void {
    this._elapsed += deltaMs;
    // ... toggle reel alpha or something
    if (this._elapsed >= this._duration) this._complete();
  }

  protected onSkip(ctx: SkipContext): void { /* slam: cleanup; quicken: cut a wait */ }
}

builder.phases((f) => f.register('flash', FlashPhase));
```

Replacing a built-in works the same way: register your class under the same
key (`'start'`, `'spin'`, `'anticipation'`, `'stop'`). This is also the only
way a phase written from scratch gets to run. The controller asks the factory
for the lifecycle keys and nothing else, so a phase registered under a name of
its own, like `'flash'` above, is never constructed. To replace a phase,
register under its key.

Live demo (phase-from-scratch-start): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-phases/

#### What a phase may call

A phase drives its reel through `this.reel`. Everything the built-in phases
call on it, a custom phase may call too, and it is all in the published
typings:

| Call | Does | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `reel.beginMotion()` | Re-masks lifted unmask symbols the instant the reel begins to move. Idempotent. | `StartPhase` on launch |
| `reel.notifySpinStart()` | Tells every symbol it is in a spin (blur, static-spin presentations). Idempotent. | `StartPhase` at full speed, and from `onSkip` |
| `reel.forceSpeed(v)` | Jump to a speed, drive included. Assigning `reel.speed` from a phase is ramped back under the drive model; this is not. | `StartPhase.onSkip`, `AnticipationPhase.onSkip` |
| `reel.placeStrip(frame)` | Place a full strip, buffers included. `placeSymbols` is the visible-window form for game code and drops a big symbol's tail parked in a buffer row. | `StopPhase.onSkip` |
| `this.land(cells?)` | Halt the drive, snap to the grid, tell the symbols the spin ended and that they landed, lift unmask art, raise `spin:reelLanding`. The only way a phase lands a reel. | `StopPhase`'s `land` step |
| `this.bounce(options?)` | The landing overshoot, carrying lifted views along on every frame. Returns `{ done, cancel() }`; `done` settles on the rest position or right after `cancel()`. Defaults come from the profile; `BounceOptions` (`distance`, `duration`, `ease`, and `animation` for a different shape) override them per call. | `StopPhase`'s `bounce` step |

`land()` and `bounce()` are public on the base, so a step written outside the
class reaches them as `ctx.phase.land()` / `ctx.phase.bounce()`. The reel's
own `haltDrive`, `snapToGrid`, `notifySpinEnd`, `notifyLanded` and
`offsetLiftedViews` stay internal; the two helpers are the only things that
use them. `this.reel` and `this.speed` are the public getters; `this._reel`
and `this._speed` are the same fields, kept for subclasses written against
them.

A phase that never moves its reel relies on two guarantees. `SpinPhase` never
writes `reel.speed`, and `Reel.update` does nothing at `speed === 0`. So a stop
that places its frame and slides it in, with no spin-out at all, is supported.

Timing that belongs to a phase can live on the speed profile. Declare the
profile type the phase reads as the second type parameter, and `this._speed`
sees the extra fields. `register()` infers it from the class, so the
registration needs no cast. At run time the manager hands every phase the
profile instance the game registered, so the fields are there.

```ts
interface InstantProfile extends SpeedProfile { slideMs: number }

class InstantStopPhase extends ReelPhase<StopPhaseConfig, InstantProfile> {
  readonly name = 'stop';
  readonly skippable = true;
  private _bounce: ReelBounce | null = null;

  protected onEnter(config: StopPhaseConfig): void {
    this.reel.forceSpeed(0);
    this.reel.placeStrip(config.targetFrame);
    // ...slide the container in over this._speed.slideMs, then:
    this.land();
    this._bounce = this.bounce();
    void this._bounce.done.then(() => this._complete());
  }
  update(): void {}
  protected onSkip(): void { this._bounce?.cancel(); }
}

builder
  .speed('normal', { ...SpeedPresets.NORMAL, slideMs: 140 })
  .phases((f) => f.register('stop', InstantStopPhase));
```

The built-in phases take the same parameter, so a subclass keeps the profile
type instead of falling back to `SpeedProfile`. Name it on the class, and
`defaultSteps()`, `*PhaseOptions` and `ctx.profile` follow:

```ts
class TeasedStop extends StopPhase<InstantProfile> {
  override defaultSteps(): PhaseStep<StopStepContext<InstantProfile>>[] {
    return replaceStep(super.defaultSteps(), 'bounce',
      step<StopStepContext<InstantProfile>>('bounce', (ctx) =>
        ctx.phase.bounce({ duration: ctx.profile.slideMs })));
  }
}
```

`StopPhase` with no argument is `StopPhase<SpeedProfile>`, as before.

Live demo (phase-from-scratch-stop): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-phases/

#### Steps: edit a built-in without subclassing it

A built-in phase runs a named list of steps in order, and hands a game that
list before it runs. Re-register the same class under the same key with
`options.steps`:

```ts
import { StopPhase, step, insertAfter, replaceStep, removeStep } from 'pixi-reels';

builder.phases((f) => f.register('stop', StopPhase, {
  steps: (steps) => insertAfter(steps, 'land', step('flash', (ctx) => flash(ctx.reel.reelIndex))),
}));
```

| Phase | Steps, in order | Cut by a quicken |
|---|---|---|
| `StartPhase` | `delay`, `launch`, `pull` (only on a profile that bounces), `accelerate`, `announce` | `delay` |
| `StopPhase` | `delay`, `spinOut`, `land`, `bounce` | `delay` |
| `AnticipationPhase` | `tease` (the whole tease, whichever shape) | `tease` |
| `SpinPhase`, cascade phases, `AdjustPhase` | none; they wait or run one parallel timeline | |

A step is `step(name, (ctx) => result, { cut? })`. The runner waits on the
result. It may be a gsap tween or timeline (killed when a slam cuts it), a
promise (told to stop through `ctx.signal`), a cancellable like the one
`ctx.phase.bounce()` returns, or nothing. `ctx` carries `reel`, `profile`,
`config`, `gsap`, `container`, `main` (the container property that is the
travel axis), `phase`, `signal`, `quickened`, `anticipated` (whether the reel
teased earlier in this spin), and `step` (what the speed profile configured
for this step; see below). It also carries two waits a slam can cut:
`wait(ms)` on the gsap clock, and `until(predicate)`, checked from the phase's
`update()`.

`insertBefore`, `insertAfter`, `replaceStep` and `removeStep` return a copy
and throw on a name the list does not have, so a stale edit fails at build.
Plain array code works too.

`land` and `bounce` matter. Remove `land` and the reel never announces its
landing. Change the bounce shape through `phase.bounce({ animation })` rather
than a raw tween of the container, because the base carries lifted unmask
symbols along for as long as a bounce runs.

A subclass changes the list from the inside by overriding `defaultSteps()`,
or any step method (`_beginSpinOut`, `land`, `bounce`). A phase written from
scratch may run its own list through `this.runSteps(steps)` and
`this.tickSteps()` in `update()`, or ignore the runner entirely.

Live demo (phase-steps): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-phases/#steps

A custom phase can work the same way. Write the class as before, let
`runSteps()` sequence it, mark the waits `cut`, and expose `defaultSteps()`
through a constructor option. Then a quicken skips the hold with no `onSkip`
branch, a slam cancels the step in flight, and the game edits the list with
`f.register('stop', MyPhase, { steps })`, the same as it edits `StopPhase`'s.

Live demo (phase-steps-custom): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-phases/#steps

The feel work these lists are for (stagger curves, a wind-up launch, a landing
kick, beats and FX that follow the speed profile, a spotlight around the tease,
one extra beat on the last reel) is six short recipes on
[Spin feel](/mechanics/feel/).

#### Configure a phase from the speed profile

Editing the step list is code. The speed profile is the thing a game swaps at
run time, and it carries a section per phase, keyed by the phase's registered
name:

```ts
const normal = {
  name: 'normal',
  spinDelay: 0,
  spinSpeed: 200,
  stopDelay: 140,
  anticipationDelay: 450,
  bounceDistance: 80,
  bounceDuration: 600,
  start: { steps: { accelerate: { ease: 'sine.out', duration: 300 } } },
  stop: {
    bounceDistance: 40,
    steps: { bounce: { ease: 'power1.out' } },
    whenAnticipated: { steps: { bounce: { ease: 'sine.out' } } },
  },
} satisfies SpeedProfile;
```

The flat fields are unchanged and still work: a phase reads `spinSpeed` the
same way whether the profile set it at the top level or inside `start`. A
section restates any of them for that phase alone, configures the phase's
steps by name under `steps`, and carries a `whenAnticipated` half that is
merged on top for a reel that ran an anticipation tease earlier in the spin.
Resolution, lowest first:

A phase reads the result as `this.timing`, a step reads it as `ctx.profile`,
and a step reads its own entry as `ctx.step`, the segments configured for that
step, in order. A single object in the profile arrives as one entry, and the
built-in steps read `ctx.step[0]`. A list is for a step written to consume
segments, such as a two-stage acceleration in a phase of your own.

The bounce has three profile fields. `bounceEase` sits beside `bounceDistance`
and `bounceDuration`, and `phase.bounce()` uses it when the call names no ease
of its own. `bounce({ ease })` still wins, and with neither the ease is
`'power1.out'`. Like any flat field it can go in a section, so a teased landing
that differs only in its ease is `stop: { whenAnticipated: { bounceEase:
'sine.out' } }`, with no phase code.

Override part of a section at run time with `speed.tune(phase, section)`; it
merges rather than replaces, so naming one step's ease leaves the rest
standing. `speed.clearTune(phase?)` drops it. Like a speed change, a tune
takes effect on the next spin.

```ts
reelSet.speed.tune('stop', { steps: { bounce: { ease: 'back.out(2)' } } });
```

##### A custom phase's section is typed too

`PhaseProfiles` is the registry the built-in sections live in. Merge your own
phase into it and its section is checked and autocompleted everywhere a
profile is written, instead of being an opaque object:

```ts
declare module 'pixi-reels' {
  interface PhaseProfiles {
    'bigwin:flash': PhaseSection<{ pulse: StepTiming }, { flashes: number }>;
  }
}

// checked field by field, and a typo in a step name is a compile error:
reelSet.speed.addProfile('cinematic', {
  ...SpeedPresets.NORMAL,
  'bigwin:flash': { flashes: 3, steps: { pulse: { duration: 120 } } },
});
```

`PhaseSection<TSteps, TExtra>` takes the phase's step names mapped to each
step's config, and any extra fields the phase reads that are not profile
timings. A phase that does not extend `ReelPhase` reads its section with
`resolvePhaseProfile(profile, phase, anticipated)` and
`resolveStepTiming(profile, phase, step, anticipated)`.

##### Knowing that a reel teased

`PhaseFactory` passes a `PhaseCreateContext` to a registered factory as its
third argument, with `phase`, `reelIndex`, `anticipated` and `quickened`, so a
registration can build a different phase per reel:

```ts
builder.phases((f) =>
  f.registerFactory('anticipation', (reel, speed, ctx) =>
    ctx.reelIndex === 4
      ? new CustomAnticipationPhase(reel, speed)
      : new AnticipationPhase(reel, speed)),
);
```

`anticipated` means the reel ran a tease to its end earlier in this spin. It
is false for the tease itself, true for every phase after it, and false again
when a `'quicken'` press cut the tease short: the press asked for the landing,
and what it cut is the tease that `whenAnticipated` pays off. `quickened` is
in the same context if you want the other reading. The same context reaches
the phase as `phase.anticipated` and `phase.context`, and every step as
`ctx.anticipated`.

#### Subclass a built-in

Most changes to a built-in are small: a sound on landing, a flash when the stop
begins, a different tease curve. Writing those against `ReelPhase` means
rebuilding the stop sequencer or the anticipation timeline to get at one line.
Subclass instead, override the hook you care about, and call `super`.

```ts
import { StopPhase } from 'pixi-reels';
import type { StopPhaseConfig } from 'pixi-reels';

class ThudStopPhase extends StopPhase {
  protected onEnter(config: StopPhaseConfig): void {
    super.onEnter(config);
    playSfx('reel-thud');
  }
}

builder.phases((f) => f.register('stop', ThudStopPhase));
```

Live demo (phase-subclass-stop): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-phases/#steps

##### The contract

Five rules cover every subclass.

Call `super` from every hook you override. The base `onEnter` is what starts
the phase. A `StopPhase` whose override never reaches it spins forever and
takes the spin promise with it. The order is yours: put your code before
`super` to run it as the phase begins, or after it to run it once the phase is
set up.

Resolve exactly once. A phase ends by calling `this._complete()`, and the base
classes already do that at the right moment. Call it yourself only in a phase
you wrote from scratch, or in an override that replaces the base's ending.
Calling it twice is harmless, since the second call is a no-op. Never calling
it hangs the reel.

`onSkip(ctx)` sets the slam pose under `'slam'` and cuts a wait under
`'quicken'`. `ctx` is a `SkipContext`: `{ mode, speed?, payload? }`. Under
`'slam'` (a slam calls `forceComplete(ctx)`) the base has already cancelled the
step in flight. Kill anything else and leave the reel in the state the phase
would have ended in, with speed and position where a natural finish would have
put them; the base completes the phase afterwards. `StopPhase.onSkip` places
the full target frame and rests the container; `StartPhase.onSkip` jumps to
full spin speed. Under `'quicken'` the hook is reached only when the phase
declares `quickenable = true`. Then cut a wait, never the landing, and call
`_complete()` yourself when the natural end is reached (right away if the slam
pose already is that end, which is what `StartPhase` does). A phase on
`runSteps()` needs nothing here, since its `cut` steps are skipped for it. A
phase without the flag is left alone by a quicken and runs its course, so a
phase written for slams only keeps working. Override the hook when your
addition also needs to fire on a pressed reel, and pass `ctx` to `super` so
the built-in still sees the mode; a bare `super.onSkip()` is taken as a slam.
`ctx.payload` is whatever the game put on the press.

`update(deltaMs)` runs every frame while the phase is active, and only then.
It accumulates ticker time, not wall-clock time, so it stays correct in a
backgrounded tab. GSAP-driven phases leave it empty.

A quicken reaches every built-in the same way. `StopPhase` skips its `delay`
step and spins out at once, `AnticipationPhase` skips its `tease` step and
returns to full speed, `SpinPhase` drops its floor, and `StartPhase` completes
at full speed. A press that names a profile swaps `this.speed` before any of
that, so the spin-out and bounce that follow read the new one. A reel
quickened before it reached its stop has the stop phase asked as soon as it is
created, so a wait inside a custom stop is cut whether the press came before
it or during it.

Here is a subclass that uses the first four at once: `onEnter` shows a
per-reel countdown, `update` drives it, and `onSkip` takes it off when a press
cuts the tease short. The demo's button slams (`skipSpin()`, queued through
`requestSkip()` before the result). A `mode: 'quicken'` press would take the
countdown off through the same `onSkip`, because `AnticipationPhase` completes
on either mode. The difference is what the reel does next: here it is placed on
its frame, on a quicken it spins out and bounces.

Live demo (phase-subclass-anticipation): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-phases/#steps

A subclass reads `this.reel` (including `reel.reelIndex`), `this._speed` (the
active `SpeedProfile`) and `this.isActive`. `name` and `skippable` are readonly
fields on the class, and a subclass inherits both. Overriding `skippable` on a
built-in does not protect a phase from a slam; `forceComplete()` ignores the
flag. Use [tease protection](/reference/api-reelset/) for that.

##### Phases that take constructor arguments

The four standard phases are constructed with `(reel, speed)`, so
`register(key, Class)` is enough. The cascade and MultiWays phases carry
build-time config as extra constructor arguments, so a subclass of one has to
be registered through `registerFactory` and forward them.

```ts
import { CascadeDropInPhase, resolveTumbleConfig } from 'pixi-reels';
import type { CascadeDropInPhaseConfig } from 'pixi-reels';

const TUMBLE = { dropIn: { duration: 500, cellStagger: 40 } };
// Fills the partial config out to the fully-specified shape the constructor
// takes, the same way `.tumble()` does internally. Hand-writing those fields
// is how a subclass silently drifts from the set's real tumble settings.
const resolved = resolveTumbleConfig(TUMBLE);

class LoudDropInPhase extends CascadeDropInPhase {
  protected onEnter(config: CascadeDropInPhaseConfig): void {
    super.onEnter(config);
    playSfx('tumble-land');
  }
}

builder
  .tumble(TUMBLE)
  // AFTER .tumble(), which registers the defaults this replaces.
  .phases((f) =>
    f.registerFactory('cascade:dropIn', (reel, speed) =>
      new LoudDropInPhase(reel, speed, resolved.dropIn, resolved.gravity)),
  );
```

`CascadeFallPhase` takes `(reel, speed, resolved.fall, resolved.gravity)`,
`CascadePlacePhase` takes `(reel, speed, resolved.gravity)`, and `AdjustPhase`
takes `(reel, speed, { durationMs, ease })`.

Live demo (phase-subclass-cascade): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-phases/#steps

Chain position does not matter. `.phases(...)` configurators are deferred to
`build()` and applied after the tumble and MultiWays defaults, so an override
wins from anywhere in the chain. The last override of a given key wins.

Before 2.3 they ran at call time, while `.tumble()` registered its defaults
inside `build()`, so a `'cascade:*'` or `'adjust'` override was dropped
wherever it sat.

##### Stability

The built-in phases are engine internals. Every field and method on one is
`protected`, so a subclass can reach `_beginSpinOut`, `_landAndBounce`,
`_stage`, `_launch`, `_runSegment` and the rest instead of copying the phase.
That surface can change in a minor release, so a subclass may need to follow.
The config types and the hook shape are the stable parts. If you want a
guarantee rather than a hook, extend `ReelPhase` and own the whole phase.

#### Skip granularity

A slam force-completes every active phase, `AnticipationPhase` included, so by
default a skip press ends the tease before the player sees it. These levers
open that up:

| Lever | What it does |
|---|---|
| `setAnticipation(reels, { protect })` | Skip presses stop ending the tease. `'once'` lands the reels around it and leaves the tease running (the next press ends it); `'stepwise'` then releases one tease reel per press, in tease order; `'always'` never lets a press end one. |
| `slamStop({ reels })` / `slamStop({ except })` | A per-reel slam. Those reels land now; everything else keeps running its phase chain to a natural landing. |
| `setMinimumSpinTime(ms \| ms[])` | A per-reel `SpinPhase` floor, replacing the profile's single shared `minimumSpinTime`. Without this, no individual reel can land below the profile floor except through an all-reels slam. |
| `requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken', speed? })` | The press that lands instead of cutting. Frees the same reels a slam press would and quickens them: the tease ends, the delay is cut, and the spin-out and bounce still play, optionally on a named profile. A `mode: 'slam'` press afterwards still cuts what is moving. `builder.skipMode('quicken')` makes it the default. |

`skip:requested` / `skip:completed` carry `{ reels, partial }` so a listener can
tell a partial slam from a round-ending one.

The per-reel `SpinPhase` floor is also reachable from a subclass, which is
where to put it when the floor is derived rather than configured:

Live demo (phase-subclass-spin): https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-phases/#steps

Every lever above has a worked demo on [Skip and slam](/mechanics/skip/).

There is a fairness reason to use `protect` rather than raising the floor on
teasing spins. If a skip with no scatters lands at once but a skip during a
tease settles slower, the response time itself tells the player a feature is
coming before the reels have landed. `protect` keeps the non-tease reels
landing at the same instant either way, so the only tell is on screen.

### ReelSet
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/api-reelset/
The PIXI.Container that runs the reels. Build it with ReelSetBuilder, then call its methods to spin, set results and run cascades.

`ReelSet` extends `PIXI.Container`. Construct it with [`ReelSetBuilder`](/reference/api-builder/), add it to your stage, then drive it with the methods below.

Every method on this page is synchronous unless its return type is `Promise`. Most errors throw synchronously at the call site, in the same stack frame you wrote. The exceptions are cancellation: `spin()` rejects on its watchdog or `SpinOptions.signal`, and `nudge()` rejects with an `AbortError`.

#### Spin

| Method | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `spin` | `(options?: SpinOptions) => Promise<SpinResult>` | Start a spin. Resolves on `spin:complete`. Pass `{ holdReels: [...] }` to freeze columns, or `{ mode: 'cascade' }` to override the builder default for one call. |
| `setResult` | `(symbols: ColumnTarget[]) => void` | Set the target grid. Triggers the stop sequence. One `ColumnTarget` per reel: `{ visible, bufferStart?, bufferEnd? }`. |
| `setAnticipation` | `(reelIndices: number[], options?) => void` | Mark reels that should enter `ANTICIPATION` before stopping. Held indices are dropped without an error. Options: `stagger`, `slowdown`, `duration`, and `protect` (`'once'` \| `'stepwise'` \| `'always'`), which stops a skip press from hiding the tease. |
| `setStopDelays` | `(delays: number[]) => void` | One delay in ms per reel, overriding `reelIndex * speed.stopDelay` for the current spin. Persists across `refill()` calls in the same round. |
| `setMinimumSpinTime` | `(ms: number \| number[] \| null) => void` | Override the `SpinPhase` floor the profile's single `minimumSpinTime` imposes on every reel. Pass an array for per-reel values. This lets one reel land below the shared floor without slamming the whole set. Persists until cleared with `null`. |
| `setDropOrder` | `(order: 'ltr' \| 'rtl' \| 'all' \| number[] \| null, stepMs?: number) => void` | Wraps `setStopDelays`. Common patterns: `'ltr'` (initial cascade reveal), `'all'` (the usual refill), `[0,0,200,200,400]` (V-shape). A named order counts over the reels that spin, so it covers reels added later and orders an `expand()` step by place. |
| `skipSpin` | `(options?: SkipOptions) => void` | The round-aware press. The first press boosts speed (standard mode) or flags refills to auto-slam (cascade mode); later presses free the rest. `options.mode` is what the press does to the reels it frees. `'slam'` places them (the default unless `builder.skipMode()` says otherwise). `'quicken'` asks each for its landing sooner: the tease ends, the delay is cut, and the spin-out and bounce still play, on `options.speed` if one is named. `payload` reaches every phase's `onSkip(ctx)`, rides on `skip:requested` / `skip:completed` beside the `speed` profile, and ends up in `SpinResult.skipContext`. Throws before `setResult()`. Between two `expand()` steps, when nothing spins, the press carries to the next step instead of being dropped. |
| `requestSkip` | `(options?: SkipOptions) => void` | The safe press before `setResult()`. Queues until the result arrives, then presses with the same `options` as `skipSpin`. Bypasses the round-side-effect machine. Between two `expand()` steps it queues for the next step, as `skipSpin()` does there. Either mode is a skip: `skipStage` advances, `wasSkipped` is `true`, `SpinResult.skipMode` says which. A quicken press treats the reels it already quickened as down and walks on to the next group; a slam press cuts them. In cascade mode a quicken slams and warns once with code `quicken-cascade`. |
| `slamStop` | `(options?: { reels?: number[] \| except?: number[] }) => void` | An unconditional slam, whatever the set's `skipMode`. No boost, no auto-slam flag, no tease protection. With `reels` or `except` (not both) it lands only those reels, and every other reel keeps running to a natural landing. Throws before `setResult()`, like `skipSpin()`; a spin whose result will never come is aborted through `spin({ signal })`. |
| `skipNudge` | `(reel?: number) => void` | Fast-forward an in-flight `nudge()` to its landed state. `skipSpin` and `slamStop` land a spin; this lands a nudge. |
| `skipStage` | `readonly 0 \| 1 \| 2` | `0` until the first press of the round, `2` after the press that ended it, in either mode. `1` means a press freed the reels around a protected tease and left the tease running, so the button should stay live; the next press ends it. Decided before the press lands anything, so a `spin:complete` listener already sees `2`. Drive UI labels from this, but gate on `isSpinning` first. The stage is scoped to the round and only resets on the next `spin()`, so an `'always'` round (where no press ever reaches `2`) leaves it parked at `1` through the idle window. |
| `isSpinning` | `readonly boolean` | `true` between `spin:start` and `spin:complete`. In a cascade round it goes true and false once per refill. See the [cascades guide](/mechanics/cascade/#concept). |

```ts
const result = await reelSet.spin({ holdReels: [0, 4] });
console.log(result.symbols);       // final visible grid
console.log(result.wasSkipped);    // true if slam ended the spin
```

#### Cascade (tumble)

Available when the builder was configured with `.tumble({...})`. See the [cascades guide](/mechanics/cascade/#concept) for the mental model.

| Method | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `refill` | `(opts: RefillOptions) => Promise<RefillResult>` | Moment B: place and drop in the survivors and the new symbols. There is no fall and no wait for a result. The default `mode: 'combined'` animates survivors and new symbols together. `mode: 'gravity-then-drop'` splits it into a survivor-settle stage, a hold, then a drop-in stage; see [Two-stage refill](#two-stage-refill) below. Pass `signal: AbortSignal` to cancel mid-refill. Throws without `.tumble()`. The result exposes `winnersRefilled`, `finalGrid`, `wasSkipped`, `duration`. |
| `destroySymbols` | `(cells: ReadonlyArray<Cell>, opts?: DestroySymbolsOptions) => Promise<void>` | Calls each symbol's `playDestroy()` (the default is a brief scale and fade implode). Lifts zIndex so the destroy is not clipped. Optional `delay`, `zIndex`, `dim`, `signal`. |
| `runCascade` | `(opts: RunCascadeOptions) => Promise<RunCascadeResult>` | Runs the whole cascade in one call: detect, destroy, pause, refill, repeat. Pass `signal: AbortSignal` to cancel from the caller. Use it for a slam press between refills, because `reelSet.skipSpin()` does nothing while the engine is idle. The two-stage options apply per chain here: `mode` is called `refillMode`, and `gravityHold` is a function of `info` that builds the promise; `gravityHoldMs` and `onGravityComplete` keep their names. See [Two-stage refill](#two-stage-refill). Per-stage progress comes as `cascade:chain:start` and `cascade:chain:end`; the awaited promise resolves when the chain is over. |

```ts
import type { Cell, RunCascadeResult } from 'pixi-reels';

// Moment A: fall, wait, drop in.
const spinDone = reelSet.spin({ mode: 'cascade' });
reelSet.setResult(await server.spin());
await spinDone;

// Moment B: N refills until no more wins.
const summary: RunCascadeResult = await reelSet.runCascade({
  detectWinners: (grid): Cell[] => myClusterDetector(grid),
  nextGrid:      (_, winners) => server.cascade(winners),
  onCascade:     ({ chain }) => ui.bumpMultiplier(chain),
});
console.log(summary.chainLength, summary.totalWinners, summary.wasSkipped);
```

##### Types

| Type | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Cell` | `{ reel: number; cell: number }` | A grid cell. `reel` is the column, `cell` is the visible cell index. Used by `destroySymbols`, `runCascade`'s `detectWinners`, and `refill({ winners })`. |
| `DestroySymbolsOptions` | `{ delay?, zIndex?, dim?, signal? }` | Defaults: zero delay, zIndex `1000`, no viewport dim. `delay` accepts a number or a `(cell, index) => number` function for a per-cell stagger. Pass `zIndex: null` to suppress the bump, for when another presenter already drove the visual. `signal` aborts mid-destroy and snaps cells to their destroyed pose. |
| `RunCascadeOptions` | `{ detectWinners, nextGrid, presentWinners?, onCascade?, pauseAfterDestroyMs?, maxChain?, destroyOptions?, signal?, refillMode?, gravityHoldMs?, gravityHold?, onGravityComplete? }` | `detectWinners` and `nextGrid` carry the game rules. Everything else is timing, cancellation or gravity feel. Both callbacks may be `async`. `nextGrid` must return `ColumnTarget[]`; a plain `string[][]` is not accepted anywhere in the API, so wrap it with `grid.map((visible) => ({ visible }))`. Defaults: `pauseAfterDestroyMs: 250`, `maxChain: 32`, `refillMode: 'combined'`, `gravityHoldMs: 250`. The `onCascade` payload is `{ chain, winners, currentGrid }`, the same grid `cascade:chain:start` reported. Here `gravityHold` is a function, `(info: { chain, winners }) => Promise<void>`, called once per chain stage; the promise it returns gates that stage's drop-in. `onGravityComplete` is `(info) => void \| Promise<void>` and fires after both hold sources resolve, before the drop-in starts. |
| `RunCascadeResult` | `{ chainLength, totalWinners, finalGrid, wasSkipped }` | Returned by `runCascade`. `chainLength === 0` means no wins on the initial grid (no refill ran). |

```ts
// Cancellation via AbortSignal: the right shape for "player tapped slam
// between refills" (reelSet.skipSpin() is a no-op when the engine is idle).
const controller = new AbortController();
skipBtn.addEventListener('click', () => controller.abort());

const { wasSkipped } = await reelSet.runCascade({
  detectWinners, nextGrid,
  signal: controller.signal,
});
```

`runCascade` also listens to `skip:requested`, so `reelSet.skipSpin()` during a refill works. Only the AbortSignal handles a press in the idle window between refills.

##### Two-stage refill

`refill({ mode: 'gravity-then-drop' })` splits the refill in two. Survivors slide first, then there is a hold across the board for anticipation visuals, then the new symbols enter. This is how Reactoonz, Gates of Olympus and Mummyland refill. `'combined'`, the default, is how Sweet Bonanza and Sugar Rush refill.

```ts
// Single refill: pass the promise directly.
await reelSet.refill({
  winners,
  grid: nextGrid,
  mode: 'gravity-then-drop',
  gravityHoldMs: 150,                 // minimum wall-clock floor (default 250)
  gravityHold: multiplierRoll.done,   // OR an already-in-flight animation
  onGravityComplete: () => sfx.peak(),// awaitable hook between stages
});
```

`gravityHoldMs` and `gravityHold` run in parallel under `Promise.all`, and the drop-in waits for whichever finishes last. Pass both when you want a wall-clock floor under an animation that might be fast. `onGravityComplete` runs after both, so it can read the state after the hold.

```ts
// Per cascade: runCascade calls the builder once per chain stage.
await reelSet.runCascade({
  detectWinners, nextGrid,
  refillMode:    'gravity-then-drop',
  gravityHoldMs: 150,
  gravityHold:   ({ chain }) => multiplier.bumpTo(chain + 1).done,
});
```

The events `cascade:gravity:start`, `cascade:gravity:symbol` and `cascade:gravity:end` fire only in this mode. See the [events reference](/reference/api-events/#cascade-tumble).

If your `gravityHold` promise never resolves, the engine waits forever and the cascade hangs. There is no built-in timeout. If your animation source can stall (an animation library error, missed user input, a hung XHR), wrap it in your own `Promise.race([yourPromise, timeoutReject])` before passing it in, or rely on `gravityHoldMs` alone. A rejection in `gravityHold`, or a throw from `onGravityComplete`, does not reject the `refill()` or `runCascade()` call. The engine catches it, emits `cascade:gravity:error`, logs it and slams to recover, so the awaited promise still resolves. A `try` block never sees it; subscribe to `cascade:gravity:error`.

#### MultiWays

Available when the builder was configured with `.multiways({...})`.

| Method | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `setShape` | `(rowsPerReel: number[]) => void` | Record the row counts each reel should land on this spin. Call it between `spin()` and `setResult()`. |
| `isMultiWaysSlot` | `readonly boolean` | True if the builder used `.multiways(...)`. Read once at startup, not every spin. |

#### Growing the board

Add reels after the last one and take them away again, at rest. `expand()` is the "infinity reels" chain built on them; see the [recipes](/mechanics/infinity-reels/).

| Method | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `addReels` | `(count: number, options?: AddReelsOptions) => readonly Reel[]` | Append `count` reels, laid out, masked and pooled like the built ones; `reelSet.reels` grows in place and the viewport with it. `options.visibleCells` is one number or one per reel (default the last reel's count, or `maxCells` on MultiWays), and `options.initialFrame` is one `ColumnTarget` per reel. A reel may not be taller than the tallest one. The reels one call adds join a `setReelGroups()` layout as one trailing group, take a `setCurve()` curve, and land a pending `setShape()` at the shape they were added with. Fires `reels:added`. |
| `removeReels` | `(count?: number) => void` | Destroy the last `count` reels; without `count`, every reel added since `build()`, a no-op when there are none. Their symbols go back to the pool (an animation still playing on one stops with it), pins on them expire (`'explicit'`), a spotlight hides, groups drop them, and the viewport, mask and pool shrink back. Fires `reels:removed`. |
| `addRows` | `(count: number, options?: AddRowsOptions) => void` | Grow every reel by `count` rows below the last one, at its cell size; the viewport, mask and pool grow with it. `options.cells` is what the new rows show, one array per reel (default random). Between `expand()` steps it goes in `onStepLanded`. Not on MultiWays, where a reel's rows are its shape. Fires `rows:added`. |
| `removeRows` | `(count?: number) => void` | Remove the last `count` rows from every reel; without `count`, every row `addRows()` added, a no-op when there are none. Pins on removed rows expire (`'explicit'`). A big symbol that no longer fits the shorter strip is replaced with random symbols. Fires `rows:removed`. |
| `setColumn` | `(reel: number, column: ColumnTarget, options?: SetColumnOptions) => void` | Show `column` on one reel at rest: it shows `column.visible.length` cells. `options.height` says what gives. `'grow'`, the default, keeps the cell size, so the reel grows or shrinks and the board re-anchors around it (with the default `reelAnchor` of `'center'` it grows both ways). `'keep'` keeps the reel's height and resizes its cells to share it. On MultiWays `'keep'` is the default and the only mode, within `[minCells, maxCells]`. Big symbols get their whole block, as in a landing. A pinned cell has to keep its pinned symbol. Only the cells that change are replaced; every other symbol keeps its instance and animation. Fires `column:set`. |
| `splitSymbol` | `(reel: number, cell: number, ids: string[], options?: SetColumnOptions) => { reelIndex, from, count }` | Split the symbol covering `(reel, cell)`, any symbol one reel wide in full view (a 1x1 or a stack), into `ids`, one per cell. The cells above and below keep their symbols, and a pin below rides down with its symbol. A pinned symbol does not split, and a big symbol in `ids` has to end inside them. `options.height` works as in `setColumn()`: `'grow'` adds the difference to the reel, `'keep'` shrinks its cells. Returns where the new cells are. Implemented through `setColumn()`. |
