| `resetColumns` | `() => void` | Every reel back to the cells it was built or added with, at their size, keeping its top cells. This undoes `setColumn()`, `splitSymbol()` and `addRows()`. A pin past a reel's cells expires, as on `removeRows()`. A no-op when no reel changed. Not on MultiWays. |
| `isExpanding` | `boolean` (getter) | `true` from `expand:start` on: the `spin:*` events a step fires belong to the expansion, not a new round. `false` again by `expand:complete` and `expand:end`, so a listener there can start the next round. |
| `expand` | `(options: ExpandOptions) => Promise<ExpandResult>` | Grow the board by `columns` (one `ColumnTarget` per reel to add; the server decides how many), `step` reels at a time (a number, default `1`, or a function of the step): add them, spin only them, land them, repeat. Awaits `onStepAdded(step)` before each step spins and `onStepLanded(step)` after it lands. `anticipation` teases a step's reels (`true`, `AnticipationOptions`, or a function per step). Aborting `signal` fast-forwards: everything still to come lands in one step. The steps are one round: pin turns are not spent per step, a skip press speeds up the rest once (the fastest profile; in cascade mode the later steps land at once), a press between steps carries to the next one, and delays stagger by place in the step. MultiWays reels take their shape from `visible.length`; a big symbol widens the step it would straddle. Columns, symbol ids, shapes, blocks and an `anticipation` object are validated before the first reel is added. |

`addReels`, `removeReels` and `expand` throw while the reels spin, a nudge runs, or `expand()` runs; `spin()` throws while `expand()` runs. `addRows`, `removeRows`, `setColumn`, `splitSymbol` and `resetColumns` throw while the reels spin or a nudge runs, and inside an expansion they are allowed only between steps (in `onStepLanded`). `setColumn` and `splitSymbol` also throw on a reel that a big symbol wider than one reel covers, because the reels a block spans share one geometry.

| Type | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ExpandStep` | `{ index, from, count, reelCount, fastForward }` | One step: the reels `from .. from + count - 1` it added, the board size after it, and whether it is the fast-forward. |
| `ExpandStepLanded` | `ExpandStep & { result: SpinResult }` | The step after its reels landed; `result.symbols` is the whole board. |
| `ExpandResult` | `{ from, reelCount, steps, symbols, wasSkipped }` | What `expand()` resolves with. |

| Accessor / Method | Signature |
|---|---|
| `speed` | `readonly SpeedManager` |
| `setSpeed` | `(name: string) => void`. Activates a registered profile and emits `speed:changed`. |

#### Spotlight + wins

| Accessor | Description |
|---|---|
| `spotlight` | `SymbolSpotlight`. Dims losers, cycles winning lines, plays per-cell win animations. |

The library also ships [`WinPresenter`](/reference/api-events/), a higher-level win driver that works through events. Listen to `win:start`, `win:group`, `win:symbol` and `win:end`.

#### Pins (persistent cell claims)

| Method | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pin` | `(reel, cell, symbolId, opts?: CellPinOptions) => CellPin` | Place a sticky, expanding or turn-bound pin. Applies immediately if idle, otherwise at the next `setResult()`. |
| `unpin` | `(reel, cell) => void` | Remove a pin. No-op if none. Fires `pin:expired` with reason `'explicit'`. |
| `getPin` | `(reel, cell) => CellPin \| undefined` | A map lookup. |
| `pins` | `readonly ReadonlyMap<string, CellPin>` | Keyed by `"reel:cell"`. Reads are safe at any time. |
| `movePin` | `(from, to, opts?: MovePinOptions) => Promise<void>` | Animate a pin to a new cell at rest. The engine's walking-wild primitive. |
| `setSymbolAt` | `(reel, cell, symbolId) => void` | Swap a single cell in place, at rest. Throws on a pinned cell; call `unpin()` first if you mean it. |

#### Cell / footprint queries

| Method | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `getVisibleGrid` | `() => string[][]` | One id per visible cell. Cross-reel `OCCUPIED` stubs resolve to the big symbol's anchor id. |
| `getTargets` | `() => ColumnTarget[]` | The whole board in the shape `setResult` takes, buffers included and big-symbol anchors at their true positions, so `setResult(reelSet.getTargets())` reproduces it. `getVisibleGrid()` cannot. It reports the visible window only, so a block anchored in `bufferStart` with just its tail showing would replay as an anchor at cell 0 and expand. Read with `getVisibleGrid`, replay with `getTargets`. |
| `getCellBounds` | `(reel, cell) => CellBounds` | ReelSet-local rectangle for a 1x1 cell. Use it for paylines, hit areas and debug overlays. |
| `getBlockBounds` | `(reel, cell) => CellBounds` | Pixel rect covering a big symbol's whole `NxM` block. Returns the cell bounds for a 1x1. |
| `getSymbolFootprint` | `(reel, cell) => { anchor: { reel, cell }; size: { reels, cells } }` | Resolves `OCCUPIED` stubs to the anchor cell and reports the block size. |

#### Random symbol pools

| Accessor | Description |
|---|---|
| `randomSymbols` | `RandomSymbolControl`. `{ set(pool, scope?), clear(), weights(scope?) }`. Narrows what the engine may draw for cells you did not name: globally or per reel, for the whole strip, for both buffer ends, or for one end on its own. |

```ts
// Nothing collectible may sit half-visible above or below the grid.
reelSet.randomSymbols.set({ exclude: ['COIN'] }, { slots: 'buffer' });

// ...or just above it. `bufferStart` is the smaller main coordinate (above
// when vertical, left when horizontal), the same end ColumnTarget names.
reelSet.randomSymbols.set({ exclude: ['COIN'] }, { slots: 'bufferStart' });

// Reel 2 runs hot on wilds for the feature, then back to normal.
reelSet.randomSymbols.set({ weights: { WILD: 40 } }, { reel: 2 });
reelSet.randomSymbols.set(null, { reel: 2 });
```

A pool governs the random draw only. An explicit `setResult` target always
wins. Layers resolve in this order, widest first: base weights, global
spinning, per-reel spinning, global buffer, per-reel buffer, global side,
per-reel side. Weights override per id, exclusions accumulate, and a narrower
layer can never re-admit what a wider one banned. `weights({ slots: 'buffer' })`
reports what both sides inherit; ask for one side to see exactly what it draws
from. The build-time equivalent is `builder.randomSymbols(pool, scope)`.

#### Frame middleware (runtime-mutable)

| Accessor | Description |
|---|---|
| `frame` | `FrameAPI`. `{ use(mw), remove(name), readonly middleware }`. Add or remove `FrameMiddleware` after build (e.g. feature-mode strip swaps). |

```ts
reelSet.frame.use(featureWildsMiddleware);
// ... feature exit
reelSet.frame.remove('feature-wilds');
```

#### Reel access

| Accessor | Returns |
|---|---|
| `reels` | `readonly Reel[]` |
| `getReel(i)` | `Reel`. The per-column surface: `getSymbolAt`, `getVisibleSymbols`, `events`, `setSymbolAt` and so on. |

#### Events

`reelSet.events` is a typed `EventEmitter<ReelSetEvents>`. See the [events reference](/reference/api-events/) for the full surface. Per-reel events live on `reel.events`.

```ts
reelSet.events.on('spin:complete', (r) => console.log(r.symbols));
reelSet.events.on('cascade:dropIn:symbol', squishOnLand);
reelSet.events.off('cascade:dropIn:symbol', squishOnLand); // unsubscribe
```

#### Lifecycle

| Accessor / Method | Notes |
|---|---|
| `isDestroyed` | `readonly boolean` |
| `destroy()` | Releases pooled symbols, removes ticker callbacks, tears down pin overlays, removes all listeners. Cascades to every child (`{ children: true }`). |

#### Example: minimal cascade slot

```ts
import { ReelSetBuilder, SpriteSymbol } from 'pixi-reels';

const reelSet = new ReelSetBuilder()
  .reels(6).visibleCells(5).symbolSize(95, 95).symbolGap(5, 5)
  .symbols((r) => { /* register your sprites */ })
  .tumble({
    fall:   { duration: 280, ease: 'sine.in',       cellStagger: 40 },
    dropIn: { duration: 480, ease: 'back.out(1.6)', cellStagger: 50 },
  })
  .ticker(app.ticker)
  .build();
app.stage.addChild(reelSet);

const spinDone = reelSet.spin();
reelSet.setResult(await server.spin());
await spinDone;

await reelSet.runCascade({
  detectWinners: detectWins,
  nextGrid:      (_, winners) => server.cascade(winners),
});
```

### Glossary
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/glossary/
Definitions of slot vocabulary and of the names pixi-reels gives its parts.

Two groups of terms are mixed here: slot vocabulary, which every slot uses whatever the library, and library-specific names, which are what pixi-reels calls its pieces. If a word reads as jargon, it is probably defined here; search the page.

#### Slot vocabulary

**Anticipation**. A slow-down on one reel to build tension. The classic pattern: two scatters are already on screen, so the last reel or two decelerate slowly to make the player hope for a third.

**Base game**. The normal spin mode, as opposed to a bonus round like free spins or Hold & Win.

**Bet**. The amount staked per spin. Not modeled by pixi-reels; it is a number in your game code.

**Bonus**. Any secondary game mode triggered off the base game (free spins, Hold & Win, pick-a-prize, etc.).

**Cascade (tumble)**. A chain mechanic: winning symbols disappear, the remaining ones fall, gaps fill from above, wins are checked again, repeat. Candy Crush with a paytable.

**Cluster win**. A win shape where N or more adjacent matching symbols (orthogonally connected) pay, regardless of row or column. Compare with "line win".

**Free spins (FS)**. A bonus round where the player gets a fixed number of spins at no cost. Often includes sticky wilds, multipliers or expanding wilds.

**Grid**. The two-dimensional snapshot of visible symbols, indexed `grid[reelIndex][cellIndex]`. A 5x3 slot has a 5x3 grid.

**Hold & Win (Link & Win, Respin)**. A bonus round where special "coin" symbols lock in place when they land, and the respins continue until no new coin lands, or the whole grid fills and pays a jackpot.

**Line win**. A win paid for N or more matching symbols on a payline (usually left to right on a fixed row).

**Multiplier**. A number applied to a win. Often grows with consecutive cascades.

**Near-miss**. A result that almost triggered a big win (two scatters on screen, the third just off the visible window). A retention trick.

**Paytable**. The map from winning combinations to payouts. Lives on the server, not in this library.

**Payline**. A fixed path through the grid (row 1, zigzag, V-shape) where matching symbols pay.

**Reel**. One vertical column of symbols.

**Reel strip**. The long, invisible list of symbols a reel draws from. Not exposed by pixi-reels directly; the engine asks a frame middleware chain for the next symbol.

**Respin**. A spin where some reels are held in place and only the others move. A single-reel respin holds every reel except one; a Hold & Win respin holds every "coin" cell.

**RTP (Return To Player)**. The expected long-run payout percentage (e.g. 96%). Determined by the paytable and reel strips on the server.

**Scatter**. A symbol that pays regardless of position and usually triggers the bonus. Unlike line wins, scatters count wherever they land.

**Slam-stop (skip)**. The player presses the spin button a second time and the reels land immediately. In pixi-reels this is `reelSet.skipSpin()`.

**Spin**. One turn of the reels. In this library the lifecycle runs `START`, `SPIN`, optionally `ANTICIPATION`, `STOP`, then `IDLE`.

**Stacked symbol**. A symbol that fills several rows of the same reel in a single column. Often wilds.

**Sticky wild**. A wild that, once it lands, stays in place for the remaining spins of a round.

**Symbol**. One cell on a reel. A graphic: a sprite, an animated sprite, a Spine skeleton, or a custom drawing.

**Turbo / Super-turbo**. Faster spin profiles. Same outcome, less wait.

**Walking wild**. A wild that moves one column per respin and typically triggers free respins along the way.

**Wild**. Substitutes for other symbols to complete wins. Usually cannot substitute for scatters.

**Win spotlight**. The visual highlight on winning cells, which pixi-reels ships as `SymbolSpotlight.show()` / `.cycle()`.

#### Library-specific names

**`ReelSet`**. The top-level object, the whole slot board: a PixiJS container that holds the reels, the spin controller, the speed manager and the spotlight. You build one with `new ReelSetBuilder()...build()` and `addChild` it to your stage.

**`ReelSetBuilder`**. A fluent builder (chainable methods) that turns a pile of config into a `ReelSet`. It checks every required call at `.build()` time, so you cannot forget to wire a piece.

**`Reel`**. One column. Owns the symbols currently on screen, their vertical motion, and the "land on this frame" logic.

**`ReelSymbol`**. The abstract base class for a single cell. Subclass it to draw whatever you like: `SpriteSymbol` for plain sprites, `AnimatedSpriteSymbol` for sprite sheets, `SpineSymbol` for Spine skeletons, or your own.

**`ReelViewport`**. The clipping and layering container. Holds the mask (so symbols that scroll above or below the visible area do not leak) plus a "promoted" layer where winning symbols are lifted above the mask for a celebration animation.

**Spin controller (internal)**. Drives every reel through its lifecycle phases, coordinates `setResult()`, and emits events. `ReelSet` wires it; you never construct one. Since 1.0 it is not exported from the package entry.

**`ReelPhase`**. A single stage in a reel's life during a spin. The built-in phases cover the wind-up, the constant-speed blur, the optional anticipation slow-down, and the decelerate, snap and bounce stop. Add your own by extending `ReelPhase` and registering it through the `PhaseFactory` callback in `builder.phases(f => f.register('name', MyPhase))`. The built-in phase classes are exported too, so you can subclass or replace one. Their config types (`StartPhaseConfig`, `SpinPhaseConfig`, etc.) are the stable part of that surface.

**`SpinningMode`**. The per-frame motion strategy: one method, `computeDelta(slotPitch, speed, deltaMs)`, returning how far the strip travels this frame. `StandardMode` is the default. `CascadeMode` multiplies by a gravity factor (1.5) and caps the step at one slot pitch. `ImmediateMode` returns 0, so the phase places symbols directly. Not the same thing as `spin({ mode: 'standard' | 'cascade' })`, which picks the phase chain.

**`SpeedManager`**. Holds named `SpeedProfile` objects (timings, easings, bounce distance). Switch profiles at runtime with `reelSet.setSpeed('turbo')`.

**`SymbolSpotlight`**. The win-animation primitive. Dims non-winners, promotes winners above the mask, runs `playWin()` on each, and can cycle through multiple lines.

**`FrameBuilder` / middleware**. A small middleware pipeline that fills a reel's whole frame (buffer start, visible cells, buffer end) with symbol ids each time the engine builds one. Intercept it for rules like no three in a row, or a mystery symbol every seventh frame.

**`ObjectPool<T>`**. The reuse bucket behind every symbol. Scrolling a 5x3 board for 5 seconds allocates no new `ReelSymbol` objects; they come from the pool and go back to it.

**`EventEmitter`**. Typed pub/sub. Events are namespaced with colons (`spin:start`, `spin:reelLanded`, `speed:changed`). Every exit path from a spin fires an event, so wire audio, HUD and analytics to events rather than to method calls.

**`TickerRef`**. A safe wrapper around `PIXI.Ticker`. Tracks every callback it adds and removes them all on destroy. Never call `ticker.add()` directly in this codebase.

**`Disposable`**. The interface every resource-holding class implements. `destroy()` cascades through the composition tree, so one `reelSet.destroy()` cleans up the whole scene.

**`enableDebug(reelSet)`**. Attaches `window.__PIXI_REELS_DEBUG` with `.log()`, `.snapshot()`, `.grid()`, `.trace()`, `.metrics()`. It is the only way to inspect reel state through a `canvas`, including from an AI agent.

**`debugOverlay(reelSet)`**. The same state drawn on the canvas: cells, mask, travel axis, a per-reel hud, a metrics plaque and a phase timeline per spin. Ships at `pixi-reels/debug` and draws with `pixi-silk`, an optional peer, so only a debug build pays for it. `SpinMetrics` is the per-round recorder behind it, `DebugPlaque` the readout plate it and the recipes are built from.

**`CellPin`**. The cell-persistence primitive. Lock a symbol id to a cell with `reelSet.pin(reel, cell, id)`; the engine acquires an overlay during the spin, migrates the cell on a reshape, and supports an animated `movePin(from, to)` tween. Works with any `ReelSymbol` subclass; it is not Spine-specific.

**`RefillOptions` / `RefillResult`**. The typed pair around `reelSet.refill(opts)`. Pass `{ winners, grid, mode?, signal? }`; receive `{ winnersRefilled, finalGrid, wasSkipped, duration }`. Mirrors the shape of `RunCascadeOptions` / `RunCascadeResult`.

**`RunCascadeOptions` / `RunCascadeResult`**. The pair around `reelSet.runCascade(opts)`. The two required callbacks (`detectWinners`, `nextGrid`) encode the game rules; the result reports `chainLength`, `totalWinners`, `finalGrid` and `wasSkipped`. `signal: AbortSignal` lets the caller slam mid-chain.

**`createTestReelSet`**. The headless harness. Builds a `ReelSet` with a `FakeTicker` and a `HeadlessSymbol`, so you can run a full spin lifecycle in Node, with no DOM or canvas, and assert on the final grid. Since 1.0 it ships at the `pixi-reels/testing` subpath, so the harness stays out of production bundles.

**`CheatEngine` (outside the library)**. A deterministic outcome generator used by the recipes and by the library's own integration tests. Lives in the private `@pixi-reels/cheats` workspace package, not in the library. ADR 009 covers why.

**Changeset**. A small markdown file under `.changeset/` describing a release-worthy change and which package(s) to bump. Generated by `pnpm changeset`; consumed by the release workflow to version and publish.

**Snapshot release**. A short-lived npm publish stamped `<base>-<tag>-<timestamp>` under a per-branch dist-tag. Every push to a non-main branch creates one, so reviewers can `pnpm add pixi-reels@<branch-tag>` and test.

### Migrating to 1.0.0
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/migrating-to-1-0/
Mechanical changes to move from 0.x to 1.0.0. Every breaking change with a before and after.

This page covers the 0.x to 1.0.0 step. Its `After` snippets are written in v2
form so they still run today, but several names changed again in 2.0.0. Do this
page's rewrites first, then [Migrating to 2.0](/reference/migrating-to-2-0/),
which starts with a codemod that handles the mechanical half.

Every breaking change in 1.0.0 is below with a before and after snippet. Each section is mechanical: find the pattern, apply the rewrite. Every pre-1.0 pattern appears verbatim in a `Before` code block, so a `git grep skip()` or `git grep visibleSymbols` in your repo lands on the matching rewrite here.

#### visibleSymbols is gone

The deprecated `visibleSymbols` builder setter is removed. It aliased `visibleRows`, which 2.0.0 renamed again to `visibleCells`. Replace every call:

Before:

```ts
// Pre-1.0 code: .visibleSymbols(3) is removed in 1.0.
builder
  .reels(5)
  .visibleSymbols(3);
```

After:

```ts
builder.reels(5).visibleCells(3);
```

#### setResult and initialFrame accept only ColumnTarget[]

The legacy `string[][]` form is removed, including the negative-index buffer-above mutation pattern. `ReelSet.setResult` and `ReelSetBuilder.initialFrame` accept only `ColumnTarget[]`.

Before (legacy form with a buffer-above prefill):

```ts
// Pre-1.0 code. Will not type-check against 1.0.
const grid: string[][] = [
  ['A', 'B', 'C'],
  ['A', 'B', 'C'],
];
// Buffer-above slot 0 was set via negative-index property assignment:
(grid[1] as any)[-1] = 'COIN';
reelSet.setResult(grid);
```

After:

```ts
reelSet.setResult([
  { visible: ['A', 'B', 'C'] },
  { visible: ['A', 'B', 'C'], bufferStart: ['COIN'] },
]);
```

If your server returns a plain `string[][]` of visible rows, convert at the boundary:

```ts
const response: string[][] = await server.spin();
reelSet.setResult(response.map((visible) => ({ visible })));
```

The same conversion applies to `ReelSetBuilder.initialFrame(...)` and to the `grid` field passed to `ReelSet.refill(...)`.

#### Hidden exports from the package entry

Eight types and classes are no longer re-exported from `pixi-reels`. They remain in the source tree but are not part of the public API.

| Removed export | What it was | Replacement |
|---|---|---|
| `OCCUPIED_SENTINEL` | The cross-reel stub the engine paints into big-symbol non-anchor cells | Never produce or consume directly. `ReelSet.getVisibleGrid()` resolves stubs to anchor ids. |
| `ReelMotion` | Per-`Reel` Y-displacement and wrap helper | Wired by `Reel` itself. |
| `StopSequencer` | Per-`Reel` target-frame manager | Wired by `Reel` itself. |
| `ReelSetInternalConfig` | Shape internal to the builder-to-engine handoff | Use `ReelSetBuilder` to wire a `ReelSet`. |
| `ResolvedReelGridConfig` | Same | Same. |
| `SymbolFactory` | Pooling layer for symbol instances | Register symbol classes via `builder.symbols(registry => ...)`. |
| `RandomSymbolProvider` | Weighted symbol picker | Pass weights via `builder.weights({...})`. |
| `OffsetCalculator` | Geometry helper for `ReelViewport` | Internal. |

If you imported any of these from `pixi-reels`, remove the import. If you need the internal, import it from the source path; internals can change without a major bump.

#### SpinController and the built-in phase classes are hidden

`SpinController`, `SpinControllerHooks` and the built-in phase classes (`StartPhase`, `SpinPhase`, `StopPhase`, `AnticipationPhase`, `AdjustPhase`, `CascadeFallPhase`, `CascadePlacePhase`, `CascadeDropInPhase`) are no longer exported. `ReelSet` wires the controller itself, so a game never constructs one. A custom phase extends `ReelPhase` rather than a built-in; the built-ins were not designed for subclassing.

The phase config types (`StartPhaseConfig`, `SpinPhaseConfig` and the rest) stay exported as stable shape descriptions.

Before:

```ts
// Pre-1.0 code. Removed in 1.0.
import { SpinController, StartPhase, SpinPhase } from 'pixi-reels';

class MyStartPhase extends StartPhase {
  // ...
}
```

After:

```ts
import { ReelPhase, type StartPhaseConfig } from 'pixi-reels';

class MyStartPhase extends ReelPhase<StartPhaseConfig> {
  // ...
}

builder.phases((f) => f.register('start', MyStartPhase));
```

#### Internal-leaking methods lost their leading underscore

Three methods on `Reel` and `ReelSet` were called across files under the underscore convention. They lose the underscore, and their JSDoc now names the call sites.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `Reel._getAnchorCell(visibleRow)` | `Reel.getAnchorCell(visibleCell)` |
| `ReelSet._peekTargetShape()` | `ReelSet.peekTargetShape()` |
| `ReelSet._clearTargetShape()` | `ReelSet.clearTargetShape()` |

Do not call these from a game. They are marked `@internal` and stripped from the published `.d.ts` (next section).

#### Internal methods stripped from .d.ts (`stripInternal`)

`tsconfig.json` now sets `"stripInternal": true`. Methods marked `@internal` in JSDoc stay in the runtime JS, so the engine's own cross-file callers keep working, but they are absent from the published `.d.ts` and no longer show up in autocomplete.

Affected methods on `Reel`:

- `setStopFrame`, `setCrossReelResolver`, `getAnchorCell`, `notifySpinStart`, `notifySpinEnd`, `notifyLanded`, `snapToGrid`, `reshape`.

If your code typechecked against `Reel.reshape(...)` or any of the above, switch to the public alternative:

- For reshape, `reelSet.setShape([...])`. It only runs on a MultiWays slot and migrates pins in the same step.
- For grid inspection, `reelSet.getVisibleGrid()`, `reelSet.getSymbolFootprint()` and `reelSet.getBlockBounds()`.

#### skip is now skipSpin

`skip()` is renamed `skipSpin()`, so it reads alongside `skipNudge()`. `slamStop()` is unchanged: it lands now, unconditionally, with no boost.

Before:

```ts
// Pre-1.0 code: reelSet.skip() is removed in 1.0.
reelSet.skip();
```

After:

```ts
reelSet.skipSpin();
```

The three actions side by side:

```ts
reelSet.skipSpin();   // Round-aware spin land. Applies the boost / auto-slam side effect.
reelSet.skipNudge();  // Fast-forward an in-flight nudge() to its landed position.
reelSet.slamStop();   // Unconditional land-now. No boost. For tests, anti-cheat.
```

#### refill() returns RefillResult, accepts a signal

`reelSet.refill()` takes a `RefillOptions` object and returns a `RefillResult`, shaped like the result of `runCascade`, instead of a `SpinResult`. A caller that discards the return value keeps working.

Before:

```ts
// Pre-1.0: refill returned SpinResult.
const result: SpinResult = await reelSet.refill({ winners, grid });
console.log(result.symbols); // string[][]
```

After:

```ts
import type { RefillOptions, RefillResult } from 'pixi-reels';

const result: RefillResult = await reelSet.refill({
  winners,
  grid,
  signal: ac.signal, // new: abort mid-refill, the await unblocks immediately
});
console.log(result.finalGrid, result.winnersRefilled, result.wasSkipped);
```

`finalGrid` and `wasSkipped` are the same fields `RunCascadeResult` has. `winnersRefilled` and `duration` belong to a refill and cover one stage.

#### Testing utilities moved to pixi-reels/testing

The headless harness is a separate subpath export, so a production bundle never pulls it in, even when tree-shaking is imperfect.

Before:

```ts
// Pre-1.0. Removed from the main entry in 1.0.
import {
  createTestReelSet,
  FakeTicker,
  HeadlessSymbol,
  spinAndLand,
  captureEvents,
  expectGrid,
  countSymbol,
} from 'pixi-reels';
```

After:

```ts
import {
  createTestReelSet,
  FakeTicker,
  HeadlessSymbol,
  spinAndLand,
  captureEvents,
  expectGrid,
  countSymbol,
} from 'pixi-reels/testing';
```

The types (`TestReelSetOptions`, `TestReelSetHandle`) move with them. The Spine subpath (`pixi-reels/spine`) is unchanged.

#### Concurrent calls during nudge() now throw

`spin()`, `setResult()`, `pin()` and `setShape()` throw while a `nudge()` is still tweening. Await the nudge promise before calling any of them.

Before (undefined behavior, no error):

```ts
const nudging = reelSet.nudge(2, { distance: 1, direction: 'forward', incoming: ['wild'] });
// reelSet.spin() here used to race the nudge tween silently.
```

After (the engine throws "ReelSet.spin: cannot be called while nudge() is in flight."):

```ts
const nudging = reelSet.nudge(2, { distance: 1, direction: 'forward', incoming: ['wild'] });
await nudging;
await reelSet.spin();
```

If your UI lets the player press spin during a nudge, call `reelSet.skipNudge()` first, which fast-forwards the nudge to its landed position, then call `spin()`.

#### symbol:recycled event removed

The `'symbol:recycled'` field on the per-reel `ReelEvents` interface is removed. Nothing ever emitted it. Delete any listener you registered for it.

#### /guides/spine-pins/ renamed to /guides/pins/

A pin works with `SpriteSymbol`, `AnimatedSpriteSymbol`, `SpineSymbol` or any other `ReelSymbol` subclass, so the old URL was misleading. The page is now at `/guides/pins/`. The old path redirects permanently, so bookmarks keep working.

### Migrating to 2.0.0
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/migrating-to-2-0/
Every breaking change in 2.0.0, with a before and after. Rows became cells, above/below became start/end, and one codemod does most of it.

Run the codemod first. It has not reached npm yet, so run it from a clone of
this repo:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/schmooky/pixi-reels
cd pixi-reels && pnpm install
node packages/pixi-reels-codemod/bin/cli.js v1-to-v2 /path/to/your/src
```

Add `--dry --print` to see the rewrite without touching anything. The codemod
edits in place, so commit before you run it for real. Then read this page for
the things a codemod cannot do.

#### Why any of this

v2 has one engine for four layouts: vertical or horizontal, forward or
reverse. Once a strip can run sideways, "row" stops describing anything, so a
reel's strip is made of cells, and the off-window slots at either side are
start and end.

Start and end are geometric. Start is the smaller screen coordinate (above on
a vertical reel, left on a horizontal one), whichever way the reel travels.
They do not follow travel because a buffer symbol is presentation, a coin
peeking above the top row, and flipping a reel's direction must not move that
coin to the opposite edge.

There are no deprecated aliases. A v1 name either fails to compile or throws
with a message naming its replacement. A quiet alias would let a `bufferAbove`
that now means something different reach production.

#### Geometry

Before:

```ts
new ReelSetBuilder()
  .reels(5)
  .visibleRows(3)
  .visibleRowsPerReel([3, 5, 5, 5, 3])
  .reelPixelHeights([300, 500, 500, 500, 300])
  .reelAnchor('bottom')   // or 'top'
  .bufferSymbols({ above: 1, below: 0 });
```

After:

```ts
new ReelSetBuilder()
  .reels(5)
  .visibleCells(3)
  .visibleCellsPerReel([3, 5, 5, 5, 3])
  .reelExtents([300, 500, 500, 500, 300])
  .reelAnchor('end')      // or 'start'
  .bufferSymbols({ start: 1, end: 0 });
```

On `Reel`: `reelHeight` is `extent`, `offsetY` is `mainOffset`,
`spinSymbolHeight` is `spinCellSize`, `bufferAbove` / `bufferBelow` are
`bufferStart` / `bufferEnd`.

`Reel.symbolWidth` and `Reel.symbolHeight` are unchanged. They are the
screen-space pair you hand to `ReelSymbol.resize(width, height)`, and
screen-space inputs stay screen-space in v2.

##### MultiWays

All three keys were renamed, and the builder throws on the old ones:

```ts
// Before
builder.multiways({ minRows: 2, maxRows: 7, reelPixelHeight: 700 });
// After
builder.multiways({ minCells: 2, maxCells: 7, reelExtent: 700 });
```

`setShape()` takes the same array, cells per reel.

#### Result grids

Before:

```ts
reelSet.setResult([
  { visible: ['A', 'B', 'C'], bufferAbove: ['COIN'], bufferBelow: ['X'] },
]);
```

After:

```ts
reelSet.setResult([
  { visible: ['A', 'B', 'C'], bufferStart: ['COIN'], bufferEnd: ['X'] },
]);
```

A `ColumnTarget` now travels unchanged all the way down to the reel. The
internal negative-index encoding, `arr[-1]` for a buffer-above slot, is gone.
In a custom frame middleware, `FrameContext.targetSymbols` (a `string[]`) is
now `FrameContext.target` (a `ColumnTarget`). Read one cell of it with
`getTargetSlot(target, cell)`, or materialize the strip with
`columnTargetToStrip(target, bufferStart)`.

`Reel.placeSymbols` takes a `ColumnTarget` instead of a `string[]`. If you
had a full strip frame, buffers included, use the new `Reel.placeStrip`.

#### Coordinates

Every `(col, row)` pair is now `(reel, cell)`:

Before:

```ts
reelSet.pin(2, 1, 'wild');
const p = reelSet.getPin(2, 1);
console.log(p.col, p.row, p.originRow);

reelSet.events.on('cascade:chain:end', (e) => e.winners.forEach((w) => w.row));
reelSet.events.on('pin:migrated', (m) => console.log(m.fromRow, m.toRow));
```

After:

```ts
reelSet.pin(2, 1, 'wild');
const p = reelSet.getPin(2, 1);
console.log(p.reel, p.cell, p.originCell);

reelSet.events.on('cascade:chain:end', (e) => e.winners.forEach((w) => w.cell));
reelSet.events.on('pin:migrated', (m) => console.log(m.fromCell, m.toCell));
```

The positional arguments did not move, only the names. `SymbolPosition.rowIndex`
is `cellIndex`, and it gains an optional `setId` for a game that composes more
than one reel set.

`BoardGrid` and `HoldAndWinBoard` keep `cols` and `rows` as board dimensions,
because a board is a real 2-D grid. Only their cell coordinates changed:
`BoardCell` and `HwCell` are `{ reel, cell }`.

#### Big symbols

`SymbolData.size` was `{ w, h }`, which became ambiguous once a reel could run
sideways. It is now `{ reels, cells }`: `reels` spans columns and `cells` spans
the strip, in every orientation.

Before:

```ts
builder.symbolData({ bonus: { weight: 0, size: { w: 2, h: 2 } } });
const fp = reelSet.getSymbolFootprint(2, 1);
console.log(fp.anchor.col, fp.size.w);
```

After:

```ts
builder.symbolData({ bonus: { weight: 0, size: { reels: 2, cells: 2 } } });
const fp = reelSet.getSymbolFootprint(2, 1);
console.log(fp.anchor.reel, fp.size.reels);
```

`getBlockBounds` still returns screen-space `{ x, y, width, height }`.

One restriction is new. A cross-reel block (`size.reels > 1`) cannot be
combined with a mixed `directionPerReel([...])`. The coordinator assumes one
shared feed edge across the reels a block covers, so `build()` throws instead
of shipping a block that would split at run time. Use a single `direction()`,
or keep blocks within one reel.

#### Cascades

Before:

```ts
builder.tumble({
  fall: { rowStagger: 40, rowOrder: 'bottomToTop' },
  dropIn: { rowStagger: 30, rowOrder: 'topToBottom' },
});
reelSet.events.on('cascade:place:end', (e) => console.log(e.winnerRows));
```

After:

```ts
builder.tumble({
  fall: { cellStagger: 40, cellOrder: 'endFirst' },
  dropIn: { cellStagger: 30, cellOrder: 'startFirst' },
});
reelSet.events.on('cascade:place:end', (e) => console.log(e.winnerCells));
```

`'endFirst'` is what `'bottomToTop'` meant: the cell at the gravity-exit
edge moves first. `DropOffset.originalRow` / `.offsetRows` are
`.originalCell` / `.offsetCells`.

`DropOffset` also gains `isNew`. If you branched on `originalCell < 0` to
tell an arriving symbol from a surviving one, switch to `isNew`. The sign
test only holds under forward gravity.

##### Cascades on a reverse or horizontal set

`tumble()` takes a `gravity` option. The default, `'auto'`, follows each
reel's own direction, so a reverse or horizontal cascade needs nothing extra.
Set it only when the tumble should settle against the reel's travel:

```ts
builder.direction('reverse').tumble({});        // drains up, refills from below
builder.orientation('horizontal').tumble({});   // drains right, refills from the left
builder.tumble({ gravity: 'reverse' });         // spin one way, drop the other
```

Whichever edge gravity exits by is the edge your server must pack survivors
against in the grids it returns. The engine animates the result and does not
reorder it. On a `'reverse'` cascade that means survivors first and new
symbols at the end of each column, the mirror of the v1 convention.

#### Nudge

`direction` is now relative to the reel's own axis, not to the screen:

Before:

```ts
await reelSet.nudge(2, { distance: 1, direction: 'down', incoming: ['wild'] });
```

After:

```ts
await reelSet.nudge(2, { distance: 1, direction: 'forward', incoming: ['wild'] });
```

`'up'` became `'reverse'` by the same rule. `NudgeOptions.direction` is
`'forward' | 'reverse'`, with no screen-relative values left.

On a vertical forward reel these are the same motion. On a reel built with
`direction('reverse')`, `'forward'` now travels the way that reel spins and
feeds from the matching edge. In v1 it always fed from the top.

#### Motion internals

If you wrote a custom `SpinningMode` or phase:

| v1 | v2 |
|---|---|
| `ReelMotion.displace(deltaY)` | `.advance(travelDelta)`, a signed travel distance, not screen pixels |
| `ReelMotion.slotHeight` | `.slotPitch` |
| `ReelMotion.getRowY(row)` | `.getCellMain(cell)` |
| `SpinningMode.computeDeltaY(symbolHeight, ...)` | `.computeDelta(slotPitch, ...)` |

A positive `travelDelta` means forward for this reel, and the axis turns that
into a screen direction. Your mode no longer needs to know which way the reel
points.

`ReelMotion`'s wrap callback lost its `arrayIndex` and `direction`
arguments. Nothing read them; the consumer derives position from the symbol
itself.

#### Offsets

`OffsetXMode` is `CrossOffsetMode`, and the trapezoid's
`topWidthFactor` / `bottomWidthFactor` are `startFactor` / `endFactor`.

#### The horizontal reel classes are gone

`HorizontalReel`, `HorizontalReelBuilder`, `HorizontalReelConfig`,
`HorizontalDirection` and `HorizontalReelEvents` were deleted. A sideways
banner is now a `ReelSet` whose strip travels along X.

```ts
// Before
const banner = new HorizontalReelBuilder()
  .visibleCount(5)
  .symbols((r) => { /* ... */ })
  .ticker(app.ticker)
  .build();

// After
const banner = new ReelSetBuilder()
  .orientation('horizontal')
  .reels(1)              // one strip
  .visibleCells(5)       // 5 symbols along it
  .symbols((r) => { /* ... */ })
  .ticker(app.ticker)
  .build();
```

Everything else carries over. `spin()` returns the same promise,
`setResult([{ visible: ids }])` takes the same `ColumnTarget[]`, and
`refill`, `runCascade` and `destroySymbols` work on it as on the main board.
Add the built set to the stage yourself; there is no composition layer.

The codemod does not rewrite this one, because the shapes are too different.
It is the one migration you do by hand.

#### Motion blur follows travel now

`MotionBlurOptions.axis` used to default to `'y'`, and its docs told you to
pass `{ axis: 'x' }` for a `HorizontalReel`, the class that no longer exists.
A horizontal set using `StaticSpinSymbol` therefore smeared across its
direction of travel, with no warning.

The axis now defaults to the owning set's orientation. If you passed
`{ axis: 'x' }` to work around the old default, delete it. If you want a
cross-smear, keep it; an explicit value still wins.

#### Custom mask strategies

This only matters if you passed your own `maskStrategy(...)`. The two built-in
strategies are unchanged.

Both methods now take a single `MaskContext` instead of positional
arguments, and the context carries the axis:

Before:

```ts
const strategy: MaskStrategy = {
  build: (rects, totalWidth, totalHeight) => { /* ... */ },
  update: (g, rects, totalWidth, totalHeight) => { /* ... */ },
};
```

After:

```ts
import { MASK_STRATEGY_VERSION, type MaskStrategy } from 'pixi-reels';

const strategy: MaskStrategy = {
  version: MASK_STRATEGY_VERSION,
  build: ({ rects, width, height, axis }) => { /* ... */ },
  update: (g, { rects, width, height, axis }) => { /* ... */ },
};
```

`maskStrategy()` throws on any strategy that does not declare version 2. The
field is there because a `ReelMaskRect` is screen-space: on a vertical set the
strip runs along `y` and `height`, on a horizontal set along `x` and `width`.
A v1 strategy written for one rect per column, with height equal to the
visible window, would receive the same struct with a transposed meaning and no
compile error to catch it. A v1 strategy handed a `MaskContext` would also read
`rects` as an object, find no `.length`, and draw a full-bleed rect that clips
nothing.

If your strategy unions the rects it is given and assumes no axis, adding the
field is the whole migration. If it assumes an axis, branch on `axis.mainProp`
or `axis.toLocal(width, height)`.

#### gsap is now per reel set

v1 kept one gsap instance in a module global; the last `setGsap` call won.
With a single `ReelSet` that was harmless. With two, the second `build()`
moved the first set's tweens onto a different timeline without warning.

`builder.gsap(instance)` now binds that set only, at `build()` time. Nothing
changes for a single-set game that never calls it.

Two consequences:

```ts
// Before: driveGsapWithTicker looked the instance up from the global.
const stop = driveGsapWithTicker(app.ticker);

// After: pass the SAME instance you gave the builder.
const stop = driveGsapWithTicker(app.ticker, myGsap);
```

Omit the second argument only if you never called `.gsap(...)` either.

In a custom `ReelSymbol` subclass, animate on `this.gsap` rather than an
imported `gsap`:

```ts
class MySymbol extends ReelSymbol {
  async playWin() {
    // `this.gsap` is the owning set's instance, bound by SymbolFactory.
    await this.gsap.to(this.view.scale, { x: 1.2, y: 1.2, duration: 0.2 });
  }
}
```

An imported `gsap` still works when your app and the engine resolve to the
same module. `this.gsap` is correct whether they do or not.

#### Render order

This one is new and optional. `cellStacking` and `reelStacking` make render
order explicit:

```ts
builder.cellStacking('ascending').reelStacking('ascending');  // the defaults
```

`'ascending'` is the v1 behaviour: the cell or reel at the larger coordinate
draws in front. The order is geometric, so `direction('reverse')` does not
flip it. Art lit from above keeps overlapping the way it was drawn, and a
per-spin reversal tease does not re-layer the board. Pass `'descending'` if
your art wants the opposite.

#### Cascade grids are validated now

`refill()` and `runCascade()`'s `nextGrid` run the same checks `setResult()`
always did: shape, v1 option keys, and buffer counts that fit the reels.

They previously checked nothing. A grid still carrying `bufferAbove` was read
for `bufferStart`, came back `undefined`, and was random-filled with no
warning, on every stage of the chain. If a cascade of yours has been dropping
a peeking symbol, this is why. It now throws. Errors name their own entry
point, so a bad `nextGrid` says `runCascade(): nextGrid` rather than
`refill()`.

#### The debug snapshot follows the travel axis

`debugSnapshot()`'s `reels[].allSymbols[].y` is now `.main`, the coordinate
along that reel's travel axis, and each reel reports its `orientation` and
`direction`:

```ts
// Before
snap.reels[0].allSymbols[0].y
// After
snap.reels[0].allSymbols[0].main
snap.reels[0].orientation  // 'vertical' | 'horizontal'
```

The old field was hard-coded to `view.y`, so on a horizontal set every
symbol reported a constant `0`.

#### The v1 rename tables are no longer exported

`CODEMOD_HINT`, `V1_BUILDER_METHODS`, `V1_OPTION_KEYS` and
`V1_OPTION_VALUES` were public in the pre-release. They are 1.x migration
scaffolding, and exporting them would have pinned that scaffolding into all
of 2.x.

Nothing you write needs them. The guards still read the table internally,
and every throw names the replacement and the codemod. If you built your own
migration tooling against these, copy the pairs you need out of
[the tables above](#geometry); they are frozen.

`Gsap` is now exported, so you can name the type you pass to
`driveGsapWithTicker(ticker, gsap)` and `ReelConfig.gsap`.

#### The example apps left the repo

`examples/` is gone. The standalone demo apps live in their own repo now, and
the runnable demos are on this site under [`/recipes`](/mechanics/), about
130 of them, each with its source alongside.

Nothing in the published package changed; `examples/` was never in the
tarball. This only matters if you were importing reference code out of the
repo, which the old README encouraged. Where it went:

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| `examples/shared/BlurSpriteSymbol.ts`, `CoinSymbol.ts`, the Spine loaders, `prototypeSpriteLoader.ts` | `packages/kit/src/` (same filenames), published as `@pixi-reels/kit` |
| `examples/shared/cheats.ts`, `seededRng.ts` | the private `@pixi-reels/cheats` package, still outside the library per ADR 009 |
| `examples/assets/prototype-symbols/` | `apps/site/public/prototype-symbols/` |
| `examples/orientation-matrix/` | `tests/e2e/fixtures/orientation-matrix/` |
| `examples/shared/mockServer.ts`, `ui.ts`, `CheatPanel.ts`, `WinBox.ts`, `roundBus.ts` | moved out with the demo apps |

None of these were ever library API, so none of them is a `pixi-reels`
reference code you copy; the package never exported them.

#### What the codemod will not do

It is an AST transform, so it leaves two things for you:

- Your own local variables. `row`, `col`, `w` and `h` are ordinary words, and
  a codemod that renamed them would rewrite `for (const row of table)`. Code
  like `reelSet.getCellBounds(col, row)` keeps working; those are your values
  passed positionally.
- Your comments. Grep them afterwards.

Most of what it misses on the API surface is a type error, and a v1 key
that reaches the engine throws at the call site naming the replacement.

Two more things to check by hand:

- Review the codemod's diff before you keep it. It rewrites the names it
  knows wherever it can prove the receiver is a reel set or builder. Anything
  it cannot prove, it leaves alone and reports.
- `nudge({ direction })` values. `'down'` and `'up'` became `'forward'` and
  `'reverse'`. Passing the old value throws, but only the literal form inside
  a `nudge(...)` call gets rewritten. A direction hoisted into a config object
  is yours to fix.

### Migrating to 3.0.0
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/migrating-to-3-0/
Every breaking change in 3.0.0, with a before and after. Skip presses take a mode, phases take a skip context, the built-in beats are moves, and the unpublished hurry API is gone.

3.0.0 is a small migration for a game and a real one for a custom phase. There
is no codemod; every change below is a few lines, and the engine names the
replacement in the typings.

#### Why any of this

2.8 had one thing a skip press could do to a reel: slam it. A press placed the
frame and landed it in the same tick, so it always read as a cut, and a tease
was hidden rather than shortened. 3.0 gives the press a mode: `'slam'` is
the cut, `'quicken'` asks each freed reel for its landing sooner without
changing what the landing looks like. To carry that through a phase, the
phase's skip hook grew a context, and while the hooks were open the animated
beats hard-wired into the built-in phases became replaceable and their private
internals became protected.

#### Skip presses

`requestSkip()` and `skipSpin()` take an options object. With no argument they
do what they did.

```ts
// before
reelSet.requestSkip();

// after: the same slam
reelSet.requestSkip();
// or the new mode, per press...
reelSet.requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken', speed: 'turbo' });
// ...or as the set's default
builder.skipMode('quicken');
```

A quicken is a skip: `skipStage` advances, `SpinResult.wasSkipped` is `true`,
the new `SpinResult.skipMode` says which mode ended the round, and
`SpinResult.skipContext` is that press in full (`mode`, `speed`, `payload`).

`slamStop()` before `setResult()` now throws, as `skipSpin()` always did. It
used to warn with `slam-before-result` and land the reels on random fill. A
spin whose result will never come is aborted through its signal:

```ts
// before: lands on whatever the strip shows, warns slam-before-result
reelSet.slamStop();

// after
const abort = new AbortController();
const spin = reelSet.spin({ signal: abort.signal });
// ...the server failed:
abort.abort();
```

`skipStage` is decided before a slam lands anything, so a `spin:complete`
listener on the press that ended the round sees `2`. It saw `0` in 2.8, and
read the stage one tick too early.

#### Skip events

`skip:requested` and `skip:completed` carry `mode`. A listener that only ever
meant a slam keeps working; one that meant "these reels are about to be
placed" checks the mode now.

```ts
// before
reelSet.events.on('skip:requested', ({ reels, partial }) => flashPlaced(reels));

// after
reelSet.events.on('skip:requested', ({ reels, partial, mode }) => {
  if (mode === 'slam') flashPlaced(reels);
});
```

Both events carry the whole press. The `info` is a `SkipInfo`,
`{ reels, partial, mode, speed?, payload? }`: the `SkipContext` every phase's
`onSkip(ctx)` sees, plus the reels. Code that hangs off the event gets what
the game attached to the press, without a side channel:

```ts
reelSet.requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken', speed: 'turbo', payload: { button: 'skip' } });

reelSet.events.on('skip:requested', ({ reels, mode, speed, payload }) => {
  sfx.play(mode === 'quicken' ? 'whoosh' : 'thud', { source: payload?.button });
  if (speed) hud.flash(`landing on ${speed.name}`);
});
```

Keys the press did not set are absent, and an engine slam (an abort, a
timeout, `slamStop()`) is a bare `mode: 'slam'`. `skip:completed` fires in the
same tick for a slam and as the last freed reel lands for a quicken, with the
same `info`. On a Hold & Win board, `feature:skip` is
`{ inFlight, mode, speed?, payload? }` with the press's options as given, and
`board.skip(options?)` takes the same options as `requestSkip()`;
`HoldAndWinBuilder.skipMode()` sets the board's default.

#### Custom phases: `onSkip(ctx)`

Every phase hears a press through `onSkip(ctx)`, where `ctx` is a
`SkipContext`: `{ mode, speed?, payload? }`. `ReelPhase.skip(ctx?)` and
`forceComplete(ctx?)` take the same object.

```ts
// before
protected onSkip(): void {
  this._tween?.kill();
  this.reel.placeStrip(this._frame);
}

// after
protected onSkip(ctx: SkipContext): void {
  if (ctx.mode === 'quicken') {
    // cut a wait, keep the landing; complete yourself when you reach it
    this._delay?.kill();
    this._beginSpinOut();
    return;
  }
  this._tween?.kill();
  this.reel.placeStrip(this._frame);
}
```

Under `'slam'` the hook is the slam pose it always was, and the base completes
the phase after it. Under `'quicken'` only the hook runs: the phase cuts a
wait and completes itself when its natural end is reached, right away if the
slam pose already is that end (`StartPhase` and `AnticipationPhase` do this).
A phase that ignores the mode runs its course, so the reel still lands.

A subclass of a built-in that calls `super.onSkip()` with no argument keeps
its 2.8 meaning, because the built-in hooks default `ctx` to a slam. Pass
`ctx` through to take part in quickens:

```ts
protected onSkip(ctx: SkipContext): void {
  flash(this.reel.reelIndex);
  super.onSkip(ctx);
}
```

`SpinPhase` handles `'quicken'` too (it drops its floor), so a subclass of it
that overrides `onSkip` should call `super.onSkip(ctx)` where it used to do
nothing.

#### Steps

The built-in phases run a named list of steps, and a game edits that list by
re-registering the same class with options. If you subclassed `StartPhase` or
`StopPhase` only to change or insert one thing, this is the shorter road:

```ts
import { StopPhase, StartPhase, step, insertAfter, replaceStep, removeStep } from 'pixi-reels';

builder.phases((f) => {
  f.register('stop', StopPhase, {
    steps: (steps) => insertAfter(steps, 'land', step('flash', (ctx) => flash(ctx.reel.reelIndex))),
  });
  f.register('start', StartPhase, { steps: (steps) => removeStep(steps, 'pull') });
});
```

`StopPhase` runs `delay, spinOut, land, bounce`; `StartPhase` runs `delay,
launch, pull, accelerate, announce`; `AnticipationPhase` runs one `tease`
step. A different bounce shape goes through `ctx.phase.bounce({ animation })`.

#### `quickenable`

A quicken only reaches `onSkip(ctx)` on a phase that declares it:

```ts
class MyStop extends ReelPhase<StopPhaseConfig> {
  readonly quickenable = true;   // "my onSkip branches on ctx.mode"
  ...
}
```

A phase without the flag is left alone by a quicken and runs its course, so
a 2.8 phase whose `onSkip` kills its tweens and places the frame keeps
working: the reel still lands. The built-ins declare it.

#### Built-in phase internals

Every `private` on `StartPhase`, `SpinPhase`, `AnticipationPhase`,
`StopPhase`, `AdjustPhase`, `CascadeFallPhase`, `CascadePlacePhase` and
`CascadeDropInPhase` is `protected`. A subclass that copied a whole method to
reach one field can call it instead. `ReelPhase.speed` is a public getter
beside `reel`; `this._speed` still works. `land()` and `bounce()` are public,
so a step written outside the class can reach them.

The rule from the phases page stands: the protected surface can change in a
minor release, so a subclass may need to follow.

#### Removed: the unpublished hurry API

2.9 was cut on `main` but never published, so nothing below ever reached npm.
If you built against a snapshot:

| 2.9 snapshot | 3.0 |
|---|---|
| `reelSet.requestHurry(options)` | `reelSet.requestSkip({ mode: 'quicken', ...options })` |
| `HurryOptions` | `SkipOptions` (`mode`, `speed`, `payload`) |
| `hurry:requested` | `skip:requested` with `mode === 'quicken'` |
| `board.hurry(options)` / `BoardGrid.hurrySpinning()` | `board.skip({ mode: 'quicken', ...options })` / `BoardGrid.skipSpinning(options)` |
| `feature:hurry` | `feature:skip` with `mode === 'quicken'` |
| `ReelPhase.hurry(speed?)` | `ReelPhase.skip({ mode: 'quicken', speed })` |
| `protected onHurry(): boolean` | `protected onSkip(ctx)` branching on `ctx.mode` |
| notice `hurry-cascade` | notice `quicken-cascade` |
| notice `slam-before-result` | `slamStop()` throws instead |

### Migrating to 4.0.0
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/reference/migrating-to-4-0/
The visual debug tools moved to the pixi-reels/debug subpath and draw with pixi-silk; two imports change and two console helpers are gone. A Hold & Win board's landing wave now steps by the speed profile's stopDelay.

4.0.0 touches debugging and one Hold & Win default. A game that never imported
`debugOverlay`, never called `__PIXI_REELS_DEBUG.showMask()` or `.overlay()`, and
has no Hold & Win board with its own speed profiles has nothing to do.

#### Why

The debug overlay drew with PixiJS `Graphics`, which tessellates. Thin outlines
crawled and rounded corners faceted whenever a reel set was fitted to a canvas
at anything but 1x, which is always. It now draws with
[pixi-silk](https://pixi-silk.schmooky.dev), which renders every shape as an
exact signed distance field. A production build should not pay for that
dependency, so the drawing half of debugging moved behind its own subpath, the
same way Spine support lives behind `pixi-reels/spine`. `pixi-silk` is an
optional peer, and only `pixi-reels/debug` imports it.

#### Install pixi-silk for the overlay

```bash
pnpm add -D pixi-silk
```

It is only needed where you import `pixi-reels/debug`. A dev dependency is
enough, since the overlay should be dev-only.

##### What pixi-silk needs to draw

pixi-silk 0.1 draws through a WebGL shader, and everything in
`pixi-reels/debug` that draws (`debugOverlay`, `DebugPlaque`, `WinLines`) is
built on it. Two things follow:

- A WebGL renderer. On WebGPU the plates, outlines and lines draw nothing
  (Pixi logs `Mesh shader has no gpuProgram`); only plaque text shows. Ask for
  WebGL while you debug: `await app.init({ preference: 'webgl' })`.
- A DOM, or a stand-in for one, to build them. A `SilkGraphics` probes the
  shader's precision through `DOMAdapter.createCanvas()`, so in plain Node
  `new DebugPlaque()`, `new WinLines()` and `debugOverlay()` (its `describe()`
  included) throw `document is not defined`. A headless test hands Pixi a
  canvas without WebGL, and the probe settles on `mediump`:

```ts
import { DOMAdapter, BrowserAdapter } from 'pixi.js';

DOMAdapter.set({
  ...BrowserAdapter,
  createCanvas: (width = 0, height = 0) =>
    ({ width, height, getContext: () => null }) as unknown as HTMLCanvasElement,
});
```

`enableDebug()`, `debugSnapshot()` and `debugGrid()` stay in the main entry and
need neither.

#### `debugOverlay` and `OVERLAY_LABEL` moved

```ts
// before
import { debugOverlay, OVERLAY_LABEL } from 'pixi-reels';
import type { DebugOverlayHandle, DebugOverlayLayer } from 'pixi-reels';

// after
import { debugOverlay, OVERLAY_LABEL } from 'pixi-reels/debug';
import type { DebugOverlayHandle, DebugOverlayLayer } from 'pixi-reels/debug';
```

The options, the layer names and `describe()` are the same. Each layer is now a
`SilkGraphics` rather than a `Graphics`, still labelled
`pixi-reels:debugOverlay:<layer>`; code that read a layer's bounds keeps
working. Three layers are new: `hud` became a plaque, and `metrics` and
`timeline` were added. `layers: 'all'` draws more than it did, and the two new
panels sit under the mask, so fit your camera after enabling them, or list the
layers you want.

#### `showMask()` and `overlay()` left the window hook

`enableDebug()` still attaches `window.__PIXI_REELS_DEBUG` with `snapshot()`,
`grid()`, `log()`, `trace()` and the recorder, and gained `metrics()`. The two
helpers that drew are gone, because the main entry no longer draws:

```ts
// before, in the console
__PIXI_REELS_DEBUG.showMask(true);
__PIXI_REELS_DEBUG.overlay({ layers: ['cells'] });

// after, in your debug build
import { debugOverlay } from 'pixi-reels/debug';
debugOverlay(reelSet, { layers: ['mask'] });   // what showMask drew, above the spotlight
debugOverlay(reelSet, { layers: ['cells'] });
```

`showMask` drew into the masked container, under the spotlight; the `mask`
layer draws the same box and per-reel rects above everything.

#### Hold & Win: the landing wave follows `stopDelay`

A board's cells land in a diagonal wave, and its step is now the active profile's
`stopDelay` instead of a fixed 70 ms. A board built on the builder's defaults is
unchanged (its `'normal'` profile sets `stopDelay: 70`). A board that registers its
own profiles and never calls `.stagger()` now waves by their `stopDelay`: 140 ms a
step on `SpeedPresets.NORMAL`, none on TURBO and SUPER_TURBO. To keep the old wave:

```ts
new HoldAndWinBuilder()
  .speeds({ normal: NORMAL, turbo: TURBO })
  .stagger((reel, cell) => (reel + cell) * 70);
```

Or set `stopDelay` on each profile, which is what the wave reads now.

#### New, if you want it

- `SpinMetrics`: the per-round recorder behind the `metrics` and `timeline`
  layers, usable on its own. See [Debugging](/learn/debugging/).
- `DebugPlaque`: the readout plate every panel and every recipe label uses.
- `__PIXI_REELS_DEBUG.metrics()`: the same rounds as plain JSON for an agent.

URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/api/classes/debug.WinLines/

URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/api/classes/index.AdjustPhase/
Tween-only phase between SPIN and STOP for MultiWays slots.

### AnimatedSpriteSymbol
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/api/classes/index.AnimatedSpriteSymbol/
Symbol implementation using PixiJS AnimatedSprite. Swaps frame arrays on activate. Win animation plays the full sequence.

### AnticipationPhase
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/api/classes/index.AnticipationPhase/
Anticipation phase: the tease before a reel stops.

### BoardGrid
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/api/classes/index.BoardGrid/

### CardSymbol
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/api/classes/index.CardSymbol/
One visible cell on a reel. the thing that actually draws.

### CascadeDropInPhase
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/api/classes/index.CascadeDropInPhase/
Drop-in half of the tumble cascade. Animates each visible symbol from its computed origin (above the viewport for new symbols, its old grid cell for…

### CascadeFallPhase
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/api/classes/index.CascadeFallPhase/
Fall-out half of the tumble cascade. Replaces StartPhase when the builder was configured with .tumble(...).

### CascadeMode
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/api/classes/index.CascadeMode/
Cascade/tumble spinning mode. Symbols fall from above with gravity-like acceleration, used for tumble/avalanche mechanics.

### CascadePlacePhase
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/api/classes/index.CascadePlacePhase/
Identity-swap half of the tumble cascade. Runs after CascadeFallPhase (Moment A) or right at the start of refill() (Moment B).

### CuePlayer
URL: https://pixi-reels.schmooky.dev/api/classes/index.CuePlayer/
